- `makeTranslate(messages: Messages): TranslateFn` — Build a TranslateFn over messages (missing keys return the key).
- `memo<P>(component: Component<P>, areEqual?: (prev: P, next: P) => boolean): Component<P>` — Wrap a component so the reconciler bails out of re-rendering it when its props have not meaningfully changed. Without areEqual, props are compared with shallowEqualProps (the same default the reconciler applies to every component); pass areEqual for custom control (return true to skip the re-render). Context changes always bypass the bailout — a consumer still re-renders when a context it reads changes.
- `type Messages = Record<string, string>` — A flat message catalog for one locale: message key → template string.
- `type ModuleEndpoints<M, P> = mapped` — Every exported HTTP-method handler of a route module, as { GET: InferEndpoint; … }. P is the pattern-derived params record (never for a static route).
- `interface NativeIdTokenSignIn` — What a native id_token sign-in sends.
- `interface NativeMfaChallenge` — A native sign-in that still owes a second factor: finish it with NativeSession.completeMfa. Single-use — every call answers a fresh one on the error it throws — and short-lived (five minutes from the id_token sign-in).
- `interface NativeMfaEnrollment` — A first factor being enrolled to finish a pending sign-in (NativeSession.enrollMfa).
- `nativeSession(options: NativeSessionOptions): NativeSession` — A native session against a remote denext server (denextAuth({ native })). Pass it as createApiClient({ base, auth: session }).
- `interface NativeSession` — A native session: an auth provider for createApiClient, plus sign-in and sign-out.
- `class NativeSessionError` — A failed native-session call.
- `interface NativeSessionOptions` — Options for nativeSession.
- `interface NativeSessionStorage` — Where the refresh token is kept — secureStore from denext/mobile fits as is.
- `interface NativeSessionUser` — The user a native sign-in answers with.
- `navigate(href: string, options?: NavigateOptions): Promise<void>` — Perform a soft navigation to href: fetch the target page, swap its markup into the hydration root, update history and <head>, and re-hydrate. Falls back to a full-page navigation on cross-origin URLs or network failure.
- `interface NavigateOptions` — Options controlling a soft (client-side) navigation.
- `notFound(): never` — Throw to render the nearest not-found UI with a 404 status.
- `interface PasskeyCallOptions` — Options shared by every passkey call.
- `type PasskeyClientError = unsupported | cancelled | invalid | unauthorized | reauth_required | email_unverified | code_required | exists | rate_limited | network` — Why a passkey call failed.
- `interface PasskeySignInOptions` — Options for signInWithPasskey.
- `type PasskeySignInResult = object | object` — What signInWithPasskey resolves to.
- `passkeysSupported(): boolean` — Whether this browser can run a WebAuthn ceremony at all.
- `type PlainBody<H> = conditional` — A plain handler's request body: the B of its TypedRequest<B> first param, else never.
- `type PlainResponse<H> = conditional` — A plain handler's response: the T of its TypedResponse<T> return, else unknown.
- `prefetch(href: string): void` — Prefetch the page at href in the background (same-origin only) and cache its HTML, so a subsequent navigate is instant. No-op on the server, for cross-origin URLs, or when already prefetched/in-flight.
- `Profiler(props: ProfilerProps): VNode` — Measure render timing for children and report it to onRender after each commit. Renders as a Fragment carrying the profiler config for the reconciler, so it adds no DOM of its own and is transparent during SSR.
- `type ProfilerOnRender = (id: string, phase: ProfilerPhase, actualDuration: number, baseDuration: number, startTime: number, commitTime: number) => void` — Callback invoked after each commit of a Profiler's subtree.
- `type ProfilerPhase = mount | update` — The commit phase reported to a Profiler's onRender.
- `interface ProfilerProps` — Props for Profiler.
- `type PropsComparator = (prev: Record<string, unknown>, next: Record<string, unknown>) => boolean` — Compares a component's previous and next props; true means "skip re-render".
- `provideMessages(messages: Messages, child: VNodeChild): VNode` — Wrap child in a MessagesContext provider so descendants resolve useTranslations() against messages during server rendering.
- `PUBLIC_ENV_PREFIXES: typeOperator` — Prefixes that mark an environment variable as safe to expose to the browser. NEXT_PUBLIC_ matches Next.js for drop-in compatibility; DENEXT_PUBLIC_ is the denext-native prefix. Any other variable stays server-only.
- `publicEnv(): Record<string, string>` — Read the public environment variables (isomorphic). On the client, returns the variables embedded in the page — only ever the public-prefixed ones. On the server, returns the public subset of the live process environment.
- `qrl<E>(loader: () => Promise<(event: E) => unknown>, id: string, capture?: typeOperator): Qrl<E>` — Define a lazily-loaded event handler. Give it a **stable, explicit id** so the server-serialized reference and the client loader agree.
- `interface Qrl<E>` — A reference to a lazily-loaded handler: callable, tagged with its stable id.
- `type QueryInput = Record<string, string | number | boolean | null | undefined> | string` — An href's query: a record (nullish values are dropped) or a pre-built query string.
- `class ReadonlyURLSearchParams` — Next's ReadonlyURLSearchParams — the read-only view of the URL query that useSearchParams() returns. It is a real URLSearchParams for reads/iteration, but its mutating methods throw (you cannot change the URL by mutating this object; navigate instead).
- `interface RegisteredApi` — Augmentation target for the generated .denext/api.ts: declare module "denext" { interface RegisteredApi { schema: ApiSchema } } makes createApiClient() typed with no type argument.
- `type RegisteredParams = conditional` — The per-route params map when typed-routes is wired (from .denext/routes.ts), else a loose fallback. Each key is a route pattern (/blog/[slug]) → its params object ({ slug: string }).
- `interface RegisteredRoutes` — Typed-routes registry (augmentation seam). denext build/dev emit .denext/routes.ts, which augments this interface with routes: Routes; import that file anywhere in your app and Link / Router.push narrow to real paths. Empty by default ⇒ Href is string (no enforcement until you opt in).
- `type RegisteredSchema = conditional` — The registered app schema when .denext/api.ts is imported, else the open ApiSchema.
- `registerPasskey(options?: PasskeyCallOptions & object): Promise<RegisterPasskeyResult>` — Register a passkey for the signed-in user: {basePath}/passkey/register/options, the browser's create ceremony, then {basePath}/passkey/register. The server requires a recent sign-in ("reauth_required" otherwise).
- `type RegisterPasskeyResult = object | object` — What registerPasskey resolves to.
- `type RequestArgs<E> = conditional` — The trailing call args: the opts object is required only when it has a required key.
- `type RequestOf<E> = parenthesized & parenthesized & parenthesized & object` — The options object for one endpoint: params/body/query are typed when the route declares them.
- `type RequiredKeys<T> = indexedAccess` — The keys of T that are required (used to decide whether the opts arg is optional).
- `type ResponseOf<E> = conditional` — The awaited response type for one endpoint.
- `interface Root` — A mounted (or hydrated) render root that can be re-rendered or torn down.
- `interface RootOptions` — Options accepted by createRoot/hydrateRoot for React parity. identifierPrefix is wired into the root's useId scope; the three error callbacks observe error handling without changing denext's default behavior (a boundary still catches, an uncaught error still surfaces, a hydration mismatch still keeps the client render).
- `interface Router` — Imperative navigation API returned by useRouter (Next.js AppRouterInstance).
- `interface RouterNavigateOptions` — Options for Router.push / Router.replace (Next.js NavigateOptions).
- `type SearchOutput<S> = conditional` — What a Standard Schema produces from the query string — its validated output type.
- `class SearchParamsValidationError` — Thrown by useSearchParams(schema) when the URL query fails the schema. It is a normal error, so the nearest error.tsx boundary catches it (matching the server's defineApi validation).
- `SessionProvider(props: SessionProviderProps): VNode` — Provide session state to the tree. Seed it with session from the server for no loading flash, or omit it to fetch {basePath}/session on mount.
- `interface SessionProviderProps` — Props for SessionProvider.
- `interface SessionUser` — The signed-in user exposed to the client (non-sensitive fields only).
- `setApiInvalidationSource(source: ApiInvalidationSource | null): void` — Install the transport that delivers tag invalidations to useApi({ tags }) (the Live client does this in configureLive / useApiLive).
- `interface ShellHandoff` — What the user did in one shell field before the app took over: the field's text, its selection (character offsets into text), whether it had focus, and its scroll position.
- `shellReady(): Promise<void>` — Tell denext the app is ready to replace the prerendered spa.shell: the app, rendered off-screen meanwhile, is swapped in before the next paint (in a microtask, so a call from a render or an effect lands after the commit in progress), and the text, selection, focus and scroll of each data-denext-shell-key field carry over. With spa.shell.readyOn: "shellReady" this is the only trigger besides maxHoldMs; with the default ("first-settled-commit") it swaps early.
- `signIn(provider: string, options: SignInOptions & object): Promise<CredentialsSignInResult>` — Start sign-in. For an OAuth/OIDC provider this navigates to the provider (or, with redirect: false, resolves with the URL it would have gone to); for a Credentials provider (pass credentials) it POSTs and resolves with the result — { ok: false } for a refusal (a wrong password, a spent attempt budget), never a rejection; test result.ok.
- `interface SignInOptions` — Options for signIn.
- `signInWithPasskey(options?: PasskeySignInOptions): Promise<PasskeySignInResult>` — Sign in with a passkey — or, while the session owes a second factor, complete it with one: {basePath}/passkey/authenticate/options, the browser's get ceremony (the authenticator offers its passkeys for this site), then {basePath}/passkey/authenticate. On success it navigates to callbackUrl unless redirect: false.
- `signOut(options?: SignOutOptions): Promise<void>` — Sign out (same-origin POST to {basePath}/signout), then navigate to callbackUrl.
- `interface SignOutOptions` — Options for signOut.
- `startTransition(callback: () => void): void` — Run callback as a low-priority "transition": the callback runs synchronously (like React), but any state updates it triggers are scheduled at transition priority — flushed after the reconciler yields to the browser, so urgent updates and paint/input happen first. Without the client scheduler it just runs the callback. The transition render is time-sliced and interruptible: a higher-priority (sync) update abandons the in-flight transition and restarts it (see the Async transitions guide: /docs/rendering#async-transitions).
- `type StateUpdater<S> = (value: S | parenthesized) => void` — State setter returned by useState. Accepts either the next value or an updater function that receives the previous value and returns the next one.
- `Suspense(props: SuspenseProps): VNode` — A Suspense boundary. Renders fallback until its children stop suspending.
- `SuspenseList(props: SuspenseListProps): VNode` — React.SuspenseList — coordinates the reveal order of sibling <Suspense> boundaries. With revealOrder="forwards" a boundary stays in its fallback until every boundary before it has revealed ("backwards" reverses; "together" holds all until the last resolves). tail="collapsed" shows only the next boundary's fallback, "hidden" shows none.
- `interface SuspenseListProps` — Props for SuspenseList.
- `interface SuspenseProps` — Props for the Suspense boundary component.
- `type TranslateFn = (key: string, vars?: TranslationVars) => string` — A translation function: look up key and interpolate any {var} placeholders.
- `type TranslationVars = Record<string, string | number>` — Values interpolated into a message template's {name} placeholders.
- `type TypedAction<Out> = (prevState: ActionResult<Out>, formData: FormData) => Promise<ActionResult<Out>>` — A typed action, shaped for useActionState(action, initial).
- `type TypedQuery<Q> = conditional` — A schema-typed query, required; an uninformative (any/unknown) schema stays free-form.
- `type TypedUrlObject = indexedAccess` — The typed object form of an href: a route pattern as pathname plus the params object it requires (checked against this app's routes when .denext/routes.ts is imported). A route with no dynamic segments takes no params. Unresolved dynamic segments are filled from params, so { pathname: "/blog/[slug]", params: { slug } } navigates to /blog/<slug>.
- `unauthorized(): never` — Throw to render the nearest unauthorized.tsx UI with a 401 status.
- `interface UrlObject` — Next.js UrlObject — the object form Link/useRouter accept as an href.
- `use<T>(usable: Promise<T> | Context<T>): T` — React 19's use: read a resource during render. Given a **promise**, unwrap its value, suspending (throwing the promise) while it is pending — the same promise instance must be passed across renders (cache it). Given a **context** (from createContext), read its current value like useContext — this overload may be called conditionally. Works on the client and under every SSR renderer, since both delegate to the active hook dispatcher.
- `useActionState<State, Payload>(action: (state: State, payload: Payload) => State | Promise<State>, initialState: State, permalink?: string): tuple` — Manage state driven by a form action (React 19 useActionState).
- `useApi<P, M>(path: P, method: M, opts?: RequestOf<ApiEndpointOf<P, M>>, options?: UseApiOptions): UseApiResult<ResponseOf<ApiEndpointOf<P, M>>, ErrorsOf<ApiEndpointOf<P, M>>>` — Call one of the app's own route handlers from a component, typed end to end.
- `interface UseApiOptions` — Options for useApi.
- `interface UseApiResult<T, E>` — What useApi returns.
- `useCallback<T>(fn: T, deps?: DependencyList): T` — Return a memoized version of fn that only changes when deps change.
- `useContext<T>(context: Context<T>): T` — Read the current value of context from the nearest enclosing provider.
- `useDebugValue<T>(value: T, format?: (value: T) => unknown): void` — Label a custom hook's value for the DevTools inspector. In development on the client the value is recorded against the rendering component — without taking a hook cell, so adding or removing a call never shifts hook state (Fast Refresh keeps it) — and shown on the hook row it follows in the panel, denext_hook_state and the MCP snapshot. format is never called during render: the inspector applies it lazily, only when it reads the value. In production and during server rendering this is a no-op.
- `useDeferredValue<T>(value: T, initialValue?: T): T` — Return a deferred copy of value that lags behind during rapid updates, letting urgent renders finish first. On the client this is a true **render-phase** deferral (React-accurate): during an urgent render the hook returns the previous value and schedules a low-priority transition to catch up, so the deferred update is time-sliced and interruptible and the value never trails by an extra commit. The optional initialValue (React 19) is returned on the first render, with a transition scheduled to reach value. On the server (no lane scheduler) it returns initialValue ?? value.
- `useEffect(effect: () => EffectCleanup, deps?: DependencyList): void` — Run a side effect after render, re-running whenever deps change.
- `useEffectEvent<A, R>(handler: (...args: A) => R): (...args: A) => R` — Return a callback that always sees the latest committed props/state — React 19.2's useEffectEvent. Use it for the "event" part of an Effect that should not itself be a dependency (so the Effect doesn't re-run when the handler's closure changes).
- `useErrorBoundary(): ErrorBoundaryController` — Access the nearest enclosing error boundary imperatively. Returns a ErrorBoundaryController whose captureError(e) shows that boundary's fallback (handy for async errors a boundary cannot catch during render) and whose reset() retries its children. Inert during server rendering.
- `useFormStatus(): FormStatus` — Read whether the **nearest enclosing** <form action={fn}>'s action is in flight (React 19 useFormStatus). Scoped per form — two concurrent forms report independent status. Returns { pending: false } outside a form and during server rendering.
- `useId(): string` — Return a unique, stable id string. The value is deterministic across the server render and client hydration (ids are assigned in render order), so it is safe to use for id/htmlFor/aria-* attributes without a mismatch.
- `useImperativeHandle<T>(ref: Ref<T>, create: () => T, deps?: DependencyList): void` — Customize the value exposed on a parent's ref for the current component. create builds the imperative handle; it re-runs when deps change.
- `useInsertionEffect(effect: () => EffectCleanup, deps?: DependencyList): void` — Run effect synchronously at commit in its own pre-mutation phase — before any DOM mutation and before layout effects — intended for CSS-in-JS libraries (emotion, styled-components) and animation libraries (motion) to inject styles before the DOM is read. It must NOT read layout or use refs. A no-op during server rendering.
- `useLayoutEffect(effect: () => EffectCleanup, deps?: DependencyList): void` — Like useEffect, but on the client it runs synchronously after the DOM is mutated and before the browser paints — use it for layout reads/writes that must happen before the user sees the frame. A no-op during server rendering.
- `useLocale(): string` — The active locale (reactive) for apps using i18n routing. Reads the locale the server resolved for this page from the hydration payload and re-reads it on soft navigation. Server components should read params.locale directly.
- `useMemo<T>(factory: () => T, deps?: DependencyList): T` — Memoize factory's result, recomputing only when deps change.
- `useOptimistic<S, A>(state: S, updateFn?: (current: S, action: A) => S): tuple` — Show an optimistic value while an async update is in flight. Returns [optimisticState, addOptimistic]; call addOptimistic(action) to apply an optimistic change over the current state. The optimistic value resets to state when state itself changes AND when the transition/action it was applied in settles (React semantics — a failed action reverts too). addOptimistic keeps one identity.
- `useParams<P>(): conditional` — The current route's dynamic params (reactive). Reads the params the server resolved for this page from the hydration payload; updates on soft navigation.
- `usePathname(): string` — Reactive current pathname; re-renders the component on navigation.
- `useReducer<S, A, I>(reducer: (state: S, action: A) => S, initialArg: I, init?: (arg: I) => S): tuple` — Manage component state with a reducer, returning the state and a dispatch. With a lazy init, the initial state is init(initialArg) (React parity).
- `useRef<T>(initial: T): object` — Create a mutable ref object whose .current persists across renders. React's three signatures: useRef<T>(value) → { current: T }, useRef<T>(null) → { current: T | null } (the DOM-ref idiom), useRef<T>() → { current: T | undefined }.
- `useRouter(): Router` — Access the imperative Router for programmatic navigation. Stable identity.
- `useSearchParams(): ReadonlyURLSearchParams` — Reactive current search params — a ReadonlyURLSearchParams, memoized per query string so useEffect(…, [searchParams]) re-runs only when the query changes.
- `useSelectedLayoutSegment(parallelRoutesKey?: string): string | null` — The first route segment below the calling layout's level (reactive), or null.
- `useSelectedLayoutSegments(_parallelRoutesKey?: string): string[]` — The active route path segments **below the calling layout's level** (reactive), matching Next.js. A layout at /a sees ["b","c"] for /a/b/c; the root layout sees all segments. The depth comes from the nearest LayoutSegmentContext provider (injected around each layout by the server renderer and the client route entry); outside any layout it is 0, so all segments are returned. Updates on soft navigation.
- `useSession(): ClientSession` — Read the current ClientSession. Must be under a SessionProvider.
- `useShellHandoff(key: string): ShellHandoff | null` — consumeShellHandoff as a hook: the shell field's state on the component's first render (then the same value for the component's lifetime), or null.
- `useState<S>(): tuple` — Declare local component state with no initial value (S | undefined).
- `useSyncExternalStore<T>(subscribe: (onChange: () => void) => () => void, getSnapshot: () => T, getServerSnapshot?: () => T): T` — Subscribe to an external (non-React) store and re-render when it changes. subscribe registers a change listener and returns an unsubscribe function; getSnapshot reads the current value; getServerSnapshot (optional) provides the value used during server rendering.
- `useTransition(): tuple` — Return [isPending, startTransition]. isPending stays true from the moment the transition starts until its low-priority updates have been flushed — so a pending indicator can paint (and the browser can handle input) before the transition's work runs. For an async callback it is held until the returned promise settles and the resulting flush lands. Falls back to a synchronous run when no client scheduler is installed.
- `useTranslations(): TranslateFn` — Access a translation function t(key, vars?) for the active locale (reactive). Looks up key in the locale's catalog and interpolates {var} placeholders; a missing key returns the key itself. The catalog comes from the render-time provider during SSR and from the hydration payload on the client, re-read on soft navigation (so switching locales updates the strings).
- `type ValueResult<R> = conditional` — A defineApi handler's returned VALUE type: a returned Response carries no body type, and a returned err(...) is an error envelope, not a body.
- `interface VNode` — A single virtual DOM node.
- `type VNodeChild = VNode | string | number | bigint | boolean | null | undefined` — Anything that can appear as a child in JSX.
- `type VNodeChildren = VNodeChild | VNodeChild[]` — One child or an array of children, as accepted by JSX.
- `type VNodeType = string | Component<any> | FRAGMENT` — The type field of a VNode: an intrinsic tag name, a component fn, or a fragment marker.
- `interface VProps` — Props passed to a virtual node. children is normalized separately.

### `denext/devtools`

- `interface BoundaryTiming` — One Suspense boundary's timeline: server resolve time and (live) client reveal time.
- `clearPropOverrides(fiberId: number): boolean` — Drop all live prop overrides on a component and re-render it.
- `interface CommitSummary` — A recorded commit: its timing and a synthetic flamegraph root.
- `interface DenextDevtoolsApi` — The window.__denextDevtools surface (and the denext/devtools module API).
- `disableRenderReasons(): void` — Release one enableRenderReasons hold. Tracking stops (and the commit hook is uninstalled if nothing else needs it) only once the LAST holder has released.
- `dispatchReducer(fiberId: number, hookIndex: number, action: unknown): boolean` — Dispatch an action to a useReducer cell live, driving the component's own dispatch (so the reducer runs and a re-render schedules exactly as the app would). Distinct from setHookState: a reducer's updater expects an *action*, not the next value. Returns whether the cell was found and is a reducer.
- `enableRenderReasons(): void` — Begin tracking why each component renders — install the commit hook and, when tracking was off, clear any prior data. The panel enables this when its "why did this render" view is on; the first commit after enabling seeds the baseline (so reasons appear from the next render onward). No-op in production.
- `interface FlameNode` — One node in a commit's flamegraph — a component and the time under it.
- `getBoundaryTimings(): BoundaryTiming[]` — The per-Suspense-boundary timeline — a LIVE merge of two sources: the swap runtime's real-time reveal marks (window.__denextBoundaries, populated as each hole lands, in dev) and the end-of-stream #__denext_boundary_timing island (authoritative server resolve times, present once the stream finishes). So the panel shows a boundary the instant it reveals (client reveal + the template's data-dnx-ms server time), then settles to the island's rounded server time. Empty in production / on a non-streamed page / before any boundary reveals.
- `getCommits(): CommitSummary[]` — The recorded commits (oldest first) — one summary per commit. Empty in production.
- `getCommitTree(index: number): FlameNode | null` — The flamegraph for a recorded commit — a synthetic (commit) root whose children are the tree's top-level components, each carrying selfMs/totalMs/didRender/changed. index is a CommitSummary index. null for an unknown index / in production.
- `getFiberIdForDom(el: Node | null): number | null` — The nearest component fiber id owning el — for the element picker and hover- highlight. Walks el up to the nearest host node the last getInspectorTree walk mapped, then up the fiber tree to its owning component (falling back to the host fiber's own id when no component ancestor exists). null when nothing maps — call getInspectorTree first so the DOM map is current.
- `getHostNode(fiberId: number): Element | null` — The DOM element for a fiber id — its own host node when it is a host fiber, else the first host node in its subtree (a component's rendered root). Backs the panel's tree-row → element highlight. null for an unknown id or a fiber with no host DOM.
- `getInspectorTree(): InspectNode[]` — The current component tree — every mounted root's children, each node carrying its props, hooks/state, and contexts. Serialized on demand (never per commit). Empty in production or before the first mount.
- `getOwnerStack(fiberId: number): OwnerStackEntry[]` — A node's owner stack, nearest first: React's JSX-owner chain (the component whose render created each element, with the JSX call site) when the elements came from a dev build's jsxDEV, else the component fibers above it (an element made by h() / createElement records no owner). Each entry carries its declaration source when known. fiberId comes from the most recent getInspectorTree. Empty in production or for an unknown/stale id.
- `getPageRenderMode(): PageRenderMode | null` — The server's render-mode verdict for this page — static vs dynamic vs streamed, and the page-cache outcome — read from the dev-only #__denext_render_modes JSON island the document renderer emits. null in production, outside a dev render, or if absent.
- `getProfile(): ProfileEntry[]` — The collected profile, heaviest total render time first. Empty in production.
- `getRenderModes(): RenderModeEntry[]` — The render-mode view. v1 reports the **client boundaries** — the islands, with their hydration strategy and timing (the server-rendered remainder is static/streamed HTML carrying no client boundary). A future revision adds server-emitted per-boundary static/dynamic/streamed + cache detail. Empty in production.
- `getRenderReason(fiberId: number): RenderReason | null` — The recorded RenderReason for a component — what changed to cause its most recent render, and its render count — or null when tracking is off, the id is unknown, or it hasn't rendered since enableRenderReasons.
- `getValueAt(fiberId: number, ref: ValueRef, path: Array<string | number>): SerializedValue | null` — Read one level of a component's live value at path under ref — a prop, a hook cell's value, or a read context — re-reading it fresh off the fiber and serializing it a single level deep (with child entries). Powers the panel's on-demand, click-to- expand nested-value view: expand a level by calling again with a longer path. Returns null for an unknown fiber or a path that no longer resolves.
- `interface InspectContext` — One context this component read during its last render.
- `interface InspectHook` — One hook cell as shown in the inspector.
- `interface InspectNode` — A component/host node in the inspector tree.
- `interface InspectProp` — One prop entry — for per-prop display and live override.
- `installDevtools(): void` — Install denext's first-party DevTools (inspector API + in-page panel). Idempotent, and a no-op in production / without a DOM / unless __denextDev. Imported ONLY by the dev route/Flight entries, so it never enters a production bundle.
- `installInspector(): DenextDevtoolsApi | null` — Install the inspector API on window.__denextDevtools (idempotent). Returns the API, or null in production / before __denextDev. Called by installDevtools in the dev entries; also usable directly from the denext/devtools module.
- `isProfiling(): boolean` — Whether the profiler is currently recording.
- `logValueAt(fiberId: number, ref: ValueRef, path: Array<string | number>): boolean` — console.log the *live* value at ref+path (so the developer gets the real object in the console, not the panel's serialized preview). Returns whether it resolved.
- `interface OwnerStackEntry` — One component above a node in getOwnerStack.
- `interface PageRenderMode` — The server-emitted page render mode (from the dev #__denext_render_modes island).
- `interface ProfileEntry` — One component's aggregated render profile.
- `interface RenderModeEntry` — A component boundary's render mode, for the panel's glass-box view.
- `interface RenderReason` — Which of a component's inputs changed to cause its most recent render.
- `resetProfile(): void` — Discard the collected profile (aggregate + per-commit) without stopping recording.
- `interface SerializedValue` — A display-safe rendering of a runtime value for the inspector.
- `setHookState(fiberId: number, hookIndex: number, value: unknown): boolean` — Set a useState cell's value live, driving the component's own setter (the normal setState path, so it schedules a re-render exactly as the app would). fiberId and hookIndex come from an InspectNode/InspectHook of the most recent getInspectorTree. Returns whether the cell was found and updatable.
- `setPropOverride(fiberId: number, key: string, value: unknown): boolean` — Override a component's prop live — pin key to value and re-render it (the live companion to setHookState). The override persists across the component's own re-renders until clearPropOverrides. fiberId comes from the most recent getInspectorTree. Returns whether the fiber was found.
- `setRefValue(fiberId: number, hookIndex: number, value: unknown): boolean` — Set a useRef cell's .current live. A ref write does not itself schedule a render (matching React), so the change is visible on the next commit the app makes; the panel updates its own view optimistically. Returns whether the cell was found and is a ref.
- `interface SourceLocation` — Where a component was declared — the build-time position behind the panel's source link.
- `startProfiling(): void` — Start recording per-component render timings (via the reconciler's dev-only profiler seam) — both the name-aggregated getProfile and the per-commit flamegraph (getCommits/getCommitTree). Clears any prior recording. No-op in production or if already on.
- `stopProfiling(): void` — Stop recording render timings (keeps the collected data for getProfile).
- `storeAsGlobal(fiberId: number, ref: ValueRef, path: Array<string | number>): string | null` — Stash the live value at ref+path on globalThis.$d (React DevTools' $r-style temporary), so it can be poked at from the console. Returns the global name, or null.
- `subscribe(fn: () => void): () => void` — Subscribe to commits — fn fires (cheaply) after every commit so a panel can lazily re-pull getInspectorTree. Returns an unsubscribe. No-op (returns a no-op) in production. The reconciler observer is installed only while ≥1 subscriber is active (or render-reason tracking is on).
- `subscribeBoundaries(fn: () => void): () => void` — Subscribe to Suspense-boundary reveals — fn fires each time the swap runtime reveals a streamed hole (a denext:reveal document event), so the panel's timeline can update as holes land rather than only on the next commit. Returns an unsubscribe; no-op in production or without a DOM.
- `type ValueRef = object | object | object` — A reference to one drill-in root on a component: a prop, a hook cell, or a context.

### `denext/testing`

- `act<T>(callback: () => T | Promise<T>): Promise<T>` — act(callback) — the React test helper. Runs callback, flushes all pending state updates and effects synchronously, and returns a thenable so both sync and async usage work.
- `cacheStoreContract(t: ContractContext, make: StoreFactory<CacheStore>): Promise<void>` — The CacheStore contract: data and page round-trips, hard expiry, overwrites, large values, deleteByPath, deleteByTag (every tag of an entry purges it, and a rewrite drops a tag), and expireByTag / sweepPages / takeData (single-use, atomic) when the store implements them.
- `type Component<P> = (props: P & object) => VNode | Promise<VNode>` — A component is a function that receives props and returns a renderable node.
- `interface ConformanceReport` — The full report from probeApp.
- `interface ContractContext` — Where the cases run: Deno.TestContext fits, or any { step } that runs a named case.
- `class CookieJar` — A cookie jar: stores cookies set by responses and replays them on later requests, honoring deletions (Max-Age=0 / a past Expires).
- `createTestApp(projectDir: string): Promise<TestApp>` — Build an in-process request handler for a real project directory — **no build step, no socket**. It renders Server Components, runs Server Actions and middleware.ts, and reads cookies/sessions, exactly as production does, but it ships no client bundle — so it drives the **JavaScript-disabled** path your app must support. The handler keeps one PageCache, so revalidate-based ISR is exercised across successive requests. Pair it with createTestClient.
- `createTestClient(handler: TestHandler, options?: TestClientOptions): TestClient` — Create a cookie-aware, no-JS test client over a request handler.
- `fireEvent: FireEvent` — Dispatch DOM events at rendered elements (bubbling), each wrapped in act.
- `interface FireEvent` — A dispatched-event helper: callable, plus named shortcuts. All are async.
- `formatReport(report: ConformanceReport): string` — Render a ConformanceReport as a human-readable table with a summary line. Suitable for CLI output or a test failure message.
- `type FormBody = Record<string, string | number | boolean>` — A request body helper: a plain object is sent as x-www-form-urlencoded.
- `interface FormQuery` — Locate a specific form when a page renders more than one.
- `type Key = string | number | bigint | null | undefined` — A stable identity for a VNode among its siblings, used to keep lists reconciled.
- `interface MatchOptions` — Options controlling text matching.
- `probeApp(projectDir: string, options?: ProbeOptions): Promise<ConformanceReport>` — Probe every route of the denext app at projectDir: render each in process and assert it produces a valid HTML document with no server crash.
- `interface ProbeCheck` — One conformance check applied to a single rendered route.
- `interface ProbeOptions` — Options for probeApp.
- `interface Queries` — The query methods bound to a rendered container.
- `rateLimitStoreContract(t: ContractContext, make: StoreFactory<RateLimitStore>): Promise<void>` — The RateLimitStore contract: a fixed window that opens on the first failure, counts every concurrent failure, closes on time, and reset / decrement (when implemented).
- `interface RedirectHop` — One hop in a followed redirect chain.
- `render(ui: VNode): Promise<RenderResult>` — Mount ui into a fresh in-memory DOM and return queries + interaction helpers. Effects run (wrapped in act), so await the call before asserting.
- `interface RenderResult` — The handle returned by render.
- `interface RoleOptions` — Options for Queries.getByRole.
- `interface RouteProbe` — The result of probing one concrete route path.
- `sessionStoreContract(t: ContractContext, make: StoreFactory<SessionStore>): Promise<void>` — The SessionStore contract: round-trips, expiry, overwrite, write-only-if-present update (a revoked or expired session is never resurrected), delete and deleteByUser.
- `class StoreContractError` — A contract case that failed; its message names what the store got wrong.
- `type StoreFactory<S> = () => S | Promise<S>` — Makes a fresh, empty store for one case.
- `interface TestApp` — The handler createTestApp returns: still a plain (Request) => Response function (pass it to createTestClient as before), plus close() to run the teardowns of the app's denext.config.ts plugins. await using app = await createTestApp(dir) closes it at the end of the scope.
- `interface TestClient` — A cookie-aware, no-JS test driver over a request handler.
- `interface TestClientOptions` — Options for createTestClient.
- `interface TestElement` — The read-only shape of a rendered element that query helpers return.
- `interface TestForm` — A <form> parsed out of rendered HTML, ready to TestClient.submit.
- `type TestHandler = (request: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>` — A handler under test: anything that maps a Request to a Response.
- `interface TestRequestInit` — Options for a single TestClient request.
- `interface TestResponse` — A response whose body has already been read into TestResponse.text — so assertions are synchronous and the body is never left dangling.
- `type TextMatch = string | RegExp` — A text matcher: an exact/normalized string, or a regular expression.
- `userEvent: UserEvent` — Higher-level user interactions (a pragmatic subset of @testing-library/user-event). Each method dispatches the sequence of DOM events a real interaction produces — more faithful than a single fireEvent — and flushes via act. Call directly (await userEvent.click(el)) or via userEvent.setup() (which returns this object).
- `interface UserEvent` — Higher-level user interactions (a subset of @testing-library/user-event).
- `interface VNode` — A single virtual DOM node.
- `type VNodeChild = VNode | string | number | bigint | boolean | null | undefined` — Anything that can appear as a child in JSX.
- `type VNodeChildren = VNodeChild | VNodeChild[]` — One child or an array of children, as accepted by JSX.
- `type VNodeType = string | Component<any> | FRAGMENT` — The type field of a VNode: an intrinsic tag name, a component fn, or a fragment marker.
- `interface VProps` — Props passed to a virtual node. children is normalized separately.
- `waitFor<T>(callback: () => T | Promise<T>, options?: WaitOptions): Promise<T>` — Retry callback until it returns without throwing, flushing pending denext work (effects/state) between attempts, or reject with the last error after timeout. The Testing-Library waitFor — use it for state that settles after an async effect.
- `interface WaitOptions` — Options for waitFor / the findBy* queries.

### `denext/live`

- `interface ChannelRef<T>` — A channel as the browser sees it: the id (and the phantom type).
- `configureLive(opts: object): void` — Install the Flight parser and route-refresh used by the live transport, and wire <Live> boundary registration. Called once by the generated Flight client entry.
- `defineLiveView<Model, Msg, Props>(config: LiveViewConfig<Model, Msg, Props>): LiveViewComponent<Props>` — Define a server-held live view: a Model–View–Update program whose model lives on the server, one instance per Live connection. Render the returned component from a Server Component; the first paint is plain HTML (no JavaScript needed), and in the browser the view mounts over the Live socket — events bound with send(…) run update on the server and come back as DOM patches.
- `Live(props: LiveProps): VNode` — A real-time server-component boundary. See the module docs.
- `interface LiveActionRef<A, R>` — A reference to a server function usable as a live query (a serverAction).
- `interface LiveErrorInfo` — The structured part of a server error frame, handed to a data subscription's callback.
- `interface LiveProps` — Props for Live.
- `liveReadable<T>(action: T): T` — Mark a server action as readable over the Live data channel (useLive), and return it unchanged for chaining. Only actions marked here — or admitted by the Live hub's canSubscribe policy — may be run via a data-subscribe. Use it for read-only fetchers you intend to stream; never for mutations.
- `interface LiveSubscriptionError` — Why a subscription is not (or no longer) delivering.
- `interface LiveViewComponent<Props>` — The component defineLiveView returns.
- `interface LiveViewConfig<Model, Msg, Props>` — What defineLiveView takes: a program, its id, and its gates.
- `interface LiveViewContext` — The connection a live view runs for (null for the server render of the page).
- `LiveViewIsland: (props: LiveViewIslandProps) => VNode` — The live-view island. Rendered by defineLiveView's component, registered by the generated Flight entry; not something to render by hand.
- `interface LiveViewIslandProps` — The island's props (written by defineLiveView's server render).
- `interface Presence<S>` — The presence of the current room, from usePresence.
- `subscribeChannel(channelId: string, key: string, onValue: (value: unknown, seq: number, cursor?: string) => void, onError: (info: LiveErrorInfo) => void, onReady?: () => void, since?: string): () => void` — Receive a createChannel channel's pushes for key. Backs useChannel. Returns an unsubscribe. A refusal (denied / no-policy / …) arrives through onError and marks the subscription dead so a reconnect does not re-send it.
- `subscribeLiveTags(tags: string[], onInvalidate: () => void, onError?: (info: LiveErrorInfo) => void): () => void` — Be told when any of tags is invalidated on the server (revalidateTag); backs useApi({ tags }). Returns an unsubscribe.
- `interface SubscriptionRefLike<In, Out>` — A defineSubscription ref as the client sees it (the id, plus the phantom types).
- `interface SubscriptionState<Out>` — What useSubscription returns.
- `useApiLive<P, M>(path: P, method: M, opts?: RequestOf<ApiEndpointOf<P, M>>, options?: UseApiOptions): UseApiResult<ResponseOf<ApiEndpointOf<P, M>>, ErrorsOf<ApiEndpointOf<P, M>>>` — useApi whose tags refetch on a server-side revalidateTag — the Live socket delivers the invalidation; the refetch itself is an ordinary HTTP call with the viewer's cookies. Same signature and result as useApi.
- `useChannel<T>(channel: ChannelRef<T> | object, key: string, options?: UseChannelOptions<T>): SubscriptionState<T>` — Receive a createChannel channel's pushes for key. The server authorizes the subscription in this viewer's session (and re-checks it lazily); every publish(key, payload) — from an action, a webhook, a cron — arrives as a new data. At-most-once, latest-wins; no replay on reconnect — unless the channel keeps a history: then since replays what was missed, each payload reaches onMessage, and a reconnect resumes from the last cursor.
- `interface UseChannelOptions<T>` — Options for useChannel.
- `useLive<A, R>(action: LiveActionRef<A, R>, args: A, options: UseLiveOptions<R>): R | undefined` — Subscribe to a server function's result, re-rendering whenever one of options.tags is invalidated. The function runs on the server under the viewer's own session (it must authorize its own access, like any server action). Pass a **read** action.
- `useLiveOptimistic<T, A>(liveValue: T, reducer: (current: T, action: A) => T): tuple` — Pair an optimistic overlay with a live value: apply a local update immediately, and let it reconcile automatically when the authoritative value arrives over the socket (the overlay resets whenever liveValue's identity changes).
- `interface UseLiveOptions<R>` — Options for useLive.
- `usePresence<S>(room: string, options?: UsePresenceOptions<S>): Presence<S>` — Join a presence room and observe its members (who's-online, cursors, typing…). Orthogonal to cache tags — updates push on join/update/leave.
- `interface UsePresenceOptions<S>` — Options for usePresence.
- `useSubscription<In, Out>(sub: SubscriptionRefLike<In, Out>, input: In, options?: UseSubscriptionOptions<Out>): SubscriptionState<Out>` — Subscribe to a defineSubscription over the Live socket. The server validates input, derives the tags, authorizes on every recompute, and pushes each new value.
- `interface UseSubscriptionOptions<Out>` — Options for useSubscription.

### `denext/lazy`

- `bootResumability(registry: Map<string, unknown>, eager?: boolean, islandsIn?: IslandPayload[], signalStateIn?: Record<string, unknown>): void` — Boot the deferred half of resumability: install delegated qrl dispatch (so serialized data-dnx-h handlers run without hydration), then register every island wrapper for deferred per-island hydration. The generated Flight entry dynamically imports and calls this only when a page carries lazy islands or resumable handlers, so non-resumable apps bundle none of it.
- `resumeEvent(target: unknown, eventType: string, event: unknown): ResumeResult` — Handle a delegated event: a qrl dispatches without mounting; otherwise, if the target sits in a pending client:interaction island, resume that island synchronously and replay the event so the just-attached real handler fires.
- `type ResumeResult = qrl | resumed | none` — The outcome of resumeEvent.

### `denext/desktop`

- `buildDesktopBundle(entryUrl: string, os: linux | windows, o: DesktopBundleOptions): Promise<string>` — Build a Linux / Windows bundle directory with deno desktop on denext's pinned runtime: the least-privilege flags from desktop.capabilities (with --no-prompt: a packaged GUI has no TTY to answer a prompt), desktop.denoFlags, the export and the extension modules embedded, the first existing icon, then the webview backend's laufey-launch.json beside the executable.
- `buildDesktopDeb(o: BuildLinuxPackageOptions): Promise<string>` — Build a .deb for a finished Linux bundle, with no packaging tool (ar + ustar + gzip written here), so it cross-builds from any OS. Installs into /usr/lib/<package> with a /usr/bin/<package> link, the .desktop entry (deep-link schemes as x-scheme-handler/*) and the icon; the postinst / postrm refresh the desktop and icon databases (debMaintainerScript).
- `buildDesktopMsi(o: BuildMsiOptions): Promise<string>` — Author and build the .msi for a finished Windows bundle with WiX 5 (wix build); the .wxs is kept beside the .msi for inspection. Windows-only (WiX builds on Windows).
- `buildDesktopRpm(o: BuildLinuxPackageOptions): Promise<string>` — Build an .rpm for a finished Linux bundle with rpmbuild (Fedora/RHEL, apt install rpm on Debian/Ubuntu, brew install rpm on macOS). Same installed layout as the .deb.
- `buildDesktopTarball(o: BuildDesktopTarballOptions): Promise<string>` — The .tar.gz of a finished Linux bundle, written here (ustar + gzip) rather than by the host's tar, so a bundle packaged on Windows keeps its executables' mode bits (see bundleFileMode) and the archive is the same from every host.
- `interface BuildDesktopTarballOptions` — What buildDesktopTarball archives.
- `interface BuildLinuxPackageOptions` — What buildDesktopDeb / buildDesktopRpm build.
- `interface BuildMsiOptions` — What buildDesktopMsi builds.
- `bundleDesktopVcRuntime(dir: string, arch: DesktopWindowsArch, deps?: DesktopVcRuntimeDeps): Promise<boolean>` — Ship the VC++ 2015-2022 runtime DLLs arch's deno desktop binaries import (DESKTOP_VC_RUNTIME_DLLS) next to the bundle's .exe, so the packaged app runs with NO redistributable installed on the target (otherwise it dies at launch with a silent 0xC0000135 DLL-not-found). Microsoft permits this app-local deployment. They come from System32 (the installed redist) when packaging on Windows for the host's architecture, and each one must be a PE image of arch — a Windows on Arm System32 holds x64 VC++ DLLs beside the Arm64 ones. All or nothing: when any is missing or another machine's (or packaging off Windows, or for the other architecture), none is copied and a warning names the redistributable the target needs.
- `cefHelperEntitlements(path: string): Readonly<Record<string, boolean>> | undefined` — Chromium's default entitlements for the CEF helper app path lies in (… Helper (Renderer).app and its executable), or undefined for any other code.
- `createDesktopHandler(options: RunDesktopOptions, outDir: string, proxy: ProxyModule | undefined, token?: string, onBooted?: () => void | Promise<void>, devProxy?: DesktopProxyFn, devInjectToken?: boolean, bridge?: DesktopBridge, onQuit?: () => void, trust?: DesktopTrust, preload?: string, preloadKey?: string, wsUrl?: string): (request: Request, url: URL, info?: DesktopServeInfo) => Promise<Response>` — The desktop request handler: the onRequest escape hatch, the token-gated local endpoints, then — when devProxy is set (denext desktop dev only) — the reverse proxy to denext dev for EVERYTHING else; otherwise the backend proxy, the export's static assets (no-store), the index.html shell for navigations, else 404. Exported for tests; runDesktop wires it to Deno.serve.
- `DEFAULT_DESKTOP_INSTALLERS: Readonly<Record<DesktopOs, typeOperator>>` — The formats built when neither --format nor desktop.installers.<os> names any.
- `defineDesktopExtension<C>(capability: C): C` — Define a native desktop extension: a capability that runs in the desktop app's Deno process and that the page calls through denext/desktop/client's desktopExtension. Enable it in desktop.capabilities.extensions (a module path). This is an identity helper — it returns its argument unchanged so a typeof import("./ext.ts") keeps the exact method types the client's typed proxy reads — and it is not a place for side effects (nothing should run at import).
- `defineSidecar<D>(definition: D): D` — Declare a sidecar with its type checked (an identity function, for runDesktop({ sidecars })).
- `DESKTOP_APP_CONFIG_FILE: .deno-desktop/app.json` — Where the runtime looks for the embedded origin + identifier, relative to the project root.
- `DESKTOP_APP_ORIGIN_ENV: DENO_DESKTOP_APP_ORIGIN` — The env var the denext-pinned runtime publishes the page origin in (myapp://app).
- `DESKTOP_BASELINE_FLAGS: typeOperator` — The permissions every packaged desktop binary needs regardless of capabilities, and which the per-capability flags widen rather than replace: - --allow-net=127.0.0.1,localhost: runDesktop binds loopback and any spa.proxy targets a loopback backend, so the distributed binary can't reach the wider network. - --allow-read (broad): serve the embedded out/ AND the per-user OS app-support directory — a path only known on the end-user's machine, so it can't be baked; the runtime's fs/sqlite caps confine what the page can actually reach. - --allow-env (broad): PORT plus the app's own environment.
- `DESKTOP_DEV_LAN_ENV: DENEXT_DESKTOP_DEV_LAN` — The SECOND dev-only opt-in denext desktop dev --lan sets alongside DESKTOP_DEV_URL_ENV to allow a NON-loopback dev-server target. Without it a non-loopback DENEXT_DESKTOP_DEV_URL is refused at runtime (see desktopDevProxyDecision), so an inherited/hostile env cannot turn a window into a proxy to an arbitrary remote origin.
- `DESKTOP_DEV_URL_ENV: DENEXT_DESKTOP_DEV_URL` — The env var denext desktop dev sets on the window process to put the runtime into live-reload PROXY mode: its value is the loopback denext dev URL to reverse-proxy to. It is the ONLY switch that turns proxy-all on — a release / run / package invocation never sets it, so those windows serve the static export exactly as before (see runDesktop).
- `DESKTOP_INSTALLER_FORMATS: object` — Every installer format, by the OS it is built for.
- `DESKTOP_VC_RUNTIME_DLLS: Readonly<Record<DesktopWindowsArch, typeOperator>>` — The VC++ 2015-2022 runtime DLLs each architecture's deno desktop binaries import (read from the pinned runtime's import tables). The x64 launcher also imports vcruntime140_1.dll, the FH4 exception-handling runtime; the Arm64 launcher does not. On Windows on Arm, System32's vcruntime140_1.dll (which the Arm64 redist installs there itself) is an x64 image, for x64 code under emulation, beside the Arm64 vcruntime140.dll and msvcp140.dll.
- `DESKTOP_WS_URL_ENV: DENO_DESKTOP_WS_URL` — The env var the denext-pinned runtime publishes its WebSocket-only loopback relay in, per-launch token included (ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/.deno-desktop-relay/<64 hex>): the URL the page dials, with its own path appended, for a WebSocket to its own server. The runtime keeps it to its own process (child processes don't inherit it).
- `interface DesktopAppDirs` — The three per-app storage roots a desktop app uses (absolute paths, not created here).
- `desktopAppName(entryUrl?: string): Promise<string>` — The app's name for artifact paths: DENEXT_APP_NAME, else desktop.app.name in the project's denext.config.ts, else deno.json desktop.app.name, else "app".
- `interface DesktopAppSyncReport` — What syncDesktopAppConfig did.
- `desktopAppVersion(root: string): Promise<string | undefined>` — The project's app version: deno.json version, else package.json version (undefined: neither). The installers, the executable's version resource and denext desktop publish-update all go by it.
- `interface DesktopBridge` — The runtime bridge: a request handler for its two paths, and an event emitter.
- `interface DesktopBuildFlagOptions` — Options for desktopBuildFlags.
- `desktopBuildFlags(config: unknown, os: DesktopOs, options?: DesktopBuildFlagOptions): string[]` — The full --allow-* flag list to bake into the deno desktop binary for os — the least-privilege replacement for -A in the package scripts — derived from the WHOLE project config, not just desktop.capabilities (deriving from capabilities alone would starve the non-capability runtime features: an audit found the updater, openAuthSession and a non-loopback proxy all broke). On top of DESKTOP_BASELINE_FLAGS it adds: - the enabled capabilities' run / ffi / sys exactly (the real least-privilege wins), and a single broad --allow-write when any capability writes (a per-user path can't be baked; the runtime cap layer confines it); an unscoped --allow-sys when a capability needs it (clipboard, global shortcuts, launch at login, notifications) or desktop.app.deepLinks declares a scheme (claiming it back needs it): the pinned runtime refuses those with NotCapable under a partial --allow-sys=<names>; - a non-loopback spa.proxy target's host, MERGED into the single --allow-net (Deno keeps only the last --allow-net, so every host is one flag), and so are full-app self-update's hosts (desktop.update.manifestUrl's, desktop.update.ui.feedUrl's and desktop.update.hosts), and desktop.update.ui adds the broad --allow-write its overlay needs. With netSplit (the pinned runtime, 3.0.0-rc.2 or later) the network grant is baked by direction instead: --allow-net-connect takes those outbound hosts, loopback and extraPermissions.netConnect, --allow-net-listen only loopback and extraPermissions.netListen (any port: the app's server picks one at launch), and extraPermissions.net / a sidecar's net go to both; - desktop.extraPermissions — the escape hatch for what the catalog can't see: the updater's feed host (net) and data dir (write), an extension's own run/ffi, etc. It is UNIONED in, and --regenerate-scripts preserves it because it lives in the config, not the script. A capability's read/env is dropped (already broad in the baseline); a capability's net (only downloadToFile's *) is dropped too — per-host download access is an extraPermissions grant, never * baked in.
- `interface DesktopBundleOptions` — What buildDesktopBundle builds.
- `interface DesktopCapability` — A desktop capability: a name (its address on the bridge — an extension's name is its cap name), a set of methods, and the event names it may DesktopCapCtx.emit. Built-ins live in ./caps; user extensions are authored with defineDesktopExtension.
- `interface DesktopCapabilityMethod<I, O>` — One capability method: an optional input schema (validated before the handler), an optional output schema (strips the result before it reaches the page, in production too), the Deno permissions it needs, an optional per-method timeout, and the handler that runs in the Deno process.
- `interface DesktopCapCtx` — The context a capability handler runs with: a scoped DesktopCapCtx.emit for its declared events, the OS app-support directory (which survives relaunch, unlike browser storage — see the desktop storage note), the running OS, the app window (Deno's BrowserWindow when the runtime exposes it), and an AbortSignal that fires when the handler's timeout elapses.
- `class DesktopCapError` — Throw this from a capability handler to answer the page with a specific error code and a SAFE message. The bridge puts code, the message and any data into the { ok: false, error } envelope at status (default 400). Never encode an absolute path, environment value or stack into the message — it crosses to the page. The code "unavailable" is RESERVED (it means the capability/method is not enabled, which makes the page fall back to its web path); use another code for a real failure.
- `desktopCheckCefSignature(exe: string, deps?: WindowsTrustDeps): Promise<boolean>` — After signing a CEF app on Windows: warn when the signed <App>.exe will not start here (cefSignatureProblem). Off Windows, or when the probe fails, nothing is said.
- `desktopDenoFlagArgs(entryUrl: string): Promise<string[]>` — The project's desktop.denoFlags, checked, for a scaffolded packaging script: reads denext.config.ts next to entryUrl's folder (a script in scripts/ → ../), like desktopPackageFlags. A project without a config gets []; a refused flag throws.
- `desktopDevProxyDecision(devUrl: string | undefined, lan: boolean, execPath: string, devBuild?: boolean): DesktopDevProxyDecision` — Decide whether runDesktop enters live-reload PROXY mode, enforcing the loopback rule at RUNTIME rather than trusting the env (invariant: a release build never proxies to a remote origin). Pure + testable. Proxy mode requires ALL of: - a devUrl (the DESKTOP_DEV_URL_ENV value); - execPath being the deno CLI (isDenoCliExecPath), or devBuild (the mark only a denext desktop dev build compiles in) — a packaged app IGNORES the env, so an inherited/hostile env cannot turn a shipped window into a proxy; - a parseable URL whose host is loopback — OR non-loopback WITH lan (the DESKTOP_DEV_LAN_ENV opt-in that only desktop dev --lan sets). allowNonLoopback is true only in that LAN case, and injectToken there requires the dev server's per-run session token on the URL (desktop dev --lan puts it there), so the window's page gets its bridge only from a dev server that gates its other peers. A blocked case returns { proxy: false, refused } so the caller can log why and serve static.
- `type DesktopDevProxyDecision = object | object` — The live-reload proxy decision from the env + the running binary — see desktopDevProxyDecision.
- `class DesktopEventLog` — A bounded, replayable log of desktop bridge events. One instance per running app (created by the bridge); exported as a type so DesktopBridge["events"] is documentable.
- `desktopExportEnv(os: DesktopOs): Record<string, string>` — The environment of a package run's deno task export: the TARGET OS's platform (windows when cross-packaging from a Mac), so the export resolves its .windows / .desktop files, not the host's.
- `desktopHasTool(cmd: string): Promise<boolean>` — Whether a command is on PATH. No shell is involved: on Windows where.exe is run with the name as one argument; elsewhere each PATH directory is checked for an executable file of that name. A name that is not a plain command (a path separator, whitespace, a shell or wildcard character) is never found.
- `desktopIconArgs(entryUrl: string, os: DesktopOs, candidates?: typeOperator): Promise<string[]>` — The --icon <file> args for deno desktop on os: desktop.app.icons.<macos|linux|windows> in denext.config.ts, else the same key in deno.json, else the first of candidates that exists, else one derived from the app's own icon (deriveDesktopIcon: the web manifest, the apple-touch-icon, … into .deno-desktop/; none: no icon, and deno desktop uses its default). Paths are relative to the project.
- `desktopIncludeArgs(entryUrl: string, os?: DesktopOs): Promise<string[]>` — The extra args a scaffolded packaging script must add so the packaged binary embeds every module the app loads at runtime, and loads each one from the binary, never from the build machine's disk:
- `type DesktopInstallerFormat = indexedAccess` — One installer format (desktop.installers.<os> entries, --format values).
- `desktopInstallerPlan(entryUrl: string, os: DesktopOs, requested?: typeOperator, add?: typeOperator): Promise<DesktopInstallerPlan>` — planDesktopInstallers for the project whose scripts/ holds entryUrl (its denext.config.ts supplies desktop.installers).
- `interface DesktopInstallerPlan` — What a package script builds.
- `desktopMacosSigning(entryUrl: string, options?: DesktopMacosSigningOptions): Promise<DesktopMacosSigning>` — Resolve desktop.macos for a packaging run: check the provisioning profile against the app and write the entitlements to sign with. With neither a profile nor config entitlements, the DENEXT_ENTITLEMENTS plist (if any) is passed through unchanged.
- `interface DesktopMacosSigning` — What desktop.macos resolves to for one packaging run.
- `interface DesktopMacosSigningOptions` — Options for desktopMacosSigning.
- `type DesktopMainThreadFn = Deno.UnsafeFnPointer<any> | Deno.UnsafeCallback<any> | Deno.PointerObject` — A C function void* fn(void* context) that DesktopCapCtx.runOnMainThread calls on the UI thread: a Deno.UnsafeFnPointer, a Deno.UnsafeCallback, or a function pointer.
- `interface DesktopMsiProbe` — Seams for desktopMsiProblem.
- `desktopMsiProblem(version: string | undefined, probe?: DesktopMsiProbe): Promise<string | undefined>` — Why the .msi cannot be built here, or undefined when it can: WiX runs on Windows only, the app version must fit an MSI ProductVersion, and wix must be WiX 5 (not just present).
- `desktopNpmArgs(entryUrl: string): Promise<string[]>` — desktopNpmArgsFor for a packaging script: the project is the script's parent directory (scripts/package-*.ts → ../), as desktopIncludeArgs reads it.
- `desktopOptionalInstaller<T>(format: string, explicit: boolean, build: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T | null>` — Build an installer whose failure must not sink the run when it is only a default: an asked-for one (explicit) rethrows, a default one warns and resolves null (the caller falls back).
- `type DesktopOs = darwin | windows | linux` — The operating systems a Deno Desktop app ships for (Deno.build.os spelling).
- `desktopPackageArches(arch: string): Array<x86_64 | arm64>` — The bundle arches a Linux / Windows run builds: both for both, the machine's own for host.
- `interface DesktopPackageArgs` — A package script's parsed command line.
- `interface DesktopPackageArgSpec` — What parseDesktopPackageArgs accepts.
- `desktopPackageFlags(entryUrl: string, os: DesktopOs, netSplit?: boolean): Promise<string[]>` — The deno desktop --allow-* flags for a scaffolded packaging script: read the project's denext.config.ts (next to entryUrl — a packaging script lives in scripts/, so the config is ../denext.config.ts) and derive the least-privilege flags for os via desktopBuildFlags. A project without a config (or one that exports none) gets the baseline. The config is imported dynamically at run time from a caller-supplied URL, so it is never part of this module's own dependency graph (nor a build-time import of user code). The network grant is split by direction when the build runs on denext's pinned runtime and toolchain, 3.0.0-rc.2 or later, read from the deno on PATH the script builds with (desktopNetSplitFor); DENEXT_DESKTOP_RUNTIME=stock, a local runtime build or a stock deno keep --allow-net.
- `desktopPackageMeta(entryUrl: string, fallbackName: string): Promise<DesktopPackageMeta>` — packageMetaFrom for the project whose scripts/ holds entryUrl.
- `interface DesktopPackageMeta` — What every installer says about the app.
- `interface DesktopPageGlobals` — What the injected globalThis.__denext carries besides the desktop marker and the token (see injectDesktopGlobal).
- `desktopPeFiles(dir: string): Promise<string[]>` — Every PE file under a Windows bundle directory, recursively, sorted (symlinks are not followed). The runtime refuses an update of a signed app unless EVERY PE file in it carries the running app's signature — the .exe, <App>.dll, WebView2Loader.dll, the app-local VC++ runtime, CEF's DLLs and helpers and any .node addon — so all of them are signed, third-party files included.
- `desktopPeMachine(head: Uint8Array): string | null` — The machine a PE image is built for, read from its header (MZ, e_lfanew → PE\0\0, then the file header's Machine): "x86_64", "arm64", "x86", or 0x<hex> for another one. An Arm64X DLL reports "arm64".
- `interface DesktopPermissions` — The Deno permissions a capability method needs, as --allow-* scopes. The union of every enabled capability's descriptor is what the package scripts bake into the desktop binary instead of -A (least-privilege packaging), and what denext doctor reports. An ffi or run entry means full-trust native code: least-privilege is moot for that surface once it is on.
- `type DesktopProxyFn = (request: Request, url: URL) => Response | Promise<Response>` — Forward a request the desktop window received to the denext dev server. Injected into createDesktopHandler so tests exercise the dev path with a spy and never spawn a real dev server; runDesktop wires it to proxyToBackend.
- `desktopRequireTool(tool: string, format: string, explicit: boolean): Promise<boolean>` — desktopToolGate for a tool that must be on PATH (the reason carries the install hint).
- `desktopRun(cmd: string[], env?: Record<string, string>, options?: DesktopRunOptions): Promise<void>` — Run a command with inherited stdio; throws on a non-zero exit. The error names the command line with every DesktopRunOptions.secrets value redacted.
- `interface DesktopRunOptions` — Options for desktopRun.
- `interface DesktopRuntime` — What runDesktop hands back once the server is up: the app window, the desktop world the gates enforce, and a hook that pushes an event down the page's bridge stream (what onDesktopEvent(cap, event, …) in denext/desktop/client receives) — the seam OS events (deep links, open-file, …) are emitted through.
- `interface DesktopRuntimeConfig` — What resolveDesktopCapabilities reads: the project config, or the JSON slice of it the desktop sync writes to .deno-desktop/config.json ({ desktop, spa: { proxy } }), which the generated desktop.ts imports so denext.config.ts (and every plugin it imports) stays out of the packaged app. Typed loosely so a JSON module's inferred type is accepted as it is.
- `desktopRuntimeDenoFlags(runtimeEnv: Readonly<Record<string, string>>, denoFlags?: typeOperator): string[]` — The deno desktop flags a build on denext's pinned Deno Desktop runtime (or a local runtime build) gets, given the env resolveDesktopRuntimeEnv resolved for it: --unstable-no-legacy-abort, which the runtime keeps from the compiled app's metadata (from 2.9.7-denext.21), so the app's server aborts request.signal only when a response is not delivered and prints no Deno.serve legacy-behavior notice on its first request, as under denext start and a build --compile binary. The stock runtime (an empty env) gets none: it ignores the setting. A flag already in denoFlags (desktop.denoFlags) is not repeated.
- `desktopRuntimeEnv(entryUrl: string, target?: string): Promise<Record<string, string>>` — The env a scaffolded scripts/package-*.ts adds to its deno desktop command so it builds on denext's pinned Deno Desktop runtime: DENORT_DESKTOP_BIN + LAUFEY_DEV_DIR for target (default: the host), downloaded and verified on first use. Empty under DENEXT_DESKTOP_RUNTIME=stock. The project is the script's parent directory.
- `interface DesktopServeInfo` — The part of Deno.ServeHandlerInfo the gates read. Typed loosely because transport: "memory" is not in the stock Deno.NetAddr type.
- `desktopSignWindows(files: typeOperator, deps?: DesktopSignWindowsDeps): Promise<boolean>` — Authenticode-sign files with the certificate in DENEXT_WINDOWS_CERT (password DENEXT_WINDOWS_CERT_PASSWORD, timestamped by DENEXT_SIGN_TIMESTAMP_URL), batched a few dozen files per signtool sign call. Without a certificate, or without signtool (off Windows), nothing is signed and a warning says so. The password, which signtool takes only as /p, is redacted from a failure message.
- `interface DesktopSignWindowsDeps` — What desktopSignWindows runs commands and reads settings through (tests stub them).
- `desktopSlug(name: string): string` — A filesystem-safe base name (spaces/punctuation → hyphens) for artifact paths.
- `desktopToolGate(why: string | undefined, format: string, explicit: boolean): boolean` — Whether why (a reason the tool for format cannot run, or undefined when it can) still lets the format build: a default format is skipped with a warning, an asked-for one fails.
- `type DesktopTrust = object | object | object` — The desktop world the app runs in (see the module docs).
- `desktopVcRedistUrl(arch: DesktopWindowsArch): string` — The VC++ 2015-2022 redistributable installer for arch.
- `interface DesktopVcRuntimeDeps` — What bundleDesktopVcRuntime reads the machine and files through (tests stub them).
- `desktopVersionProblem(format: msi | deb | rpm, version: string | undefined): string | undefined` — Why version (deno.json version) cannot be the package version of format — MSI packs major.minor.build into 8/8/16 bits, Debian and RPM need a leading digit and a small character set — or undefined when it can (see msiProductVersion / linuxPackageVersion).
- `type DesktopWindowsArch = x86_64 | arm64` — A Windows bundle's architecture, as the package script names it.
- `interface DesktopWindowSettings` — The resolved initial-window settings runDesktop applies (every key optional).
- `interface DesktopWindowSize` — A window size in CSS pixels.
- `desktopWindowsTargetNote(backend: string, noVcRuntime: typeOperator): string` — The closing note of a Windows package run: what the target machine needs for backend. A webview build renders through the Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime the target must have; a CEF build ships Chromium in the bundle and needs none. Either needs the VC++ 2015-2022 redistributable for each arch in noVcRuntime (the runtime could not be bundled app-local).
- `desktopWithAppVersion<T>(entryUrl: string, build: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` — Run build (a deno desktop packaging run) with deno.json carrying the app version: when deno.json has no version, package.json's is written into it for the run and taken out after (see stampDenoJsonVersion), so the bundle deno desktop compiles carries the version the installers and denext desktop publish-update go by (deno.json's, else package.json's).
- `injectDesktopGlobal(html: string, token: string | null, beacon?: boolean, preload?: string, preloadKey?: string, page?: DesktopPageGlobals): Promise<string>` — Inject globalThis.__denext = { desktop: true, token } as an inline <script> immediately after the opening <head> (falling back to after <body>, then to a prepend). The value is JSON.stringify-escaped. When beacon is set, the boot-confirm beacon (BOOT_BEACON_JS) is appended to the SAME script so one CSP hash covers both. When the shell carries a hash-based CSP meta, its script-src is extended with this script's 'sha256-…' so the script survives a strict policy.
- `installWindowCloseHandler(BrowserWindow?: unknown, exit?: (code: number) => void, intercept?: (event: Event) => boolean): unknown` — Closing the window (macOS red light / Cmd-W) quits the app. Deno.serve is a permanently-live task, so deno desktop won't auto-exit on close; adopt the initial window and exit on its close. Guarded so a non-desktop run is a no-op. Returns the adopted window (handed to capabilities as ctx.window), or undefined outside the desktop runtime.
- `isDenoCliExecPath(execPath: string): boolean` — Whether execPath is the deno CLI (deno / deno.exe, case-insensitive) rather than a compiled/packaged app binary. A packaged app's execPath is its own binary; the window denext desktop dev builds is one too, and carries the dev-build mark instead (see desktopDevProxyDecision). Pure, so the packaged-vs-dev decision is testable without the real Deno.execPath.
- `LAUFEY_LAUNCH_FILE: laufey-launch.json` — The webview backend's launch-settings file name.
- `macosCodesignArgs(path: string, options?: MacosCodesignOptions): string[]` — The codesign argv that signs path: --force, a secure timestamp with a real identity (--timestamp=none ad-hoc), the Hardened Runtime, the entitlements, then -s <identity>.
- `interface MacosCodesignOptions` — Options for macosCodesignArgs.
- `macosSigningEntitlements(defaults: Readonly<Record<string, boolean>>, options?: MacosSigningEntitlementsOptions): Promise<string>` — Write the entitlements to sign one piece of code with under the Hardened Runtime: the explicit plist (or, without one, what current is signed with now), plus each of defaults it does not set. A key the base sets, to false too, is kept as set: allow-jit = false in DENEXT_ENTITLEMENTS turns the JIT default off.
- `interface MacosSigningEntitlementsOptions` — Options for macosSigningEntitlements.
- `type NotaryCredentials = object | object` — How xcrun notarytool authenticates: a keychain profile, or an App Store Connect API key.
- `notarytoolSubmitArgs(file: string, credentials: NotaryCredentials, json?: boolean): string[]` — The xcrun notarytool submit … --wait argv for file (a .zip, .dmg or .pkg).
- `parseDesktopPackageArgs(argv: typeOperator, spec: DesktopPackageArgSpec): DesktopPackageArgs` — Parse a package script's arguments: --arch <mode>, --no-export, --no-sign, --format <list> (repeatable), the script's legacy installer flags, and -h / --help. An unknown argument or an --arch outside spec.arches throws.
- `class PickedPaths` — The runtime's picked-path set. One instance per launch is threaded (by the caps resolver) into the dialogs cap (which adds a pick) and the fs / shell caps (which resolve a handle back to a confined path).
- `interface PickedTarget` — A resolved access: the confined absolute path plus the root dir to ensure before a write.
- `type PickMode = read | readwrite | folder | readFolder` — How much access a picked handle grants.
- `planDesktopInstallers(os: DesktopOs, config: unknown, requested?: typeOperator, add?: typeOperator): DesktopInstallerPlan` — Which installers to build for os: requested (--format) when it names any, else desktop.installers.<os> from the config, else DEFAULT_DESKTOP_INSTALLERS. add (a script's legacy --dmg / --appimage) is appended to whichever list applies.
- `type PowerShellRunner = (script: string, env: Record<string, string>) => Promise<object | null>` — Runs a PowerShell script with extra environment; null when PowerShell did not run.
- `interface PreparedDesktopPackage` — What prepareDesktopPackage resolved.
- `prepareDesktopPackage(entryUrl: string, os: DesktopOs, args: Pick<DesktopPackageArgs, formats | add | export>): Promise<PreparedDesktopPackage>` — A package run's setup: the app name, the installer plan (--format, else desktop.installers.<os>, else the defaults), dist/, unless --no-export the static export (deno task export), then the .deno-desktop/app.json + compile.include + deno.json desktop.app sync and the package metadata (read after that sync wrote the deep links into deno.json; a made-up version or identifier is warned about).
- `type ProxyModule = ./dev-proxy.ts` — The lazily-imported reverse-proxy module (./dev-proxy.ts) createDesktopHandler forwards to when a backend proxy is configured; exported so the handler's signature is public.
- `interface ResolvedDesktop` — What resolveDesktopCapabilities returns — spread straight into runDesktop.
- `resolveDesktopCapabilities(runtimeConfig: DesktopRuntimeConfig | undefined, options?: ResolveDesktopOptions): Promise<ResolvedDesktop>` — Resolve config.desktop.capabilities into the capability objects the bridge serves, plus the app-support directory the runtime hands to handlers.
- `interface ResolveDesktopOptions` — Options for resolveDesktopCapabilities.
- `resolveOutDir(options: RunDesktopOptions): string` — The static-export dir to serve: outDir (relative to importMetaUrl when given), else out/.
- `runDesktop(options?: RunDesktopOptions): Promise<DesktopRuntime>` — Serve a denext SPA export in a deno desktop window. Adopts the initial Deno.BrowserWindow and quits the process on window close; under a plain deno run (no desktop runtime) it just starts the server. Resolves once the server is started, with the window and an event hook (DesktopRuntime).
- `interface RunDesktopOptions` — Options for runDesktop (and createDesktopHandler): where to serve the static export from, an optional loopback reverse proxy and request escape hatch, the signed self-updater, the enabled capability bridge, the app-support directory, and whether the loopback OAuth endpoint is enabled. The generated desktop.ts entry spreads resolveDesktopCapabilities into it.
- `shouldInjectDesktopToken(request: Request, url: URL, trust: DesktopTrust, info?: DesktopServeInfo): boolean` — Whether the per-launch token may be injected into the document this request fetches: never on a request the runtime relayed from its loopback WebSocket relay (any local process can dial it, so its missing Origin / Sec-Fetch-Dest prove nothing); otherwise a TOP-LEVEL document only (Sec-Fetch-Dest, document when absent), so a subframe that declares itself gets the desktop global without the token. Absent stays document on purpose: engines send no Sec-Fetch-* to a scheme they don't treat as secure (WKWebView has no API to register one; the Fetch spec sends them only to potentially trustworthy URLs), so failing closed would strip the token from the page itself there. Where it is absent, a same-origin frame cannot be told from the page; the per-world rules below still refuse a request that names another origin. Then, per world: loopback — a LOOPBACK Host, so a DNS-rebinding Host gets no token; memory — the in-process memory transport and an Origin that is absent or exactly the app origin; refuse — never.
- `interface SidecarDefinition` — One sidecar. Data-only fields can live in desktop.sidecars (denext.config.ts); probe, bootstrap and secrets as functions only in runDesktop({ sidecars }), which also overrides a config entry of the same name field by field.
- `interface SidecarExit` — How one run of a sidecar ended.
- `type SidecarExposedValue = string | number | boolean | null` — A value a sidecar shares with the page (SidecarDefinition.expose).
- `interface SidecarHandle` — The handle runDesktop's sidecar(name) returns.
