Made for the OTA refusals that mean "this UI needs a newer binary" (native_too_old, native_mismatch): pass it as checkForUiUpdate's onNativeUpdateRequired.
- `interface PromptStoreUpdateOptions` — Options for promptStoreUpdate.
- `type PromptStoreUpdateResult = updating | store-opened | declined | up-to-date | unsupported` — What promptStoreUpdate did: "updating" (Play's in-app update started), "store-opened", "declined" (the confirm callback said no), "up-to-date" (the store has no newer build), or "unsupported".
- `PullToRefresh(props: PullToRefreshProps): VNode` — A scrolling <div> with pull-to-refresh: pull down from the top, past threshold, and let go to call onRefresh; the spinner then rests near the top and spins while refreshing is true. Set refreshing to true in onRefresh and back to false when the data arrives, as with React Native's RefreshControl (React Native mode's RefreshControl is this same gesture and spinner).
- `interface PullToRefreshProps` — Props of PullToRefresh; any other prop goes to its scrolling <div>.
- `type PullToRefreshStyle = Readonly<Record<string, string | number | undefined>>` — An inline style object, as PullToRefresh accepts and extends it.
- `interface PurchaseOffering` — An offering: the packages a paywall shows, configured in the RevenueCat dashboard.
- `interface PurchaseOfferings` — Every offering, and the one the dashboard marks current.
- `purchasePackage(pkg: PurchasePackage): Promise<PurchaseResult>` — Buy a package through the store's purchase sheet. It resolves once the store completed the purchase (and RevenueCat recorded it), and rejects with a PurchasesError: cancelled when the user closed the sheet, store for anything the store refused.
- `interface PurchasePackage` — A package: one product placed in an offering (monthly, annual, lifetime, …).
- `interface PurchaseProduct` — A store product (the fields most apps show; the SDK's full object is passed through).
- `interface PurchaseResult` — The result of a completed purchase.
- `interface PurchasesConfig` — Options for configurePurchases.
- `interface PurchasesError` — A failed purchases call.
- `type PurchasesErrorCode = cancelled | unsupported | not_configured | store` — Why a purchases call failed, as PurchasesError's code reports it.
- `interface PushNotification` — A push notification, as the shell reports it.
- `type PushPermission = granted | denied | prompt | unsupported` — Whether the app may show notifications, or "unsupported" outside the native shell.
- `interface PushRegistration` — A device's push registration: the token your server sends to, and where it is valid.
- `interface PushTap` — A tap on (or an action of) a notification.
- `interface PushTapOptions` — Options for onPushTapped and usePushTapped.
- `interface QuickAction` — One home-screen quick action.
- `readClipboard(options?: ReadClipboardOptions): Promise<string>` — Read the clipboard: its text by default, or the HTML / image options.format asks for.
- `interface ReadClipboardOptions` — Options for readClipboard.
- `readFile(path: string, options?: ReadFileOptions): Promise<string>` — Read a file.
- `interface ReadFileOptions` — Options for readFile.
- `readSafeAreaInsets(): SafeAreaInsets` — The device's safe-area insets in CSS px, measured once now: the same values useSafeAreaInsets reports, for code outside a component (a store, a canvas setup, a one-off layout calculation). All zero during SSR and where there is no DOM. It adds and removes a hidden element, so it forces a style calculation; to follow changes, use watchSafeAreaInsets.
- `interface RecentMediaOptions` — Options for getRecentMedia.
- `RefreshControl(props: RefreshControlProps): VNode` — Pull-to-refresh around a scroll container: pulling the container down from its top past threshold and letting go calls onRefresh; while refreshing the spinner rests at progressViewOffset. Touch only (as PullToRefresh); give mouse and keyboard users a refresh button too. Pass it to a VirtualList as refreshControl — the list renders it around its scroller with the list's class and style and passes refreshing, onRefresh and progressViewOffset from its own props.
- `interface RefreshControlProps` — Props of RefreshControl (React Native's); any other prop goes to the wrapper.
- `registerForPush(options?: RegisterForPushOptions): Promise<PushRegistration>` — Register the device for remote notifications and resolve its token, for your server to send to through APNs (iOS) or FCM (Android). denext ships no push relay: store the token on your server (with the user it belongs to) and send from there.
- `interface RegisterForPushOptions` — Options for registerForPush.
- `registerSystemIcons(icons: Readonly<Record<string, string>>): void` — Add Material Symbols SystemIcon can draw off iOS: name → the d of the symbol's path in its 960-unit grid (viewBox="0 -960 960 960", as @material-symbols/svg-* ships them). A registered name replaces a built-in one.
- `reloadWidgets(kind?: string): Promise<void>` — Ask the OS to redraw widget kind (every kind when omitted) from its stored snapshot. Outside the native shell, or without the plugin, it does nothing.
- `removeDeliveredNotifications(selector: DeliveredNotificationSelector): Promise<void>` — Remove delivered notifications from the notification centre — local ones and remote pushes alike. Pending (scheduled) notifications are not touched: cancelNotification cancels those.
- `requestPermission(name: PermissionName): Promise<PermissionState>` — Ask for a permission when a prompt can still be shown, and report the outcome. A decided permission (granted, limited, blocked) comes back as it is, without a prompt. A refusal reads blocked on iOS (it never prompts again) and denied on Android's first refusal (a later request prompts again, after your rationale); see PermissionState.
- `requestPushPermission(): Promise<PushPermission>` — Ask for permission to show notifications, when it has not been decided yet, and report the result: "granted", "denied" (the user said no; only the system settings can change it) or "prompt" (still undecided). A decided state comes back without prompting again. Outside the native shell (or without @capacitor/push-notifications) it is "unsupported": there is no web-push fallback. In a Deno Desktop window with the notifications capability it is the OS's notification permission (the app's own notifications; there is no push service on desktop).
- `requestReview(): Promise<ReviewRequestResult>` — Ask the OS to show its in-app rating sheet (StoreKit's requestReview on iOS, the Play In-App Review flow on Android).
- `requestTrackingPermission(): Promise<TrackingStatus>` — Show iOS's "Allow … to track your activity" prompt (once: after an answer iOS only reports it). App Store guideline 5.1.2 requires this before any tracking, and the prompt shows NSUserTrackingUsageDescription as its reason. iOS ignores the request while the app is not active, so call it after launch settles (for example from the first screen's effect), not during startup.
- `type RestoredResult = object | object | object | object | object` — A plugin call that finished while the app was dead, as onRestoredResult delivers it:
- `restorePurchases(): Promise<CustomerInfo>` — Restore the user's earlier purchases (the "Restore purchases" button App Review expects on a paywall).
- `restoreRouteOnRelaunch(options?: RestoreRouteOptions): Promise<string | null>` — Opt in to returning to the last route after the OS killed the app in the background.
- `interface RestoreRouteOptions` — Options for restoreRouteOnRelaunch.
- `resumeFileTransfer(id: string): Promise<boolean>` — Resume a paused download, or retry a failed transfer (a download from its bytes so far when it is resumable).
- `revealInFileManager(item: ShellItem): Promise<void>` — Show a file or folder selected in Finder, Explorer or the Linux file manager.
- `type ReviewRequestResult = requested | unsupported` — What requestReview did: "requested" (the system was asked to show its review sheet; whether it did is the OS's call and is never reported) or "unsupported" (not in the native shell, or no review plugin installed).
- `runBackgroundTask(name: string, details?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<boolean>` — Run one background task now, from the page, in the runner's engine (for example after a sign-in, to warm the cache a later background run will extend). The task runs whatever its interval; its handler sees trigger: "dispatch" and details.
- `interface RunningLiveActivity` — A running Live Activity, as listLiveActivities reports it.
- `runtimePlatform(): RuntimePlatform` — The runtime the page runs in: "ios" or "android" inside a Capacitor native shell, "desktop" inside the Deno Desktop runtime, otherwise "web" (including SSR, where there is no window). The desktop case is read off globalThis.__denext.desktop, a marker the Deno Desktop runtime injects into the page before any script runs; it is a detection hint only, not a security boundary — treat it like any other client-reported value.
- `type RuntimePlatform = ios | android | desktop | web` — The runtime a page runs in, as denext/mobile distinguishes them.
- `SAFE_AREA_CSS: string` — A stylesheet fragment that defines --denext-safe-top, --denext-safe-right, --denext-safe-bottom and --denext-safe-left on :root as the device's safe-area insets (the notch, status bar, navigation bar and home indicator), 0px where there are none. Drop it into a stylesheet or a <style> tag, then pad with the variables.
- `interface SafeAreaInsets` — The device's safe-area insets in CSS px, as useSafeAreaInsets reports them.
- `interface SavedFile` — A file saveFile wrote.
- `interface SavedMedia` — What saveToLibrary saved.
- `saveFile(data: string, options?: SaveFileOptions): Promise<SavedFile | null>` — Save data to a file the user chooses.
- `interface SaveFileOptions` — Options for saveFile.
- `saveToLibrary(source: string, options?: SaveToLibraryOptions): Promise<SavedMedia>` — Save a photo (or GIF) or video to the device's photo library.
- `interface SaveToLibraryOptions` — Options for saveToLibrary.
- `scanBarcode(options?: ScanBarcodeOptions): Promise<ScannedBarcode | null>` — Scan one barcode or QR code with the camera.
- `interface ScanBarcodeOptions` — Options for scanBarcode.
- `interface ScannedBarcode` — What scanBarcode read.
- `interface ScheduledLocalNotification` — A scheduled (pending) local notification.
- `scheduleNotification(notification: LocalNotificationInput): Promise<number>` — Schedule a local notification (or show it now, without a trigger). Scheduling an id that is already pending replaces it.
- `secureStore: SecureStore` — A string key-value store for secrets.
- `interface SecureStore` — The store secureStore implements.
- `type SecureStoreFallback = session` — The opt-in fallbacks of SecureStoreSetOptions.fallback.
- `interface SecureStoreGetOptions` — Options for SecureStore.get.
- `interface SecureStoreSetOptions` — Options for SecureStore.set.
- `interface SecureStoreSetResult` — Where SecureStore.set put the value.
- `interface SentryCapacitorSdk` — The slice of @sentry/capacitor this uses: init(options, siblingInit).
- `interface SentrySiblingSdk` — The slice of the sibling SDK (@sentry/browser, @sentry/react, …): its init.
- `setAudioSession(options?: AudioSessionOptions): Promise<void>` — Set how the app's audio behaves: whether it keeps playing in the background and with the phone locked, and how it meets other apps' audio. In the iOS shell this sets the AVAudioSession category (.playback for background audio) and activates it; on Android the choice decides whether a foreground media service keeps playback alive; on the web (and without the plugin) it does nothing, as a browser decides itself.
- `setKeyboardResizeMode(mode: KeyboardResizeMode): Promise<void>` — Change how the iOS shell resizes the app when the keyboard shows (KeyboardResizeMode), through Keyboard.setResizeMode. @capacitor/keyboard supports it on iOS only, so on Android, on the web and without the plugin this does nothing (Android resizes the WebView itself). The startup mode is plugins.Keyboard.resize in capacitor.config.
- `setNotificationCategories(categories: typeOperator): Promise<void>` — Register the app's notification categories: the action buttons a notification shows when its categoryId names one. The call **replaces** every category registered before, so pass the full set each time.
- `setNowPlaying(info: NowPlayingInfo): Promise<void>` — Show what is playing on the lock screen, in Control Center / the media notification, and on headsets and cars, and offer the controls in info.controls there (they reach onMediaControl). Each call merges info into the last one, so after the first a page sends what changed: { playing: false, position } on pause, a new title for the next track. Calls that only restate the clock (a timeupdate while playing) are not sent on: the OS runs the position on from the rate.
- `setPrivacyScreen(enabled: boolean, options?: PrivacyScreenOptions): Promise<boolean>` — Turn the privacy screen on or off for the whole app.
- `setQuickActions(actions: typeOperator): Promise<void>` — Replace the app's home-screen quick actions (long-press on the icon).
- `setSystemBars(options: SystemBarsOptions): Promise<void>` — Style, hide or show the system bars.
- `setWidgetData(kind: string, data: unknown, options?: SetWidgetDataOptions): Promise<void>` — Store data as the snapshot widget kind renders, and refresh that kind's widgets.
- `interface SetWidgetDataOptions` — Options for setWidgetData.
- `share(opts: ShareOptions): Promise<ShareResult>` — Open the share sheet.
- `interface SharedContent` — One share: any of a web link, text and files.
- `interface SharedFile` — A file shared to the app, copied where the app can read it.
- `interface ShareOptions` — What share shares. At least one of text or url (or title) is needed.
- `type ShareResult = shared | copied | cancelled` — How a share ended: "shared" (the sheet completed), "copied" (no share sheet, so the text was copied to the clipboard) or "cancelled" (the user dismissed it).
- `type ShellItem = string | object` — What openPath, revealInFileManager and moveToTrash act on: an absolute path inside the app's own folders (from downloadToFile), or { handle } for a file or folder the user picked (pickDocument, pickFolder and saveFile results carry one, so the result itself can be passed). A picked item's path is display-only: pass its handle.
- `showContextMenu(items: typeOperator, options?: ContextMenuOptions): Promise<string | null>` — Open a context menu and resolve the chosen item's id, or null if it was dismissed.
- `signInNative<User>(session: IdTokenSession<User>, provider: apple | google, options?: Omit<GoogleSignInOptions, nonce>): Promise<User>` — The whole native sign-in against a denext server: fetch a single-use nonce from the server, show the provider's sheet with it, and hand the id_token to session.signInWithIdToken(provider, result) (POST /auth/native/:provider), which verifies it and starts the session.
- `signInWithApple(options?: AppleSignInOptions): Promise<SocialSignInResult>` — Show the native "Sign in with Apple" sheet (iOS 13+) and resolve its id_token, the authorizationCode, and the name and email Apple sends. **Apple sends the name only on the user's first sign-in**, so pass it to the server then (signInWithIdToken does).
- `signInWithGoogle(options: GoogleSignInOptions): Promise<SocialSignInResult>` — Show Google's native account sheet (Credential Manager on Android, Google Sign-In on iOS) and resolve its id_token plus the profile's name and email.
- `interface SocialSignInError` — A failed native sign-in.
- `type SocialSignInErrorCode = cancelled | no_id_token | unsupported | failed` — Why a native sign-in failed, as SocialSignInError's code reports it.
- `interface SocialSignInResult` — What a native sign-in sheet returns: pass it to signInWithIdToken(provider, result).
- `type SqliteBackend = native | opfs | memory` — Where a database lives: the native plugin, OPFS in the browser, or memory.
- `type SqliteBindValue = string | number | boolean | null | Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer` — A value a statement binds: booleans bind as 1/0, an ArrayBuffer as a blob.
- `interface SqliteDatabase` — An open database (openSqlite).
- `class SqliteEncryptionError` — A refused encryption request: ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE (this backing has no SQLCipher, or the plugin has encryption off; nothing ran), WRONG_KEY (another passphrase than the one the plugin keeps), KEY_REQUIRED (the database is encrypted: run PRAGMA key first) or UNSUPPORTED (a key pragma other than PRAGMA key = '…' as the first statement, such as PRAGMA rekey).
- `type SqliteEncryptionErrorCode = ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE | WRONG_KEY | KEY_REQUIRED | UNSUPPORTED` — Why SqliteEncryptionError was thrown.
- `interface SqliteOptions` — Options for openSqlite and deleteSqlite.
- `type SqliteParams = typeOperator | Readonly<Record<string, SqliteBindValue>>` — A statement's parameters: positional (?), or named by their placeholder, prefix included ({ $id: 1 } for $id, { ":id": 1 } for :id).
- `type SqliteRow = Record<string, SqliteValue>` — A row as an object keyed by column name.
- `interface SqliteRows` — Rows as column names plus one value array per row, in column order.
- `interface SqliteRunResult` — What a write reports.
- `type SqliteValue = string | number | null | Uint8Array` — A value SQLite stores.
- `interface SqliteWasmUrls` — The engine's two files.
- `startFlexibleUpdate(): Promise<AppUpdateOutcome>` — Android: start Play's flexible update, which downloads in the background while the app keeps running. Follow it with onFlexibleUpdateProgress, and once the status is "downloaded", call completeFlexibleUpdate (after asking the user) to install and restart. Call getAppUpdateInfo first.
- `startLiveActivity(name: string, attributes: LiveActivityValues, state: LiveActivityValues, options?: StartLiveActivityOptions): Promise<string>` — Start a Live Activity rendered by the UI denext mobile add live-activity --name <name> generated (<name>LiveActivity.swift, which reads context.attributes and context.state).
- `interface StartLiveActivityOptions` — Options for startLiveActivity.
- `stopBackgroundLocation(): Promise<void>` — Stop background location, whichever watch started it. Resolves once the plugin has stopped (at once without the plugin: stop a foreground fallback with the function watchPositionInBackground returned).
- `interface StoreListingOptions` — Where openStoreReview sends the user.
- `type SystemBar = status | navigation` — One of the system bars: the top status bar, or the navigation / gesture bar at the bottom.
- `interface SystemBarsOptions` — What setSystemBars changes; a field left out is left as it is.
- `type SystemBarsStyle = light | dark | auto` — The theme the system bars sit over: "light" (a light app, so dark icons and text), "dark" (a dark app, so light icons and text) or "auto" (the device's appearance). This is Capacitor's SystemBarsStyle; note that expo-status-bar's style names the content's color instead, the opposite way round.
- `SystemIcon(props: SystemIconProps): VNode` — The platform's icon: the SF Symbol name inside the iOS shell (natively rendered, tinted by the CSS color), the Material Symbol android (or the one mapped from name) everywhere else. SSR draws the Material Symbol; the iOS shell swaps in the SF Symbol before paint once it is cached, and hides the box for the one bridge round trip of a first render.
- `type SystemIconMode = monochrome | hierarchical | palette | multicolor` — How an SF Symbol is colored: "monochrome" (the default: the icon is a mask filled with the CSS color, so it follows the text color, dark mode and :hover), "hierarchical" (layers in opacities of color), "palette" (colors, one per layer) or "multicolor" (Apple's own colors).
- `interface SystemIconProps` — Props of SystemIcon.
- `type SystemIconWeight = ultralight | thin | light | regular | medium | semibold | bold | heavy | black` — An SF Symbol weight (UIImage.SymbolWeight).
- `type TrackingStatus = authorized | denied | restricted | not-determined | unavailable` — The ATT status:
- `unlockOrientation(): Promise<void>` — Release a lockOrientation lock (a no-op when nothing is locked, or on a browser without the API).
- `updateLiveActivity(id: string, state: LiveActivityValues): Promise<void>` — Replace a running Live Activity's state.
- `uploadFile(url: string, path: string, options?: UploadFileOptions): Promise<UploadFileResult>` — Upload a file to a URL, with progress.
- `interface UploadFileOptions` — Options for uploadFile.
- `interface UploadFileResult` — What an upload answered.
- `useAppResume(cb: (awayMs: number) => void): void` — Hook form of onAppResume: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount. The latest cb is always called (it is held in a ref), so passing a fresh closure each render never re-subscribes.
- `useBackHandler(handler: BackHandler, enabled?: boolean): void` — Hook form of onBack: handler is registered while the component is mounted and enabled is true, and it always sees the latest props (re-renders do not re-register it, so its place in the stack stays put). A component mounted later sits above it.
- `useBackProgress(): BackGesture | null` — Hook form of onBackProgress: the back gesture in flight (progress 0…1 and the edge it started from), or null when there is none, e.g. to drive a peek of the previous screen. Always null outside the Android shell with denext mobile add back.
- `useBackSwipe(onBack: () => void, opts?: BackSwipeOptions): (el: Element | null) => void` — Swipe right to go back. Returns a ref callback: attach it to the element that should recognize the gesture (often the page's scroll container). A touch that travels rightward at least minDistance CSS px (default 72), with horizontal travel at least ratio (default 1.4) × vertical travel, fires onBack once, as soon as it qualifies.
- `useContextMenu(items: ContextMenuItems, onSelect: (id: string) => void, options?: ContextMenuTargetOptions): (el: ContextMenuElement | null) => void` — attachContextMenu as a hook: returns a ref callback for the element. The latest items, onSelect and options are read when a menu opens, so they can change every render without rebinding.
- `useDeepLink(callback: (event: DeepLinkEvent) => void, options?: DeepLinkOptions): void` — Hook form of onDeepLink: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount. The latest callback and options are used for each link (they are held in refs), so fresh closures each render never re-subscribe.
- `useEntitlement(id: string): EntitlementState` — Whether the user has an entitlement, live: read on mount, after every purchase / restore / getCustomerInfo anywhere in the app, and each time the app returns to the foreground.
- `useFontScale(): number` — Hook form of getFontScale: the factor, read on mount and kept current. It starts at the last value read (1 before any), so the first render uses the default size.
- `useKeepAwake(active?: boolean): void` — Keep the screen from dimming and locking while the component is mounted and active is true (a video call, a recipe, a boarding pass).
- `useKeyboard(): KeyboardState` — Hook form of onKeyboardChange: the keyboard's current state, updated on every change until unmount. It reads { visible: false, height: 0 } during SSR and before mount.
- `useKeyboardInset(opts?: KeyboardInsetOptions): number` — Hook form of installKeyboardInset: installs the custom property on mount, disposes it on unmount, and returns the px of the page the keyboard currently covers (0 during SSR and before mount).
- `useLocalNotificationTapped(callback: (tap: LocalNotificationTap) => void, options?: LocalNotificationTapOptions): void` — Hook form of onLocalNotificationTapped: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and always uses the latest callback and options.
- `useLocation(options?: UseLocationOptions): LocationState` — Hook form of watchPosition: the latest fix and error, watched while mounted and enabled. Changing accuracy or minimumIntervalMs restarts the watch.
- `interface UseLocationOptions` — Options for useLocation.
- `useMediaControl(handler: (event: MediaControlEvent) => void): void` — Hook form of onMediaControl: handles the OS's media commands while the component is mounted, always with the latest handler.
- `useMomentumSafeScroll(options?: MomentumSafeScrollOptions): void` — Hook form of installMomentumSafeScroll: installs on mount and uninstalls when the last mounted hook unmounts. An install made by denext's runtime or directly with installMomentumSafeScroll is left in place. A change to force or settleMs re-runs the hook (it releases its share, then takes a new one); settleMs applies only when that share is the one that installs the shim, since a live install keeps its own options.
- `useNativeViewSlot(type: string, options?: NativeViewSlotOptions): NativeViewSlotHandle` — Keep a native view of type on a slot element: the hook behind NativeViewSlot. Put ref on the slot (give it a size), overlayRef on the element holding DOM drawn over the view, and, while placement is "embed", render nativeViewEmbedScroller inside it. Render your web fallback while status is "web" or "error".
- `useNetworkStatus(): NetworkStatus` — Hook form of networkStatus: the current status, updated on every change until unmount. Before mount (and during SSR) it reads { connected: true, connectionType: "unknown" }, so an offline banner never flashes on first paint.
- `useOpenFile(callback: (file: OpenedFile) => void): void` — Hook form of onOpenFile: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and calls the latest callback (held in a ref, so a fresh closure each render never re-subscribes).
- `useOrientation(): Orientation` — The screen's orientation, live: re-renders on every rotation. The first render reads the web API (or portrait-primary during SSR); in the native shell the plugin's answer follows.
- `usePermission(name: PermissionName, options?: UsePermissionOptions): PermissionHandle` — A permission's live status: checked on mount (or requested, with request: true), and checked again each time the app returns to the foreground, so it follows a change the user made in Settings after openAppSettings.
- `interface UsePermissionOptions` — Options for usePermission.
- `usePrivacyScreen(enabled?: boolean, options?: PrivacyScreenOptions): void` — Hide the app from the app switcher while the component is mounted and enabled is true (an account page, a banking screen). Several mounted callers share it: the privacy screen turns off once the last one unmounts or turns enabled off. On the web it does nothing.
- `usePushReceived(callback: (notification: PushNotification) => void): void` — Hook form of onPushReceived: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and always calls the latest callback.
- `usePushTapped(callback: (tap: PushTap) => void, options?: PushTapOptions): void` — Hook form of onPushTapped: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and always uses the latest callback and options.
- `useQuickAction(callback: (id: string) => void): void` — Hook form of onQuickAction: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and always calls the latest callback.
- `useReducedMotion(): boolean` — Whether the user asked for reduced motion (iOS Reduce Motion, Android Remove animations, the desktop setting), updated when it changes: prefers-reduced-motion, which the iOS and Android WebViews report from the OS. false during SSR. The same answer as Reanimated's useReducedMotion and React Native's AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled() in React Native mode.
- `useRestoredResult(handler: (result: RestoredResult) => void): void` — Hook form of onRestoredResult: listens while mounted, always calling the latest handler. Mount it high (the root layout's client provider) so it is listening when the relaunched app starts.
- `useSafeAreaInsets(): SafeAreaInsets` — The device's safe-area insets in CSS px ({ top, right, bottom, left }), kept up to date on rotation, window and visual-viewport resizes, and when Capacitor updates the insets it injects (on Android the bottom inset drops to 0 while the keyboard is up). The values are the same expressions SAFE_AREA_CSS uses, measured through a hidden fixed element, so they need viewport-fit=cover too. All zero during SSR and before mount.
- `useScreenReader(): boolean` — Hook form: whether a screen reader is on, read on mount and kept current until unmount. It is false before the first answer (and always on the web), so render the sighted layout first and let the screen-reader one replace it.
- `useShareReceived(callback: (content: SharedContent) => void): void` — Hook form of onShareReceived: subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, and always calls the latest callback.
- `useSystemBarsFollowTheme(scheme?: light | dark | null): void` — Keep the system bars' style matching the app's light / dark theme while the component is mounted: dark bars over a dark theme, light bars over a light one. With a scheme argument that is the theme; without one it follows the page, re-applied on every change: the root element's color-scheme when it names one (a theme toggle that sets it, or React Native's Appearance.setColorScheme in react-native mode), else the system's prefers-color-scheme. Only the native shell has system bars to style; elsewhere, and during SSR, it does nothing.
- `watchPosition(callback: (position: GeoPosition) => void, options?: GeoPositionOptions, onError?: (error: GeolocationError) => void): () => void` — Follow the position: callback runs with each new fix until the returned function is called. A failure (permission refused, services turned off) goes to onError; the watch keeps running where the platform keeps it (the browser does), so stop it yourself on denied.
- `watchPositionInBackground(callback: (position: GeoPosition) => void, options?: BackgroundLocationOptions, onError?: (error: GeolocationError) => void): () => void` — Follow the position in the foreground and the background: callback runs with each fix until the returned function (or stopBackgroundLocation) is called. A failure (permission refused: denied; anything else: unavailable) goes to onError.
- `watchSafeAreaInsets(onInsets: (insets: SafeAreaInsets) => void): () => void` — Follow the device's safe-area insets outside a component: calls onInsets synchronously with the current insets, then again whenever they change (rotation, window and visual-viewport resizes, Capacitor rewriting the --safe-area-inset-* it injects on <html>, and the web view applying its insets late, after the page has run), at most once per animation frame and only when they differ. It is what useSafeAreaInsets runs. During SSR (no DOM) it calls nothing and the returned stop function is a no-op.
- `writeClipboard(content: string | ClipboardContent): Promise<void>` — Write to the clipboard: text, or rich content (HTML with a plain-text alternative, or a PNG image as base64).
- `writeFile(path: string, data: string, options?: WriteFileOptions): Promise<void>` — Write a file, replacing it when it exists.
- `interface WriteFileOptions` — Options for writeFile.

### `denext/mobile/clerk`

- `interface ClerkBrowserSignInOptions` — Options for the hosted (browser) sign-in.
- `interface ClerkLike` — The slice of a clerk-js Clerk instance the hosted sign-in uses (what @clerk/expo's useHostedAuth uses).
- `interface ClerkMobileBridge` — What installClerkMobileBridge installed.
- `interface ClerkMobileBridgeOptions` — Options for installClerkMobileBridge.
- `interface ClerkMobileBrowserSignInOptions` — Options for startClerkMobileBrowserSignIn.
- `interface ClerkOAuthTransport` — @clerk/electron's OAuth transport shape.
- `interface ClerkPasskeysAdapter` — A WebAuthn adapter clerk-js accepts (passkeys from @clerk/electron/passkeys): the shape @clerk/electron/react attaches to its instance.
- `interface ClerkTokenCache` — @clerk/electron's token cache shape.
- `installClerkMobileBridge(options: ClerkMobileBridgeOptions): ClerkMobileBridge | undefined` — Install Clerk's native bridge in the Capacitor shell (see the module docs). Call it once, before the page's Clerk code loads clerk-js — from instrumentation-client.ts in an App Router app, or at the top of a SPA entry. Outside the shell (the web, Deno Desktop) it installs nothing.
- `startClerkMobileBrowserSignIn(clerk: ClerkLike, options: ClerkMobileBrowserSignInOptions): Promise<object>` — Sign in through Clerk's hosted pages in the shell's auth session and activate the session here: @clerk/expo's useHostedAuth protocol over openAuthSession, with a fresh state and S256 PKCE pair; the callback's nonce is redeemed only with the verifier, which never leaves this page. The passkey path of installClerkMobileBridge, and any method Clerk's hosted pages offer.

### `denext/updates`

- `applyUpdates(config?: UpdatesConfig, onProgress?: UpdateProgressListener): Promise<UpdatesResult>` — Install every update on offer, reporting each step to onProgress: on a phone the new UI, on Deno Desktop the whole app (or, when no newer app is on offer, the UI overlay), in a browser the newer deploy. It never throws; a target that failed is listed in failures (and reported as stage: "failed").
- `interface AvailableUpdate` — An update the server offers, verified where the platform verifies before installing.
- `checkForUpdates(config?: UpdatesConfig): Promise<UpdatesCheck>` — What the server offers this app, on whatever platform it runs. It never throws: a target that could not be checked is listed in failures.
- `interface DesktopUpdatesConfig` — Which Deno Desktop targets to update (both by default).
- `interface UpdateFailure` — A target that could not be checked or installed.
- `interface UpdateProgress` — One progress report from applyUpdates, the same shape on every platform.
- `type UpdateProgressListener = (progress: UpdateProgress) => void` — Reports progress (see UpdateProgress).
- `interface UpdatesCheck` — What checkForUpdates found.
- `interface UpdatesConfig` — Where each platform's updates come from. Only the running platform's part is read, so one config serves every build.
- `interface UpdatesResult` — What applyUpdates did, when it returns (a reload or relaunch never returns).
- `type UpdateStage = checking | downloading | ready | applying | done | up-to-date | failed` — Where one target's update is:
- `type UpdateTarget = ui | app | web` — What an update replaces:
- `interface WebUpdatesConfig` — How a browser tab learns that a newer build is deployed.

### `denext/navigation`

- `announceRoute(message: string): void` — Announce message to screen readers now (the same text twice in a row is announced twice). Nothing happens without a document or with an empty message.
- `browserHistory(): HistorySource` — The browser's own history as a HistorySource, for an app with no router (or one that navigates only through this source): push / replace write history.pushState / replaceState and stamp each entry with its index, and popstate (back, forward) is heard. A pushState made behind its back is not.
- `type Component<P> = (props: P & object) => VNode | Promise<VNode>` — A component is a function that receives props and returns a renderable node.
- `createBottomTabNavigatorFactory(core: ReactNavigationCore): (config?: unknown) => unknown` — createBottomTabNavigator for React Native mode, drawn by TabsView: visited tabs stay mounted (hidden with <Activity>), tabBarBadge / tabBarIcon / tabBarLabel / title and lazy / popToTopOnBlur / unmountOnBlur are honoured, and a press on the active tab emits tabPress (a nested stack pops to its root) then scrolls it to the top.
- `createNativeStackNavigatorFactory(core: ReactNavigationCore): (config?: unknown) => unknown` — createNativeStackNavigator for React Native mode, drawn by StackView.
- `Fragment: FragmentComponent` — Groups children without a wrapping element (<>…</> / <Fragment key ref>). The value is the FRAGMENT marker; it is typed as a component so <Fragment> type-checks as a JSX tag with React's FragmentProps, a ref receiving a FragmentInstance included.
- `interface HistoryLocation` — A location as the history bindings read it.
- `interface HistoryScreen` — One screen of a HistoryStack's table.
- `interface HistorySource` — A history-based router, as HistoryStack and HistoryTabs use it: read the location, hear it change, and navigate. browserHistory, tanstackHistory and reactRouterHistory build one; any router whose location lives in the URL history can implement it in a few lines.
- `HistoryStack(props: HistoryStackProps): VNode` — A native-feeling stack over any history-based router; see the module docs. Mount it where the router would render the routes it covers (in a TanStack Router layout route, in place of its <Outlet />), and give it the screens; the router keeps owning the URL.
- `interface HistoryStackProps` — Props of HistoryStack. theme, material and accentColor pick the look; see NavigationThemeProps.
- `interface HistoryTab` — One tab of a HistoryTabs: a TabDefinition that renders itself.
- `HistoryTabs(props: HistoryTabsProps): VNode` — A tab bar over any history-based router whose tabs keep their state; see the module docs.
- `interface HistoryTabsProps` — Props of HistoryTabs.
- `type IosBarMaterial = glass | blur` — The iOS bar material of the platform theme: "glass" (iOS 26's Liquid Glass, approximated: a floating translucent tab bar and glass header buttons; the default) or "blur" (the iOS 7–18 translucent bars, edge to edge).
- `type Key = string | number | bigint | null | undefined` — A stable identity for a VNode among its siblings, used to keep lists reconciled.
- `matchScreenPath(pattern: string, pathname: string): Record<string, string> | null` — Match pathname against a screen pattern: literal segments, :name or $name params (TanStack Router's spelling too), and a trailing * or $ splat (its value under "*" and "_splat"). Returns the decoded params, or null when it does not match.
- `type NavigationPlatform = ios | android` — The platform look a navigator takes: iOS or Android (Material).
- `type NavigationTheme = auto | platform | plain` — Which look the navigators take:
- `interface NavigationThemeProps` — The theme props every navigator takes.
- `platformThemeCss(): string` — The whole platform-theme stylesheet (exported for tests and for apps that ship it in their own CSS, e.g. to have it before the first client render).
- `interface ReactNavigationCore` — The part of @react-navigation/native (which re-exports @react-navigation/core and the routers) the factories need: import * as core from "@react-navigation/native" fits.
- `interface ReactNavigationDescriptor` — One screen's descriptor (options are the library's own screen options).
- `interface ReactNavigationObject` — The slice of the navigation object the navigators use.
- `interface ReactNavigationRoute` — A React Navigation route, as the navigators read it.
- `interface ReactNavigationState` — A navigator's state, as the navigators read it.
- `reactRouterHistory(router: ReactRouterLike): HistorySource` — A React Router data router (createBrowserRouter / createHashRouter / createMemoryRouter, library mode) as a HistorySource: the location from router.state, changes from router.subscribe, navigations through router.navigate. The entry index is the browser router's history.state.idx where it exists.
- `interface ReactRouterLike` — The slice of a React Router data router (createBrowserRouter) reactRouterHistory uses.
- `resolveScreen(screens: typeOperator, loc: Pick<HistoryLocation, pathname | search | hash>): object | null` — The first screen of screens that matches loc, with its match.
- `interface ScreenMatch` — What a screen renders from: the location it was pushed at, matched against its path.
- `interface ScreenOptions` — Options for one screen of a stack. As a page's export const screenOptions = { … } they are plain JSON (the server reads them and ships them with the page); setOptions from useStackNavigation can also set the component-valued header* slots.
- `Sheet(props: SheetProps): VNode` — A bottom sheet. Controlled by open; the user's dismissal calls onOpenChange(false).
- `type SheetDetent = medium | large | fit | number` — A height a sheet can rest at: "medium" (half the available height), "large" (the full available height), "fit" (its content's height, up to "large"), or a number (a fraction of the available height when at most 1, else CSS px).
- `interface SheetProps` — Props of Sheet.
- `type StackAnimation = default | none | fade | fade_from_bottom | slide_from_right | slide_from_left | slide_from_bottom | simple_push | ios_from_right | ios_from_left | shared_axis_x` — How a screen enters and leaves a stack. The names follow react-native-screens' native-stack animation option:
- `StackHeader(props: StackHeaderProps): VNode` — A native-style header for a stack screen. StackLayout draws it when a screen's headerShown is true; it is exported for custom headers that want the same look.
- `interface StackHeaderProps` — Props of StackHeader.
- `StackLayout(props: StackLayoutProps): VNode` — A native-feeling stack of the routes under a layout; see the module docs.
- `interface StackLayoutProps` — Props of StackLayout. theme (default "auto": the platform theme inside the native shell), material and accentColor pick the look; see NavigationThemeProps.
- `interface StackNavigation` — The stack navigation a screen gets from useStackNavigation.
- `type StackPresentation = card | modal | formSheet | transparentModal` — How a screen is presented:
- `StackView(props: StackViewProps): VNode` — The router-independent stack view; see the module docs. StackLayout is the App Router binding most apps use.
- `type StackViewAnimate = auto | external | none` — How a change of entries animates: "auto" (the view animates it), "external" (a View Transition the owner started animates it), "none".
- `interface StackViewEntry` — One screen as the stack view draws it (bottom of the stack first).
- `interface StackViewHandle` — What StackView lets its owner do.
- `interface StackViewProps` — Props of StackView. The theme props (theme, material, accentColor) pick the platform look: see NavigationThemeProps.
- `interface TabDefinition` — One tab of a TabsLayout.
- `interface TabScope` — A tab's registry of the stacks rendered inside it.
- `TabsLayout(props: TabsLayoutProps): VNode` — A tab bar layout whose tabs keep their state; see the module docs. Render it from a "use client" component your layout uses.
- `interface TabsLayoutProps` — Props of TabsLayout. theme (default "auto": the platform theme inside the native shell), material and accentColor pick the look (see NavigationThemeProps).
- `interface TabStackHandle` — What a stack inside a tab registers, so the tab bar can pop it or scroll it to the top.
- `TabsView(props: TabsViewProps): VNode` — The router-independent tab view: panels kept with <Activity>, and the bar.
- `interface TabsViewProps` — Props of TabsView. theme, material and accentColor pick the look (see NavigationThemeProps).
- `tanstackHistory(routerOrHistory: TanStackRouterLike | TanStackHistoryLike): HistorySource` — A TanStack Router (or its router.history) as a HistorySource. With the router, navigations go through router.navigate({ href }) (so loaders, blockers and view transitions run as for a <Link>); with a bare history, through history.push. The entry index comes from TanStack's __TSR_index, so back and forward are exact.
- `interface TanStackHistoryLike` — The slice of @tanstack/history's RouterHistory tanstackHistory uses.
- `interface TanStackRouterLike` — The slice of a TanStack Router tanstackHistory uses.
- `useScreenInfo(): object | null` — The screen a component renders in, or null outside a stack. Reads id and index (0 = the stack's root screen).
- `useScreenMatch(): ScreenMatch | null` — The location the screen this component renders in was pushed at (its path params, search and hash), or null outside a HistoryStack. Read this in a screen rather than the router's own location hooks: a kept screen below the top keeps its own location, while the router's hooks follow the top screen.
- `useStackNavigation(): StackNavigation` — The stack navigation for the screen this component renders in: push, pop, popToTop, replace, canGoBack, setOptions. Outside a StackLayout the methods fall back to plain navigation and history.
- `interface VNode` — A single virtual DOM node.
- `type VNodeChild = VNode | string | number | bigint | boolean | null | undefined` — Anything that can appear as a child in JSX.
- `type VNodeChildren = VNodeChild | VNodeChild[]` — One child or an array of children, as accepted by JSX.
- `type VNodeType = string | Component<any> | FRAGMENT` — The type field of a VNode: an intrinsic tag name, a component fn, or a fragment marker.
- `interface VProps` — Props passed to a virtual node. children is normalized separately.

### `denext/virtual-masonry`

- `class MasonryLayout` — A masonry layout over count items.
- `interface MasonryPlacement` — An item's placement.
- `VirtualMasonry<T>(props: VirtualMasonryProps<T>): VNode` — A virtualized masonry (Pinterest-style) layout: items of any height in numColumns balanced columns, only those near the viewport rendered. Items are measured as they render (give getEstimatedItemSize, e.g. from an image's aspect ratio, for a steadier scrollbar); appends keep every placed item where it is; onEndReached loads the next page once per data change. Import from denext/virtual-masonry.
- `interface VirtualMasonryHandle` — The imperative handle of a VirtualMasonry.
- `interface VirtualMasonryProps<T>` — Props of VirtualMasonry.

### `denext/mvu`

- `interface ChannelLike` — A channel reference as createChannel exports it (server) or its browser stub.
- `interface ChannelSubscription<Msg>` — Turn each payload a createChannel channel publishes for key into a message.
- `defineMvu<Model, Msg, Props>(program: MvuProgram<Model, Msg, Props>): MvuProgram<Model, Msg, Props>` — Identity, for inference: write the program once and run it with useMvu / MvuView in the browser or defineLiveView on the server.
- `interface DelayEffect<Msg>` — Dispatch msg after ms milliseconds (cancelled when the program stops).
- `interface DispatchEffect<Msg>` — Dispatch msg right after the current update (a follow-up message).
- `type Effect<Msg> = FetchEffect<Msg> | DelayEffect<Msg> | TaskEffect<Msg> | DispatchEffect<Msg>` — Work an update asks the runtime to do. Plain data: compare it in tests.
- `interface EffectConstructors` — The effect constructors (fx). Each returns plain data the runtime runs after the update.
- `type EventBinding = (event: Event | SyntheticEvent<any, any>) => void` — What send(…) returns: an event handler for any on* prop. It takes the synthetic event a JSX handler receives (onClick, onSubmit, onInput, …) or a DOM Event (addEventListener), and reads only its target, key and type.
- `eventPayload(event: unknown): EventPayload` — The EventPayload of a DOM event: a form control target's value / checked (an input, a select, a textarea), a keyboard event's key, and a submit's text fields. A submit is preventDefaulted (the program handles it).
- `interface EventPayload` — The parts of a DOM event a message can be built from (and the server validates).
- `interface FetchEffect<Msg>` — Fetch url and turn the response into a message.
- `fx: EffectConstructors` — Effect constructors. Each returns plain data; the runtime runs it after the update.
- `interface IntervalSubscription<Msg>` — Dispatch msg every ms milliseconds while the subscription is active.
- `type MsgSource<Msg> = Msg | parenthesized` — A message, or a function building one from the event (null dispatches nothing).
- `interface MvuProgram<Model, Msg, Props>` — A whole program: runs in the browser with useMvu / MvuView, or on the server as a live view.
- `MvuView<Model, Msg, Props>(props: MvuViewProps<Model, Msg, Props>): VNode` — Render a whole program in the browser: useMvu over its init / update / subscriptions, and its view with a send that dispatches locally. The server twin is defineLiveView.
- `interface MvuViewProps<Model, Msg, Props>` — Props for MvuView.
- `type Next<Model, Msg> = typeOperator` — What an update (or init) returns: the next model, and the effects to run.
- `type Send<Msg> = (msg: MsgSource<Msg>) => EventBinding` — Bind a message to an event: onClick={send({ type: "inc" })}, or with the event's payload onInput={send((e) => ({ type: "typed", text: e.value ?? "" }))}.
- `subs: SubscriptionConstructors` — Subscription constructors.
- `type Subscription<Msg> = IntervalSubscription<Msg> | ChannelSubscription<Msg>` — A source of messages the runtime keeps open while the model asks for it.
- `interface SubscriptionConstructors` — The subscription constructors (subs).
- `type Subscriptions<Model, Msg> = (model: Model) => ReadonlyArray<Subscription<Msg> | null | false | undefined>` — The model's active subscriptions; falsy entries are skipped (cond && subs.interval(…)).
- `interface TaskEffect<Msg>` — Run an async function and turn its result into a message.
- `type Update<Model, Msg> = (msg: Msg, model: Model) => Next<Model, Msg>` — The update function: a message and the current model in, the next model and effects out.
- `useMvu<Model, Msg>(init: () => Next<Model, Msg>, update: Update<Model, Msg>, subscriptions?: Subscriptions<Model, Msg>, options?: UseMvuOptions): typeOperator` — Run a Model–View–Update program in a component. init runs once (on the server too, for the first HTML); its effects, every later update's effects and the subscriptions run in the browser only, and stop when the component unmounts.
- `interface UseMvuOptions` — Options for useMvu.
- `type View<Model, Msg> = (model: Model, send: Send<Msg>) => VNodeChildren` — Render the model; bind events with send.

### `denext/feature`

- `feature(name: string): boolean` — Whether the feature flag name is enabled. A feature("KEY") call with a **string literal** argument is folded to a boolean literal at build time (for a KEY listed in features) so the branch is dead-code eliminated; otherwise it reads the build-seeded flag map at runtime, defaulting to false for any unset flag.

### `denext/gleam`

- `defineLustreView<Flags, Props>(config: LustreViewConfig<Flags, Props>): LustreViewComponent<Props>` — Define a Lustre server component: a Lustre app whose state lives on the server, one runtime per mounted view per Live connection. Render the returned component from a Server Component.
- `gleam(options?: GleamOptions): DenextPlugin` — The Gleam build plugin. Registers a prepare step that runs gleam build --target javascript in the Gleam project (gleam.toml at the app root, else gleam/, or options.dir).
- `interface GleamOptions` — Options shared by the plugin and denext add gleam:.
- `interface GleamResult` — A Gleam Result as Gleam's JavaScript output builds it (Ok / Error, the value at [0]).
- `interface LustreApp<Flags>` — A Lustre application (lustre.App(flags, model, msg)), as Gleam's .d.mts declares it. Flags is inferred from it: counter.app() typed App$<number, Model$, Msg$> makes the flags a number.
- `lustreElement<Attrs>(kit: LustreKit, tag: string, app: LustreApp<undefined>): (props: LustreElementAttributes<Attrs>) => VNode` — Turn a Lustre component into a denext component that renders it as the custom element tag. Export the result from a "use client" module.
- `type LustreElementAttributes<Attrs> = Partial<Attrs> & object` — The props of a Lustre custom element in JSX: its attributes (each a string, the component's on_attribute_change decoders parse them), the usual global ones, and light-DOM children for the component's slots.
- `interface LustreEventPayload` — A DOM event a Lustre view's client sent, after the built-in shape check.
- `lustreIsland<Flags, Props>(kit: LustreKit, app: LustreApp<Flags>, options?: LustreIslandOptions<Flags, Props>): (props: Props) => VNode` — Turn a Lustre app into a denext island component. Export the result from a "use client" module.
- `interface LustreIslandOptions<Flags, Props>` — How lustreIsland maps the component's props onto the app.
- `lustreKit(modules: LustreModules): LustreKit` — Wrap the app's Lustre functions for denext/gleam. The generated .denext/lustre.ts calls this; app code imports the kit from there.
- `interface LustreKit` — What denext/gleam's Lustre helpers call: the app's Lustre build, wrapped.
- `interface LustreModules` — The functions lustreKit takes, imported from the app's Lustre build.
- `interface LustreReconciler` — Lustre's client reconciler (lustre/vdom/reconciler.ffi.mjs), as far as this module uses it.
- `type LustreReconcilerClass = (root: Element, decodeEvent: (event: Event, path: string, name: string, include?: string[]) => unknown, dispatch: (event: Event, data: unknown) => void) => LustreReconciler` — The Reconciler class: new Reconciler(root, decodeEvent, dispatch).
- `type LustreRuntime = object` — A running client-side Lustre app (Lustre's Runtime).
- `interface LustreRuntimeInstance` — A Lustre server Runtime as its constructor builds it (only send is used).
- `lustreServerKit(modules: LustreServerModules): LustreServerKit` — Wrap the app's Lustre server-component functions for defineLustreView. The generated .denext/lustre-server.ts calls this.
- `interface LustreServerKit` — What defineLustreView and the Live hub call: the app's Lustre server runtime, wrapped.
- `interface LustreServerModules` — The functions lustreServerKit takes, imported from the app's Lustre build.
- `type LustreServerRuntime = object` — A running Lustre server component.
- `interface LustreViewComponent<Props>` — The component defineLustreView returns.
- `interface LustreViewConfig<Flags, Props>` — What defineLustreView takes.
- `lustreViewIsland(Reconciler: LustreReconcilerClass): (props: LustreViewIslandProps) => VNode` — The browser island for defineLustreView, bound to Lustre's reconciler. The Gleam build calls this in the generated .denext/lustre-view.ts; apps don't.
- `interface LustreViewIslandProps` — The island's props (written by defineLustreView's server render).
- `interface PrerenderedShadow` — A custom element's prerendered shadow root (a <template shadowrootmode>).

### `denext/platform`

- `platform: Platform` — The target this build is for. Folded to a string literal at build time in the app's own modules (and platform === "…" to a boolean), so other targets' branches are removed.
- `type Platform = web | ios | android | macos | windows | linux` — A build target: the web, a phone OS, or a desktop OS.

### `denext/result`

- `andThen<T, E, U, F>(result: Result<T, E>, fn: (value: T) => Result<U, F>): Result<U, E | F>` — Chain a step that can itself fail: run fn on the success value; a failure short-circuits.
- `assertNever(value: never, message?: string): never` — Fail at compile time when a value that should be impossible is still possible: put it in the default of a switch over a union (default: return assertNever(shape)), and a missing case becomes a type error. Reached at runtime (data that broke the types), it throws a TypeError.
- `err<E>(error: E): Err<E, undefined>` — A failure carrying error (a string literal stays a literal type: err("not_found") is Err<"not_found">).
- `interface Err<E, D>` — A failure: ok is false, error says what went wrong, details optionally adds more.
- `isErr<T, E>(result: Result<T, E>): result is Err` — Is result a failure? Reads .ok (see isOk).
- `isOk<T, E>(result: Result<T, E>): result is Ok` — Is result a success? Reads .ok, so it also works on a Result that crossed a serialization boundary (a Server Component prop, a Server Action's return).
- `map<T, E, U>(result: Result<T, E>, fn: (value: T) => U): Result<U, E>` — Transform the success value; a failure passes through unchanged.
- `mapErr<T, E, F>(result: Result<T, E>, fn: (error: E) => F): Result<T, F>` — Transform the error; a success passes through unchanged. The failure's details are kept.
- `match<T>(value: T): Match<T, never>` — Start an exhaustive match over a literal union or a discriminated union:
- `interface Match<Remaining, Out>` — A pattern match in progress (see match). Remaining is what no .with() has handled yet; Out is the union of the handlers' results.
- `type Narrowed<T, P> = conditional` — The members of T that pattern P can match, narrowed by it.
- `interface NonExhaustiveMatch<Remaining>` — The type of .exhaustive when cases remain: not callable, and its one property names what is still unhandled, so the compile error says which case is missing.
- `ok(): Ok<undefined>` — A success with no value (Ok<undefined>).
- `interface Ok<T>` — A success: ok is true and value is the result.
- `type Pattern<T> = conditional` — What .with() accepts for a value of type T: a literal (for a literal union), or an object whose listed keys must equal the given literals (for a discriminated union — { type: "circle" }). Matching is shallow and uses === (with NaN equal to itself).
- `type Result<T, E> = Ok<T> | Err<E>` — Either a success (Ok) or a failure (Err). Narrow on .ok.
- `tryAsync<T, E>(fn: () => T | PromiseLike<T>, mapError?: (thrown: unknown) => E): Promise<Result<Awaited<T>, E>>` — Run a throwing (or rejecting) async call and capture the outcome as a Result.
- `trySync<T, E>(fn: () => T, mapError?: (thrown: unknown) => E): Result<T, E>` — Run a throwing synchronous call and capture the outcome as a Result.
- `unwrapOr<T, E, U>(result: Result<T, E>, fallback: U): T | U` — The success value, or fallback for a failure.

### `denext/signals`

- `action<A, R>(fn: (...args: A) => R): (...args: A) => R` — Wrap fn so each call is batched and reads nothing reactively (@preact/signals-core's action).
- `batch<T>(fn: () => T): T` — Apply several writes as one change: effects and re-renders run once, when the outermost batch ends.
- `computed<T>(fn: () => T): ReadonlySignal<T>` — A signal derived from other signals: fn re-runs (lazily, when read) after one it read changed.
- `effect(fn: () => unknown): EffectDispose` — Run fn now and again after any signal it read changes. fn may return a cleanup, run before the next run and on dispose.
- `type EffectDispose = parenthesized & object` — The function effect returns: disposes the effect (also using-disposable).
- `For<T>(props: ForProps<T>): VNode` — Render children for each item of each, or fallback when it is empty (@preact/signals/utils).
- `interface ForProps<T>` — Props of For.
- `interface ReadonlySignal<T>` — A signal that can be read but not written.
- `Show<T>(props: ShowProps<T>): VNode` — Render children while when is truthy, else fallback (@preact/signals/utils).
- `interface ShowProps<T>` — Props of Show.
- `signal<T>(value: T): Signal<T>` — Create a signal.
- `class Signal<T>` — A reactive value. Read .value to use it (subscribing the computed, effect or component that reads it), assign .value to change it. peek() reads without subscribing.
- `untracked<T>(fn: () => T): T` — Run fn without subscribing to the signals it reads.
- `useComputed<T>(fn: () => T): ReadonlySignal<T>` — A computed signal owned by the component; fn is always the latest render's.
- `useLiveSignal<T>(value: T): ReadonlySignal<T>` — A signal that follows value (a prop): updated whenever the component renders with a new one.
- `useSignal<T>(value: T): Signal<T>` — A signal owned by the component (created once, kept across renders).
- `useSignalEffect(fn: () => unknown): void` — An effect owned by the component: started after mount, disposed on unmount; fn is always the latest render's.

### `denext/prisma-adapter`

- `type AdapterError = MappedError & object` — A MappedError plus the driver's own code and message.
- `type ArgScalarType = string | int | bigint | float | decimal | boolean | enum | uuid | json | datetime | bytes | unknown` — The scalar type Prisma declares for a query argument.
- `interface ArgType` — What Prisma knows about a query argument: its scalar type, native type and arity.
- `type ColumnType = indexedAccess` — One of ColumnTypeEnum's values.
- `ColumnTypeEnum: object` — Prisma's ColumnTypeEnum: the type tag a result column reports for each value.
- `interface ConnectionInfo` — What Prisma learns about the connection.
- `interface DenoSqlClient` — A Deno.SQL client (or one of its reserved connections).
- `denoSqlHasColumns(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether this runtime's Deno.SQL reports result-set column metadata (result.columns), which the Prisma adapter needs: denext's Deno runtime 3.0.0-rc.1 and later. Probes an in-memory SQLite database, so it needs no permission and touches no file.
- `interface DenoSqlOptions` — The options new Deno.SQL(url, options) takes that the adapter sets.
- `class DriverAdapterError` — The error an adapter throws so Prisma reports a typed database error instead of a generic one. Prisma recognizes it by name and cause (no instanceof), so this class needs no import from Prisma.
- `type ErrorConstraint = object | object | object` — A constraint a database error names (fields, an index, or a foreign key).
- `type IsolationLevel = READ UNCOMMITTED | READ COMMITTED | REPEATABLE READ | SNAPSHOT | SERIALIZABLE` — The transaction isolation levels Prisma may ask for.
- `type MappedError = object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object | object` — A database error in the form Prisma turns into its own P20xx errors. Each kind is one Prisma knows; postgres / sqlite carry an error it has no dedicated kind for.
- `postgresConnection(url: string, schemaOption: string | undefined): object` — A Postgres URL with Prisma's own parameters read into Deno.SQL options and removed, as PrismaDenoSql does before it connects. schema becomes the search_path, connection_limit the pool's max, connect_timeout (or pool_timeout) the connectionTimeout, and pgbouncer=true turns prepared statements off; Prisma-only parameters a server would refuse (socket_timeout, statement_cache_size, sslaccept, …) are dropped. Use it to open a Deno.SQL client of your own from a Prisma DATABASE_URL.
- `class PrismaDenoSql` — The Prisma driver adapter factory over Deno.SQL, for Postgres and SQLite. Pass it to new PrismaClient({ adapter }).
- `interface PrismaDenoSqlOptions` — Options of PrismaDenoSql.
- `type Provider = mysql | postgres | sqlite | sqlserver` — The databases a Prisma driver adapter may speak to.
- `interface SqlColumn` — A result column as Deno.SQL describes it (both drivers' fields; see Deno.SQLColumn).
- `interface SqlDriverAdapter` — A connected driver adapter.
- `interface SqlMigrationAwareDriverAdapterFactory` — The factory new PrismaClient({ adapter }) takes.
- `interface SqlQuery` — A query Prisma sends: SQL text with positional parameters and their types.
- `interface SqlQueryable` — Something that runs queries: an adapter or one of its transactions.
- `interface SqlRequest<T>` — A Deno.SQL query: awaited for its rows, or switched to another row form first.
- `interface SqlResultSet` — A query's result, in the shape Prisma's query engine reads.
- `interface SqlRows<T>` — Rows plus what the database reported about them.
- `type TimestampFormat = iso8601 | unixepoch-ms` — How a DateTime argument is stored.
- `interface Transaction` — An open transaction. Prisma sends COMMIT / ROLLBACK itself, then calls commit() / rollback().

### `denext/jsx-directives`

- `interface ClientDirectives<Placeholder>` — The client:* directive props: a Flight route's island hydration markers, and in SPA mode the deferred mount of a code-split component. The build strips every client:* key before it reaches the component or the DOM; they are authoring markers, not real props.

### `denext/cli/command`

- `interface CommandContext` — The parsed invocation handed to a command's CommandSpec.run.
- `interface CommandLocks` — The locks a CommandSpec takes for one invocation — Cargo's build-dir / artifact-dir split over a denext project. Output paths are relative to projectDir.
- `class CommandRegistry` — A registry of commands with parsing, dispatch, and help rendering.
- `interface CommandSpec` — A first-class denext CLI verb.
- `interface FlagSpec` — A declarative flag on a CommandSpec (or a global flag).
- `type FlagType = boolean | string | number` — The value kind a flag carries. A boolean flag is a bare presence switch.
- `GLOBAL_FLAGS: typeOperator` — The global flags every command accepts, as data (drives parsing + help).
- `interface GlobalFlags` — Global flags recognized on every command, parsed out before command flags.
- `type ParseOutcome = object | object | object | object` — The outcome of parsing an argv against the registry.
- `plainText(text: string): string` — text with every control character removed — C0 (\x00–\x1f), DEL and C1 (\x7f–\x9f). A verb name or summary is project content on its way to the terminal: ESC opens every ANSI/OSC sequence (cursor moves, line clears, title changes, hyperlinks), and removing the control bytes disarms them all while keeping the words.
- `interface PositionalSpec` — A declarative positional argument on a CommandSpec.
- `interface ProjectVerb` — One verb a project contributes, as CommandRegistry.formatHelp lists it.
- `suggest(input: string, candidates: typeOperator): string | undefined` — The closest name in candidates to input within a small edit-distance threshold (scaled to the input length), or undefined when nothing is close — powering "did you mean" hints for both unknown verbs and unknown flags.
- `VERB_NAME: RegExp` — A project CLI verb name: lowercase, digits and dashes, starting with a letter. The grammar denext.config.ts's commands: validation enforces (src/server/config-validate.ts), and what the help cache accepts back from disk.
- `verbIndex(argv: typeOperator): number` — Index of the first bare token in argv — the verb — or -1 when there is none. The separate value of a valued global flag (--cwd <dir>) is skipped, not taken as the verb.

### `denext/plugin-kit`

- `interface ApiDefinition` — What an endpoint declares: its schemas, error codes, and per-method body cap.
- `apiDefinitionOf(handler: unknown): ApiRouteMeta | undefined` — The definition + middleware attached to a defineApi handler, or undefined for a plain function. The seam handleApi reads (body cap, error redaction) and the accessor an OpenAPI/docs plugin uses to describe an app's endpoints.
- `interface ApiRouteMeta` — The metadata attached to a defineApi handler (what handleApi and plugins read).
- `interface AppCss` — Result of buildAppCss: everything needed by server + client + docs.
- `interface AuthorizedTapOptions<T>` — Options for tapChannelAuthorized.
- `bufferedRequest(request: Request, body: Uint8Array): Request` — Rebuild a request from already-buffered body bytes (headers/method preserved).
- `buildAppCss(opts: object): Promise<AppCss | null>` — Build the whole project's CSS assets: scan for .css files, transform each, write a JS shim per file, and emit a merged deno config (framework + project imports normalized to absolute, plus the CSS redirects) so the module loader — and deno bundle (via CssAssets.importMap) — can resolve every .css import.
- `buildNextCompatModules(options: BuildNextCompatModulesOptions): Promise<Map<string, string>>` — Build react→denext-rewritten SSR bundles for a set of route source modules, each RE-EXPORTING the source module's shape (default + named exports: metadata/generateMetadata/segment-config/…) rather than wrapping it in a render(). The main SSR loader (createNextCompatServerLoader) returns these instead of the raw source, so the whole route subtree — including npm React libraries imported inside it — runs on denext's single React.
- `interface BuildNextCompatModulesOptions` — Options for buildNextCompatModules.
- `bundleRoutes(routeEntries: Array<object>, opts: BundleOptions): Promise<MultiBundleOutput>` — Bundle several browser entries in a **single** code-split pass, so any module imported by more than one entry — chiefly the denext client runtime, which every route entry imports — is hoisted into one shared chunk they all reference (downloaded once, cached across client navigations) instead of being inlined into each entry. Contrast bundleRoute, which bundles one route in isolation and therefore cannot share a chunk with its siblings.
- `cappedBody(request: Request, maxBytes: number): Request` — request with its body wrapped so that reading past maxBytes errors the stream (the consumer — formData(), json(), a multipart parser — then throws). For streaming consumers that cannot use readCappedBody; a declared content-length over the cap is refused up front.
- `captureRequestContext(init?: object): (fn: () => T) => T` — Capture the current request so its session can be read again later, outside it — what a plugin holding a long-lived connection (a WebSocket it upgraded) uses to re-check who is on the other end: the returned function runs fn in a fresh request context for a copy of this request (its URL, its headers — cookies included — and its client address, with the app's proxy trust and limit policy), so auth(), cookies() and clientIpForLimits() answer as they did for the original. Capture BEFORE Deno.upgradeWebSocket, which consumes the request. Outside a request the function runs fn as it is.
- `interface Channel<T>` — A channel on the server.
- `class ChannelAccessError` — Why tapChannelAuthorized refused a subscriber.
- `interface ChannelContext` — The subscriber's identity handed to authorize (the Live connection context).
- `interface ChannelTapHandlers<T>` — What tapChannel reports.
- `interface CommandContext` — The parsed invocation handed to a command's CommandSpec.run.
- `interface CommandSpec` — A first-class denext CLI verb.
- `compareSpecificity(a: Segment[], b: Segment[]): number` — Order two patterns by specificity the way Next.js does: compare segment by segment from the left, and at the first position that differs the more specific kind wins (static > dynamic > catch-all > optional catch-all). A pattern that has run out of segments (its catch-all consumed the rest) ranks below one that still has a concrete segment there. Returns negative when a should be tried first.
- `interface CompatReactNativeOptions` — React Native mode (reactNative in the config) for the App Router's compat bundles: what each of the server, Flight and client-route bundles adds (see react-native-app-router.ts reactNativeCompatOptions). Absent when reactNative is off, which leaves every bundle exactly as it is without it.
- `compileMdxSource(path: string, source: string, opts?: MdxBuildOptions): Promise<string>` — Compile one MDX/Markdown source to a JS module string (React automatic runtime, jsxImportSource: "react" → aliased to denext downstream). With no opts this is the baseline plain-MDX/CommonMark path; when the app configures mdx in denext.config.ts, its unified remark/rehype/recma plugin lists (e.g. Codehike, GFM) are forwarded verbatim to MDX's compile. Exported for unit testing the plugin wiring.
- `type Component<P> = (props: P & object) => VNode | Promise<VNode>` — A component is a function that receives props and returns a renderable node.
- `createNextCompatServerLoader(base: ModuleLoader, opts: NextCompatServerLoaderOptions): ModuleLoader` — Wrap a base ModuleLoader so route source modules that have a react→denext rewritten server bundle load from that bundle instead of source (a keyed ref resolves to the module's namespace inside the single server bundle).
- `interface DenextConfig` — Project configuration exported from denext.config.{ts,js} (as default or named).
- `interface DenextPlugin` — A denext plugin. Declared in denext.config.ts as plugins: [myPlugin()]; its setup runs once per process, before the first route scan.
- `DEPLOY_MANIFEST_FILE: deploy-manifest.json` — The manifest's file name, under the build directory (.denext/deploy-manifest.json).
- `DEPLOY_MANIFEST_VERSION: 1` — The manifest format version DeployManifest.version carries.
- `interface DeployAdapter` — A deploy adapter: prepare writes a target's files from the manifest, and the optional deploy pushes them with the target's own CLI. Declare one in denext.config.ts as deploy: { adapter: fly({ app: "my-app" }) }, or contribute one from a plugin with addDeployAdapter.
- `interface DeployAssetGroup` — One directory of files the server serves as they are, with the Cache-Control it sends.
- `interface DeployCache` — The data / page (ISR) cache store the config chooses.
- `interface DeployCompile` — What denext build --compile produced.
- `interface DeployContext` — What an adapter's prepare and deploy receive.
- `interface DeployEnvVar` — An environment variable the app reads.
- `interface DeployImages` — The built-in image optimizer.
- `interface DeployJob` — A job under jobs/.
- `interface DeployManifest` — The deploy manifest denext build writes to .denext/deploy-manifest.json.
- `interface DeployNetPermissions` — DeployPermissions.net: the outbound hosts and the listen addresses.
- `interface DeployPermissions` — The Deno permissions the production server runs with.
- `interface DeployRoute` — One route of the app, classified for a host.
- `type DeployRouteKind = static | isr | dynamic | route-handler | middleware` — How a route is served, as a host needs to know it: - "static" — rendered once (at build or on the first request) and the same for everyone: denext export writes it, and a CDN may cache it until the next deploy. - "isr" — cached and re-rendered in the background every DeployRoute.revalidate seconds (export const revalidate = N): needs the server. - "dynamic" — rendered per request (dynamic = "force-dynamic", a request API such as cookies(), or a dynamic segment with no generateStaticParams): needs the server. - "route-handler" — a route.ts (or a metadata route such as sitemap.ts): needs the server. - "middleware" — the root middleware.ts / proxy.ts: runs before every matched request.
- `interface DeployRunOptions` — Options for DeployContext.run.
- `interface DeploySchedule` — One scheduled run: a job and the cron expression (UTC, POSIX weekdays) that fires it.
- `interface DeployServer` — How the production server is started.
- `interface DeployService` — A supervised service under services/, started with the server.
- `interface DeployWriteOptions` — Where DeployContext.writeFile writes.
- `edgeFunctionSource(name: string): string` — An Edge Function in Supabase's shape, for backend({ functions }) from @denext/backend: what denext generate function <name> and denext functions new <name> write.
- `interface EmittedAsset` — A generated file a build step publishes with PluginBuildContext.emitFile.
- `enableFastRefresh(): void` — Install the family-identity check and hook-signature guard into the reconciler. Idempotent; called once by the dev route entry before its first render. A no-op in production (this module is never imported there).
- `extractRouteCss(routeFiles: string[], assets: AppCss): Promise<string>` — Extract the CSS a single route needs: crawl the route's source files, keep the transformed CSS for those reachable .css files (in path order), and concatenate. Returns "" when the route pulls in no CSS.
- `fromBase64Url(s: string): Uint8Array` — Decode URL-safe base64 (no padding) back to bytes. Shared with the Remix session compat.
- `type GenerateBundleHook = parenthesized | object` — A generateBundle hook: a function, or Rollup's { handler } object form.
- `hmacSign(payload: string, secret: string, domain?: unknown): Promise<string>` — HMAC-SHA256 sign payload with secret, returned URL-safe base64. domain separates the token spaces that share one secret (the denext session cookie, a Remix cookie session): a token minted for one can never verify as the other.
- `hmacVerify(payload: string, sig: string, secrets: string[], domain?: unknown): Promise<boolean>` — Verify payload against sig for any of secrets (constant-time via subtle.verify).
- `hydrateRoot(container: Element, vnode: VNode, options?: RootOptions): Root` — Hydrate vnode against server-rendered markup already in container.
- `interface I18nConfig` — Internationalization configuration.
- `matchSegments(pattern: Segment[], pathname: string): RouteParams | null` — Attempt to match a request pathname against a parsed pattern. Returns extracted params on success, or null if the pattern doesn't match.
- `interface MdxBuildOptions` — MDX build options threaded from denext.config.ts (mdx). Mirrors the compile-time subset of the app's MDX config; typed loosely so this build module stays decoupled from the server config types. Plugin lists are unified PluggableLists.
- `interface NextCompatServerLoaderOptions` — Options for createNextCompatServerLoader.
- `interface OriginCheckOptions` — What verifyOrigin needs from the app config.
- `class PageCache` — The rendered-page store for Incremental Static Regeneration. A thin façade over the active CacheStore: the prod server consults it before rendering and populates it afterward for cacheable routes. Injecting a shared store via setCacheStore makes ISR work across replicas transparently (replicas of one build share its build id).
- `parsePattern(pattern: string): Segment[]` — Parse a route pattern like "blog/[slug]" into an ordered segment list.
- `peelLocale(pathname: string, i18n: I18nConfig | undefined, host?: string): PeeledLocale` — Peel a leading locale segment off pathname. If the first path segment is a configured locale it is stripped and returned; otherwise the default locale is used and the pathname is returned unchanged.
- `platformClientRedirects(projectDir: string, config: DenextConfig | null | undefined, platform?: Platform): Promise<Record<string, string>>` — The redirects that make a plugin's client bundle resolve the app's [platform-specific files](https://denext.dev/docs/platform-files) (Button.web.tsx) as the server render does: pass them to bundleRoutes' redirects (with projectDir), which follows them through relative imports and the app's import-map aliases alike. Empty when the app has no platform files or turned them off.
- `interface PluginBuildContext` — Context passed to a PluginBuildStep.
- `type PluginBuildStep = (context: PluginBuildContext) => void | Promise<void>` — A build-time step that emits the plugin's client bundles/assets into outDir, and publishes generated files at the site root with PluginBuildContext.emitFile. Runs at denext build and at denext export (App Router, SPA and Pages Router alike).
- `interface PluginContext` — The seams a plugin's DenextPlugin.setup may extend.
- `type PluginDeployAssets = () => typeOperator | Promise<typeOperator>` — A plugin's asset groups for the deploy manifest (PluginContext.addDeployAssets): files it serves as they are, each group with the Cache-Control the plugin sends for them.
- `type PluginDeployRoutes = () => typeOperator | Promise<typeOperator>` — A plugin's routes for the deploy manifest (PluginContext.addDeployRoutes).
- `type PluginMode = dev | build | prod | export` — Where denext is running when a plugin's DenextPlugin.setup fires.
- `interface PluginPrepareContext` — Context passed to a PluginPrepareStep (and the base of a build step's).
- `type PluginPrepareStep = (context: PluginPrepareContext) => void | Promise<void>` — A step that prepares generated inputs (typed accessors, a data artifact) BEFORE the app is bundled or served — the seam a plugin uses to generate code the app then imports.
