Unlike a PluginBuildStep (which runs only at denext build / export), a prepare step runs in **both** lifecycles: once at denext build and once at denext dev startup, and again during dev whenever a file under its PrepareStepOptions.watch globs changes — so its generated output stays live as you edit. Its PluginPrepareContext is a build step's context without the emit seam: a prepare step generates inputs, not published output.
- `type PluginRequestHandler = (request: Request) => Response | null | undefined | Promise<Response | null | undefined>` — Claim and handle a request the core router did not match. Return a Response to serve it, or null/undefined to pass (letting denext fall through to static assets and the 404). Runs AFTER App-Router page/API matching, so core routes always win.
- `type PluginTeardown = () => void | Promise<void>` — A disposer that releases resources a plugin opened in DenextPlugin.setup (watchers, connections, timers). Registered with PluginContext.addTeardown and run — most-recently-registered first — when the server drains.
- `interface PrepareStepOptions` — Options for PluginContext.addPrepareStep.
- `readCappedBody(request: Request, maxBytes: number, idleMs?: number): Promise<Uint8Array | TOO_LARGE | STALLED>` — Read a request body into memory, refusing anything over maxBytes (hard-caps even a chunked body with no Content-Length) and aborting a body that stalls for longer than idleMs. Returns the bytes, TOO_LARGE, or STALLED.
- `registerFamily(type: unknown, id: string): void` — Register a component type under a stable family id (e.g. moduleUrl#Export). Re-registering the same id with a new function ref binds that ref to the same family and marks it current — the mechanism that lets an edited module's fresh references reconcile onto existing fibers.
- `remixCodegen` — The Remix route-module codegen denext migrate --from remix uses, as a namespace: the swc-based split of a route module into a "use client" component + a server data module (remixCodegen.analyzeModule analyzeModule) and the generated denext wrappers (remixCodegen.pageWrapperSource pageWrapperSource and siblings). A router plugin (@denext/react-router) uses it to generate the same wrappers into .denext/ for an app whose sources stay untouched.
- `revalidatePath(path: string, _type?: layout | page): Promise<void>` — Invalidate the cached render(s) of path. As with revalidateTag, await the returned promise when using an async store. Inside a Server Action the client that called it also re-renders its current route.
- `revalidateTag(tag: string, profile?: string | CacheLifeProfile): Promise<void>` — Invalidate every cached data entry and page carrying tag.
- `type RouteParams = Record<string, string | string[]>` — Extracted dynamic route parameters, keyed by segment name. A [slug] segment yields a string; a [...rest] / [[...rest]] catch-all yields the remaining parts as a string[] (Next.js's shape — params.rest.join("/") for the path form).
- `type RouteSynthesizer = (manifest: RouteManifest) => void | Promise<void>` — A hook run over the scanned manifest before it is returned. May add, remove, or adjust routes — the extension point behind synthesized/derived routes. May be async (e.g. a plugin scanning its own route tree off disk).
- `interface Segment` — A single parsed route pattern segment.
- `specificity(pattern: Segment[]): number` — Specificity score for ordering routes: more specific (static) patterns should be tried before less specific (dynamic/catch-all) ones. Higher wins. Position-blind (a sum) — prefer compareSpecificity for ordering.
- `STALLED: Symbol` — Sentinel returned by readCappedBody when the body stalls (idle).
- `interface TailwindConfig` — Tailwind CSS integration. When set, denext compiles input (which contains the raw @import "tailwindcss"; directives) into output using the Tailwind v4 standalone binary — which denext downloads and manages itself — before its own CSS pipeline runs. The output file is what your layout imports.
- `tapChannel<T>(channel: Channel<T> | string, key: string, handlers: ChannelTapHandlers<T>): () => void` — Observe a channel's publishes on the SERVER: every payload published to key on any instance — through the installed transport, decoded, in seq order per instance — until the returned disposer runs. The seam a plugin uses to bridge channel pushes into another protocol (a GraphQL subscription in @denext/graphql, an SSE stream, a queue) without a second event bus. Survives setChannelTransport (re-binds to the new transport).
- `tapChannelAuthorized<T>(channel: Channel<T> | string, key: string, options: AuthorizedTapOptions<T>): Promise<() => void>` — Subscribe a viewer to one key of a channel on the server, behind the channel's authorize — the same gate, context and key the Live socket applies to a useChannel subscriber. Call it inside the viewer's request (a resolver, a route handler): authorize(ctx, key) runs there with ctx = { origin, url, cookie, peerId } from that request, and again, lazily, on the first payload after the channel's re-authorization TTL, in a copy of that request's context.
- `toBase64Url(bytes: Uint8Array): string` — Encode bytes as URL-safe base64 (no padding). Shared with the Remix session compat.
- `TOO_LARGE: Symbol` — Sentinel returned by readCappedBody when the body exceeds the cap.
- `verifyOrigin(request: Request, options: OriginCheckOptions): boolean` — Is this request from the app's own origin (or an explicitly allowed one)?
- `interface ViteEmittedFile` — A Rollup emitFile argument (only type: "asset" with a fileName is supported).
- `interface ViteEmitterBuildContext` — The parts of a plugin build step's context the emitter uses (a subset of PluginBuildContext).
- `interface ViteEmitterContext` — The plugin context (this) the hook runs with: the parts of Rollup's an emitter uses.
- `interface ViteEmitterDenextPlugin` — The denext plugin viteEmitterPlugin returns (assignable to DenextPlugin).
- `viteEmitterPlugin(vitePlugin: VitePluginLike): ViteEmitterDenextPlugin` — Wrap a Vite plugin whose generateBundle emits files (this.emitFile({ type: "asset", fileName, source })) as a denext plugin: the hook runs as a build step at denext build and denext export, and each file it emits is published at the site root.
- `interface ViteEmitterSetupContext` — The setup context viteEmitterPlugin's plugin uses (a subset of PluginContext).
- `interface VitePluginLike` — The slice of a Vite plugin viteEmitterPlugin runs.
- `interface VNode` — A single virtual DOM node.
- `type VNodeChild = VNode | string | number | bigint | boolean | null | undefined` — Anything that can appear as a child in JSX.
- `type VNodeChildren = VNodeChild | VNodeChild[]` — One child or an array of children, as accepted by JSX.
- `type VNodeType = string | Component<any> | FRAGMENT` — The type field of a VNode: an intrinsic tag name, a component fn, or a fragment marker.
- `interface VProps` — Props passed to a virtual node. children is normalized separately.

### `denext/plugin-kit/vite-emitter`

- `type GenerateBundleHook = parenthesized | object` — A generateBundle hook: a function, or Rollup's { handler } object form.
- `interface ViteEmittedFile` — A Rollup emitFile argument (only type: "asset" with a fileName is supported).
- `interface ViteEmitterBuildContext` — The parts of a plugin build step's context the emitter uses (a subset of PluginBuildContext).
- `interface ViteEmitterContext` — The plugin context (this) the hook runs with: the parts of Rollup's an emitter uses.
- `interface ViteEmitterDenextPlugin` — The denext plugin viteEmitterPlugin returns (assignable to DenextPlugin).
- `viteEmitterPlugin(vitePlugin: VitePluginLike): ViteEmitterDenextPlugin` — Wrap a Vite plugin whose generateBundle emits files (this.emitFile({ type: "asset", fileName, source })) as a denext plugin: the hook runs as a build step at denext build and denext export, and each file it emits is published at the site root.
- `interface ViteEmitterSetupContext` — The setup context viteEmitterPlugin's plugin uses (a subset of PluginContext).
- `interface VitePluginLike` — The slice of a Vite plugin viteEmitterPlugin runs.

### `denext/ui-kit`

- `type BadgeTone = ok | todo | warn | fail | info` — How a Badge reads. The CSS colours each one; a badge with no tone stays grey.
- `Control(attrs: ControlAttrs): VNode` — One control. Every widget in render.ts bottoms out here, so escaping, the disabled flag and the element vocabulary are decided exactly once.
- `interface ControlAttrs` — One <input>, <select> or <textarea>.
- `decode(spec: WidgetSpec, entries: typeOperator, prefix?: string): unknown` — Parse a posted body back into the config value its widget stands for.
- `encode(spec: WidgetSpec, value: unknown, prefix?: string): FormEntry[]` — Render a config value as the flat fields its widget posts.
- `Field(props: FieldProps): VNode` — A control wrapped in its label, help text and validation message.
- `interface FieldProps` — The label, help text and validation message around one control (Field).
- `interface FormEntry` — One posted field.
- `FormField(props: FormFieldProps): VNode` — A widget and everything under it, with the CSRF field the row buttons need: the form body of a form that edits one key.
- `interface FormFieldProps` — FormField's props: one widget, the value it holds, and the render context.
- `FormFields(props: FormFieldsProps): VNode` — Several widgets as one form body, behind a single CSRF field.
- `interface FormFieldsProps` — FormFields's props: the widgets in render order, and the render context.
- `OpButton(props: OpButtonOptions): VNode` — A real submit button carrying one list operation — the whole list editor works with JavaScript disabled, and ui.js upgrades the same submit to a fragment swap.
- `interface OpButtonOptions` — One row-operation button (↑, ↓, ✕, + Add).
- `interface RawHtml` — A pre-escaped HTML fragment: Raw inserts it into a component tree verbatim.
- `interface RenderContext` — What the renderer is told beyond the spec and the value.
- `renderView(node: VNodeChildren): RawHtml` — Render a component view to a pre-escaped fragment — synchronously, with no hydration markers and no client code. The result nests inside another tree through Raw without being escaped a second time. A throwing component throws out of this call (the UI server answers 500), and so does an async component: a view must be synchronous.
- `interface SchemaNode` — The subset of JSON Schema the config schema actually uses, plus denext's x-denext hints.
- `Widget(props: WidgetProps): VNode` — One widget and everything under it, dispatched to its kind's component — the recursive half of the form, without the CSRF field (FormField adds it).
- `interface WidgetBranch` — One alternative shape of a union field, behind the discriminator picker.
- `interface WidgetField` — One field of a multi-widget form: its widget, and the value to render it holding.
- `widgetFor(node: SchemaNode, path: typeOperator, required: boolean): WidgetSpec` — The widget for one schema node — the first matching rule of the table above wins.
- `type WidgetKind = text | textarea | number | toggle | select | segmented | multi-select | chips | list-of-forms | map | union | group | code` — Every control the config editor can render.
- `interface WidgetOption` — One choice of a select, segmented control or checkbox group.
- `type WidgetProps = object` — What every widget component is handed (Widget's props).
- `interface WidgetSpec` — A resolved widget: what to render at one path, and everything the renderer needs.

### `denext/expo/apple-authentication`

- `addRevokeListener(_listener: () => void): Subscription` — Listen for the user revoking the app's access: never reported here.
- `AppleAuthenticationButton(props: AppleAuthenticationButtonProps): VNode | null` — A "Sign in with Apple" button in Apple's styles: a <button> with the Apple logo and the label for buttonType. Like Expo's, it renders nothing where Sign in with Apple cannot run (anywhere but the iOS shell); start signInAsync from onPress.
- `type AppleAuthenticationButtonProps = object` — AppleAuthenticationButton props.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationButtonStyle` — The button's look.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationButtonType` — The button's label.
- `type AppleAuthenticationCredential = object` — A signed-in user's credential.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationCredentialState` — Whether a user's Apple ID is still authorized for the app.
- `type AppleAuthenticationFullName = object` — The parts of a name.
- `type AppleAuthenticationFullNameFormatStyle = default | short | medium | long | abbreviated` — How formatFullName joins the parts.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationOperation` — The operation a request performs.
- `type AppleAuthenticationRefreshOptions = object` — Options for refreshAsync.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationScope` — What the sign-in asks for.
- `type AppleAuthenticationSignInOptions = object` — Options for signInAsync.
- `type AppleAuthenticationSignOutOptions = object` — Options for signOutAsync.
- `enum AppleAuthenticationUserDetectionStatus` — Apple's guess whether the user is a real person.
- `formatFullName(fullName: AppleAuthenticationFullName, formatStyle?: AppleAuthenticationFullNameFormatStyle): string` — A name's parts joined for display (short and abbreviated give the given name alone).
- `getCredentialStateAsync(_user: string): Promise<AppleAuthenticationCredentialState>` — A user's credential state: not provided (check it server-side with Apple's REST API).
- `isAvailableAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether Sign in with Apple can run: in the iOS shell with the social-login plugin.
- `refreshAsync(_options: AppleAuthenticationRefreshOptions): Promise<AppleAuthenticationCredential>` — Refresh a credential: not provided (the plugin signs in only).
- `signInAsync(options?: AppleAuthenticationSignInOptions): Promise<AppleAuthenticationCredential>` — Show the Sign in with Apple sheet.
- `signOutAsync(_options: AppleAuthenticationSignOutOptions): Promise<AppleAuthenticationCredential>` — Sign out: not provided (Apple has no sign-out; forget the session on your side).
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.

### `denext/expo/application`

- `applicationId: string | null` — The bundle id (iOS) or application id (Android), or null.
- `interface ApplicationInfo` — The four constants, as applicationInfoAsync reports them.
- `applicationInfoAsync(): Promise<ApplicationInfo>` — The constants once the shell's @capacitor/app has answered (denext only; Expo's are ready synchronously). Resolves at once on the web.
- `applicationName: string | null` — The app's human-readable name (CFBundleDisplayName / the Android label), or null.
- `enum ApplicationReleaseType` — How an iOS build was distributed.
- `getAndroidId(): string` — The Android id (Settings.Secure.ANDROID_ID, per app-signing key, user and device), from @capacitor/device's getId(). Android only.
- `getInstallationTimeAsync(): Promise<Date>` — When the app was installed. No Capacitor plugin reports it.
- `getInstallReferrerAsync(): Promise<string>` — The Play install referrer. No Capacitor plugin reads it.
- `getIosApplicationReleaseTypeAsync(): Promise<ApplicationReleaseType>` — How the iOS build was distributed: SIMULATOR in a simulator (from @capacitor/device), else UNKNOWN (the provisioning profile is not readable from the web view).
- `getIosIdForVendorAsync(): Promise<string | null>` — The iOS identifierForVendor, from @capacitor/device's getId().
- `getIosPushNotificationServiceEnvironmentAsync(): Promise<PushNotificationServiceEnvironment>` — The APNs environment of the iOS build. Not readable from the web view.
- `getLastUpdateTimeAsync(): Promise<Date>` — When the app was last updated. No Capacitor plugin reports it.
- `nativeApplicationVersion: string | null` — The version string (CFBundleShortVersionString / versionName), or null.
- `nativeBuildVersion: string | null` — The build (CFBundleVersion / versionCode), or null.
- `type PushNotificationServiceEnvironment = development | production | null` — The APNs environment of an iOS build.
- `reloadApplicationInfoForTesting(): Promise<ApplicationInfo>` — Re-read the constants for the current platform: the Expo config, then the native plugins. For tests that switch between a faked shell and the web.

### `denext/expo/audio`

- `type AudioLockScreenOptions = object` — Which lock-screen controls to show (expo-audio's shape).
- `type AudioMetadata = object` — What the lock screen shows for a player (expo-audio's shape).
- `type AudioMode = object` — The audio mode (only shouldPlayInBackground and interruptionMode change anything here).
- `AudioModule: NativeAudioModule` — expo-audio's native module object (AudioModule), for code that constructs the classes through it (new AudioModule.AudioRecorder(options)) or calls its functions. The classes and the session and permission calls are the ones this module exports; preloading and the notification permission are not provided and reject with a nativeOnly error.
- `class AudioPlayer` — An audio player over an HTMLAudioElement (created on first use).
- `interface AudioPlayerOptions` — Options for a player.
- `class AudioPlaylist` — The type of expo-audio's playlist. Playlists are not provided here (useAudioPlaylist and createAudioPlaylist are not exported): constructing this stand-in throws. Queue AudioPlayers instead.
- `type AudioPlaylistLoopMode = none | single | all` — How a playlist repeats: not at all, the current track, or the whole list.
- `enum AudioQuality` — iOS audio quality (accepted, ignored).
- `class AudioRecorder` — An audio recorder over MediaRecorder.
- `type AudioSource = string | object | null` — An audio source: a URL, { uri }, or null.
- `interface AudioStatus` — A player's status.
- `class AudioStream` — The type of expo-audio's raw PCM input stream. Streams are not provided here (useAudioStream is not exported): constructing this stand-in throws. Record with AudioRecorder, or read the microphone through Web Audio.
- `createAudioPlayer(source?: AudioSource, options?: AudioPlayerOptions): AudioPlayer` — A player not tied to a component (call remove() when done).
- `getRecordingPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The microphone permission (the browser's).
- `type InterruptionMode = mixWithOthers | doNotMix | doNotMixPersistent | duckOthers` — How the app's audio meets other apps' audio.
- `class NativeAudioModule` — The type of expo-audio's native module (what requireNativeModule("ExpoAudio") returns). There is no native module on the web: constructing this stand-in throws. Use the package's functions and AudioPlayer / AudioRecorder instead.
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `interface RecorderState` — A recorder's state.
- `interface RecordingOptions` — Recording options (only web and isMeteringEnabled apply here).
- `RecordingPresets: object` — Expo's recording presets.
- `interface RecordingStatus` — A recording outcome, for the status listener.
- `requestRecordingPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — Ask for the microphone (a getUserMedia call, stopped at once).
- `setAudioModeAsync(mode: Partial<AudioMode>): Promise<void>` — Set the audio mode. shouldPlayInBackground and interruptionMode set the shell's audio session through denext/mobile's setAudioSession (denext mobile add background-audio; the iOS .playback category keeps audio playing in the background and with the phone locked); the other fields are accepted. On the web, a browser decides itself, so nothing changes. Lock-screen controls on iOS need a doNotMix mode, as in expo-audio.
- `setIsAudioActiveAsync(_active: boolean): Promise<void>` — Activate or deactivate the audio session: there is none on the web.
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `useAudioPlayer(source?: AudioSource, options?: AudioPlayerOptions): AudioPlayer` — A player for the component's lifetime (released on unmount; a new source replaces the current one).
- `useAudioPlayerStatus(player: AudioPlayer): AudioStatus` — The player's status, updated as it plays.
- `useAudioRecorder(options: RecordingOptions, statusListener?: (status: RecordingStatus) => void): AudioRecorder` — A recorder for the component's lifetime.
- `useAudioRecorderState(recorder: AudioRecorder, interval?: number): RecorderState` — The recorder's state, polled every interval ms.

### `denext/expo/auth-session`

- `class AccessTokenRequest` — An authorization-code exchange.
- `type AccessTokenRequestConfig = TokenRequestBase & object` — An authorization-code exchange's configuration.
- `class AuthError` — An error the authorization endpoint returned.
- `type AuthErrorConfig = ResponseErrorConfig & object` — An authorization error response's parameters (plus the returned state).
- `class AuthRequest` — One authorization request: its URL, PKCE verifier and state.
- `interface AuthRequestConfig` — An authorization request's configuration.
- `type AuthRequestPromptOptions = Omit<AuthSessionOpenOptions, windowFeatures> & object` — Options for AuthRequest.promptAsync.
- `interface AuthSessionRedirectUriOptions` — Options for makeRedirectUri.
- `type AuthSessionResult = object | object` — What the prompt resolves with.
- `enum CodeChallengeMethod` — The PKCE challenge method.
- `interface DiscoveryDocument` — An OAuth / OIDC provider's endpoints.
- `dismiss(): void` — Close the open auth session, where the platform allows it.
- `exchangeCodeAsync(config: AccessTokenRequestConfig, discovery: Pick<DiscoveryDocument, tokenEndpoint>): Promise<TokenResponse>` — Exchange an authorization code for tokens (AccessTokenRequest).
- `fetchDiscoveryAsync(issuer: Issuer): Promise<DiscoveryDocument>` — Fetch issuer's OpenID configuration.
- `interface FetchRequest` — A requestAsync request.
- `fetchUserInfoAsync(config: Pick<TokenResponse, accessToken>, discovery: Pick<DiscoveryDocument, userInfoEndpoint>): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>` — Fetch the signed-in user's claims.
- `getCurrentTimeInSeconds(): number` — The current time in whole seconds.
- `getDefaultReturnUrl(urlPath?: string, options?: object): string` — The default return URL (makeRedirectUri with path).
- `getRedirectUrl(path?: string): string` — The redirect URL for path on this app (makeRedirectUri).
- `enum GrantType` — The token endpoint grant types.
- `type Issuer = string` — An issuer URL.
- `type IssuerOrDiscovery = Issuer | DiscoveryDocument` — An issuer URL, or its discovery document.
- `issuerWithWellKnownUrl(issuer: Issuer): string` — The OpenID configuration URL of issuer.
- `loadAsync(config: AuthRequestConfig, issuerOrDiscovery: IssuerOrDiscovery): Promise<AuthRequest>` — Build an AuthRequest after resolving its discovery document.
- `makeRedirectUri(options?: AuthSessionRedirectUriOptions): string` — The redirect URI for an auth request: natively native when given, else <scheme>://<path>; on the web a URL on the page's origin (localhost with preferLocalhost).
- `enum Prompt` — The OpenID Connect prompt values.
- `type PromptMethod = (options?: AuthRequestPromptOptions) => Promise<AuthSessionResult>` — What useAuthRequestResult's prompt does.
- `refreshAsync(config: RefreshTokenRequestConfig, discovery: Pick<DiscoveryDocument, tokenEndpoint>): Promise<TokenResponse>` — Refresh an access token (RefreshTokenRequest).
- `class RefreshTokenRequest` — A refresh-token grant.
- `type RefreshTokenRequestConfig = TokenRequestBase & object` — A refresh's configuration.
- `class Request<T, B>` — The base of the token-family requests: a config, a body and performAsync.
- `requestAsync<T>(requestUrl: string, fetchRequest: FetchRequest): Promise<T>` — Expo's small fetch helper: send body as a form (POST) or a query string, and read the answer as JSON (for dataType: "json" or a JSON content type) or text.
- `resolveDiscoveryAsync(issuerOrDiscovery: IssuerOrDiscovery): Promise<DiscoveryDocument>` — A discovery document: fetched for an issuer URL, returned as is otherwise.
- `class ResponseError` — An OAuth error response: an authorization redirect's or a token endpoint's.
- `type ResponseErrorConfig = Record<string, string | undefined> & object` — An OAuth error response's parameters (error, error_description, …).
- `enum ResponseType` — The OAuth response type.
- `revokeAsync(config: RevokeTokenRequestConfig, discovery: Pick<DiscoveryDocument, revocationEndpoint>): Promise<boolean>` — Revoke a token (RevokeTokenRequest).
- `class RevokeTokenRequest` — A token revocation (RFC 7009).
- `type RevokeTokenRequestConfig = Partial<TokenRequestBase> & object` — A revocation's configuration.
- `class TokenError` — An error a token endpoint returned.
- `class TokenRequest<T>` — A token-endpoint request: its grant, client and body.
- `interface TokenRequestBase` — The fields every token call sends.
- `type TokenRequestConfig = TokenRequestBase` — A token request's configuration.
- `class TokenResponse` — A set of tokens.
- `interface TokenResponseConfig` — A token endpoint response.
- `enum TokenTypeHint` — Which token a revocation names.
- `useAuthRequest(config: AuthRequestConfig, discovery: DiscoveryDocument | null): tuple` — An AuthRequest for config, its latest result, and the prompt.
- `useAuthRequestResult(request: AuthRequest | null, discovery: DiscoveryDocument | null, customOptions?: AuthRequestPromptOptions): tuple` — The latest result of request and the prompt that produces it. customOptions are the defaults of every prompt (a provider's popup size, say).
- `useAutoDiscovery(issuerOrDiscovery: IssuerOrDiscovery): DiscoveryDocument | null` — Hook form of resolveDiscoveryAsync.
- `useLoadedAuthRequest(config: AuthRequestConfig, discovery: DiscoveryDocument | null, AuthRequestInstance: (config: AuthRequestConfig) => AuthRequest): AuthRequest | null` — An AuthRequestInstance (an AuthRequest or a subclass, like a provider's) for config, once its authorization URL is built for discovery; null until then. Rebuilt when the client, redirect, response type, PKCE, state, scopes, prompt or extra parameters change.

### `denext/expo/auth-session/providers/google`

- `discovery: DiscoveryDocument` — Google's OAuth / OpenID endpoints.
- `type GoogleAuthRequestConfig = AuthRequestConfig & object` — A Google request's configuration.
- `type GoogleAuthRequestHook = tuple` — What both hooks return: the loaded request, the latest response, and the prompt.
- `useAuthRequest(config?: Partial<GoogleAuthRequestConfig>, redirectUriOptions?: Partial<AuthSessionRedirectUriOptions>): GoogleAuthRequestHook` — A Google authorization request, its latest response, and the prompt. Inside the shell the code is exchanged for tokens once the prompt succeeds (see the module docs).
- `useIdTokenAuthRequest(config: Partial<GoogleAuthRequestConfig>, redirectUriOptions?: Partial<AuthSessionRedirectUriOptions>): GoogleAuthRequestHook` — A Google request for an ID token (for Firebase and your own backend): on the web it asks for id_token directly; in the shell it runs the code flow and the exchange returns it. Read it from response.params.id_token.

### `denext/expo/brightness`

- `addBrightnessListener(listener: (event: BrightnessEvent) => void): Subscription` — Call listener when the screen's brightness changes (iOS, as in Expo: with DenextBrightness from denext mobile add brightness; never elsewhere).
- `interface BrightnessEvent` — What a brightness listener receives.
- `enum BrightnessMode` — How the system sets the brightness (Android).
- `getBrightnessAsync(): Promise<number>` — The current brightness: the screen's (iOS) or the app window's (Android; the system's while the window follows it, as in Expo, or -1 without DenextBrightness).
- `getPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The system-settings permission (see requestPermissionsAsync).
- `getSystemBrightnessAsync(): Promise<number>` — The system brightness: off Android the screen's, as Expo (getBrightnessAsync); on Android the system setting.
- `getSystemBrightnessModeAsync(): Promise<BrightnessMode>` — The system brightness mode: off Android BrightnessMode.UNKNOWN, as in Expo; on Android the system setting's (AUTOMATIC or MANUAL).
- `isAvailableAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether the brightness can be changed: the shell with the plugin.
- `isUsingSystemBrightnessAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Android: whether the app window follows the system brightness (it has no level of its own). Off Android false, as in Expo.
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `type PermissionHookOptions<Options> = Options & object` — Options for a permission hook (createPermissionHook).
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `requestPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — Ask for the system-settings permission: on Android the system screen for WRITE_SETTINGS; granted elsewhere in the shell, undetermined on the web.
- `restoreSystemBrightnessAsync(): Promise<void>` — Android: let the app window follow the system brightness again. Off Android it does nothing, as in Expo.
- `setBrightnessAsync(brightnessValue: number): Promise<void>` — Set the brightness while the app runs.
- `setSystemBrightnessAsync(brightnessValue: number): Promise<void>` — Set the system brightness: off Android the screen's, as Expo (setBrightnessAsync); on Android the system setting (switching its mode to manual first, as Expo), which needs WRITE_SETTINGS (requestPermissionsAsync).
- `setSystemBrightnessModeAsync(brightnessMode: BrightnessMode): Promise<void>` — Set the system brightness mode: off Android, or for UNKNOWN, it does nothing, as in Expo; on Android it writes the system setting, which needs WRITE_SETTINGS (requestPermissionsAsync).
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `usePermissions: (options?: PermissionHookOptions<object>) => tuple` — Hook form of the permission: [response, request, get].

### `denext/expo/calendar`

- `interface AddEventWithFormOptions` — The event ExpoCalendar.addEventWithForm pre-fills.
- `interface Alarm` — An alarm. Only relativeOffset (minutes from the start) reaches the plugin.
- `interface AlarmLocation` — Where an alarm triggers.
- `enum AlarmMethod` — How an alarm alerts (Android).
- `interface Attendee` — An event attendee.
- `enum AttendeeRole` — An attendee's role.
- `enum AttendeeStatus` — An attendee's response.
- `enum AttendeeType` — An attendee's kind.
- `enum Availability` — An event's free/busy state.
- `interface Calendar` — A calendar (or an iOS reminders list).
- `enum CalendarAccessLevel` — The current user's access to a calendar (Android).
- `type CalendarDialogOpenParamsNext = CalendarDialogParamsNext & OpenEventPresentationOptions` — CalendarDialogParamsNext with the viewer's options.
- `interface CalendarDialogParams` — Which event a dialog shows.
- `type CalendarDialogParamsNext = Omit<CalendarDialogParams, id> & PresentationOptions` — Which occurrence the object API's dialogs show, and how.
- `enum CalendarDialogResultActions` — How a calendar dialog ended.
- `enum CalendarType` — A calendar's kind (iOS).
- `createAttendeeAsync(eventId: string, details?: Partial<Attendee>): Promise<string>` — Add an attendee to an event (Android).
- `createCalendar(details?: Partial<Calendar>): Promise<ExpoCalendar>` — Create a calendar (see createCalendarAsync).
- `createCalendarAsync(details?: Partial<Calendar>): Promise<string>` — Create a calendar, or (iOS, entityType: "reminder") a reminders list. On Android the plugin needs source.name (the account) and ownerAccount.
- `createEventAsync(calendarId: string, eventData?: Omit<Partial<Event>, id | organizer>): Promise<string>` — Create an event. Attendees and absolute or location alarms are not passed on; timeZone is set through DenextCalendar (ignored without it).
- `createEventInCalendarAsync(eventData?: Omit<Partial<Event>, id>, _presentationOptions?: PresentationOptions): Promise<DialogEventResult>` — Open the system's new-event editor, pre-filled. On iOS the result says whether it was saved (with the new id) or canceled; Android does not report it (done, id: null).
- `createReminderAsync(calendarId: string | null, reminder?: Reminder): Promise<string>` — Create a reminder.
- `enum DayOfTheWeek` — A weekday, as Expo numbers it (Sunday is 1).
- `interface DaysOfTheWeek` — A weekday of a recurrence.
- `deleteAttendeeAsync(id: string): Promise<void>` — Remove an attendee (Android).
- `deleteCalendarAsync(id: string): Promise<void>` — Delete a calendar (or reminders list) and everything in it.
- `deleteEventAsync(id: string, recurringEventOptions?: RecurringEventOptions): Promise<void>` — Delete an event, one occurrence (instanceStartDate) or this and the following ones (futureEvents).
- `deleteReminderAsync(id: string): Promise<void>` — Delete a reminder.
- `interface DialogEventResult` — How an event dialog ended, and the event's id.
- `editEventInCalendarAsync(params: CalendarDialogParams, presentationOptions?: PresentationOptions): Promise<DialogEventResult>` — Open the system's event editor on an event (one occurrence, with instanceStartDate, through DenextCalendar). Android does not report the outcome (done).
- `enum EntityTypes` — What a calendar holds.
- `interface Event` — An event.
- `enum EventAccessLevel` — An event's visibility (Android).
- `enum EventStatus` — An event's status.
- `class ExpoCalendar` — A calendar, with methods (the new API).
- `class ExpoCalendarAttendee` — An event's attendee, with methods (the new API; the methods are Android only).
- `class ExpoCalendarEvent` — An event, with methods (the new API).
- `class ExpoCalendarReminder` — A reminder, with methods (the new API, iOS).
- `enum Frequency` — How often a recurrence repeats.
- `getAttendeesForEventAsync(id: string, recurringEventOptions?: RecurringEventOptions): Promise<Attendee[]>` — An event's attendees (of one occurrence, with instanceStartDate).
- `getCalendarPermissions(writeOnly?: boolean): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The calendar permission, without prompting (the new API).
- `getCalendarPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The calendar permission, without prompting (legacy).
- `getCalendars(entityType?: EntityTypes): Promise<ExpoCalendar[]>` — The calendars, as objects (see getCalendarsAsync).
- `getCalendarsAsync(entityType?: string): Promise<Calendar[]>` — The calendars. On iOS, entityType picks event calendars or reminders lists (both when omitted; reminders lists only when reminders access allows reading them). Android ignores it, as Expo does.
- `getDefaultCalendarAsync(): Promise<Calendar>` — The default calendar for new events (isPrimary: true).
- `getEventAsync(id: string, recurringEventOptions?: RecurringEventOptions): Promise<Event>` — One event: by id (through DenextCalendar), or its occurrence starting at recurringEventOptions.instanceStartDate (the startDate a listing returned).
- `getEventsAsync(calendarIds: string[], startDate: Date | string, endDate: Date | string): Promise<Event[]>` — The events (occurrences) overlapping [startDate, endDate] in the given calendars (all calendars when the list is empty).
- `getReminderAsync(id: string): Promise<Reminder>` — One reminder.
- `getRemindersAsync(calendarIds: parenthesized[], status: ReminderStatus | null, startDate?: Date | string | null, endDate?: Date | string | null): Promise<Reminder[]>` — The reminders in the given lists (all lists when empty), by status; a date range filters on the due date (on the completion date for completed).
- `getRemindersPermissions(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The reminders permission (iOS), without prompting.
- `getRemindersPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The reminders permission (legacy).
- `getSourceAsync(id: string): Promise<Source>` — One calendar account.
- `getSourcesAsync(): Promise<Source[]>` — The calendar accounts.
- `isAvailableAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether the calendar API works here: the shell with the plugin installed.
- `listEvents(calendars: parenthesized[], startDate: Date, endDate: Date): Promise<ExpoCalendarEvent[]>` — The events overlapping [startDate, endDate] in the given calendars, as objects.
- `type ModifiableAttendeeProperties = Pick<Attendee, name | email | role | status | type>` — What ExpoCalendarAttendee.update changes.
- `type ModifiableCalendarProperties = Pick<Calendar, color | title>` — What ExpoCalendar.update changes.
- `type ModifiableEventProperties = Pick<Event, title | location | timeZone | url | notes | alarms | recurrenceRule | availability | startDate | endDate | allDay>` — What ExpoCalendarEvent.update changes.
- `type ModifiableReminderProperties = Pick<Reminder, title | location | timeZone | url | notes | alarms | recurrenceRule | startDate | dueDate | completed | completionDate>` — What ExpoCalendarReminder.update changes.
- `enum MonthOfTheYear` — A month (January is 1).
- `interface OpenEventDialogResult` — How an "open event" dialog ended.
- `openEventInCalendar(id: string): void` — Open an event in the Android calendar app (Expo's deprecated Android-only call; it returns before the app opens).
- `openEventInCalendarAsync(params: CalendarDialogParams, presentationOptions?: OpenEventPresentationOptions): Promise<OpenEventDialogResult>` — Show an event (or, with instanceStartDate, one occurrence) in the system's event viewer: EKEventViewController on iOS, which reports done, responded, deleted or canceled; the calendar app on Android, which reports nothing (done).
- `interface OpenEventPresentationOptions` — How to present an existing event.
- `interface Organizer` — An event's organizer.
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `type PermissionHookOptions<Options> = Options & object` — Options for a permission hook (createPermissionHook).
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `interface PresentationOptions` — How to present a dialog (Android).
- `presentPicker(): Promise<ExpoCalendar | null>` — The system calendar chooser (one calendar). Needs calendar access first.
- `interface RecurrenceRule` — How an event or reminder repeats.
- `interface RecurringEventOptions` — Which occurrence(s) of a recurring event a call means.
- `interface Reminder` — A reminder (iOS).
- `enum ReminderStatus` — A reminder's completion state.
- `requestCalendarPermissions(writeOnly?: boolean): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — Ask for calendar access (the new API).
- `requestCalendarPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — Ask for full calendar access (legacy).
- `requestPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — Ask for full calendar access (legacy, deprecated in Expo).
- `requestRemindersPermissions(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — Ask for reminders access (iOS).
- `requestRemindersPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — Ask for reminders access (legacy).
- `interface Source` — A calendar account.
- `enum SourceType` — A calendar source's kind (iOS).
- `updateAttendeeAsync(id: string, details?: Partial<Attendee>): Promise<string>` — Change an attendee (Android).
- `updateCalendarAsync(id: string, details?: Partial<Calendar>): Promise<string>` — Change a calendar's (or reminders list's) title and colour; other fields are ignored.
- `updateEventAsync(id: string, details?: Omit<Partial<Event>, id>, recurringEventOptions?: RecurringEventOptions): Promise<string>` — Change an event, or with instanceStartDate one occurrence of it (with futureEvents, it and the following ones). An occurrence and a time zone are changed through DenextCalendar; on Android the changed occurrence becomes an exception event, whose id is returned, and with futureEvents the series is split there (it ends before the occurrence, and a new event with the changes carries the rest: its id is returned, as EventKit's new identifier is on iOS).
- `updateReminderAsync(id: string, details?: Reminder): Promise<string>` — Change a reminder.
- `useCalendarPermissions: (options?: PermissionHookOptions<object>) => tuple` — Hook form of the calendar permission: [response, request, get].
- `useRemindersPermissions(options?: PermissionHookOptions<object>): tuple` — Hook form of the reminders permission (iOS): [response, request, get].

- `createCalendarAsync(details?: Partial<Calendar>): Promise<string>` — Create a calendar, or (iOS, entityType: "reminder") a reminders list. On Android the plugin needs source.name (the account) and ownerAccount.

On iOS the result says whether it was saved (with the new id) or canceled; Android does not report it (done, id: null).

- `getEventAsync(id: string, recurringEventOptions?: RecurringEventOptions): Promise<Event>` — One event: by id (through DenextCalendar), or its occurrence starting at recurringEventOptions.instanceStartDate (the startDate a listing returned).
- `getEventsAsync(calendarIds: string[], startDate: Date | string, endDate: Date | string): Promise<Event[]>` — The events (occurrences) overlapping [startDate, endDate] in the given calendars (all calendars when the list is empty).
- `getReminderAsync(id: string): Promise<Reminder>` — One reminder.
- `getRemindersAsync(calendarIds: parenthesized[], status: ReminderStatus | null, startDate?: Date | string | null, endDate?: Date | string | null): Promise<Reminder[]>` — The reminders in the given lists (all lists when empty), by status; a date range filters on the due date (on the completion date for completed).
- `getRemindersPermissionsAsync(): Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The reminders permission (legacy).
- `getSourceAsync(id: string): Promise<Source>` — One calendar account.
- `getSourcesAsync(): Promise<Source[]>` — The calendar accounts.
- `isAvailableAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether the calendar API works here: the shell with the plugin installed.
- `enum MonthOfTheYear` — A month (January is 1).
- `interface OpenEventDialogResult` — How an "open event" dialog ended.
- `openEventInCalendar(id: string): void` — Open an event in the Android calendar app (Expo's deprecated Android-only call; it returns before the app opens).

### `denext/expo/camera`

- `interface BarcodeBounds` — Where a code was found (not reported by denext's scanner: zeros).
- `interface BarcodePoint` — A point in view coordinates.
- `interface BarcodeScanningResult` — A scanned code.
- `interface BarcodeSettings` — The kinds a scan looks for.
- `type BarcodeType = aztec | ean13 | ean8 | qr | pdf417 | upc_e | datamatrix | code39 | code93 | itf14 | codabar | code128 | upc_a` — A barcode kind, by Expo's name.
- `Camera: object` — The permission calls and scanFromURLAsync, as Expo's Camera object groups them (expo-camera exports the permission calls only here). Camera: granted when the native scanner plugin is installed (it asks when it opens), else the browser's camera permission (a request is a getUserMedia call, stopped at once). Microphone: the browser's.
- `interface CameraCapturedPicture` — A picture takePictureAsync took.
- `type CameraMode = picture | video` — What the camera is for.
- `class CameraNativeModule` — The type of expo-camera's native module (what requireNativeModule("ExpoCamera") returns). There is no native module on the web: constructing this stand-in throws. Use Camera, CameraView and the permission hooks instead.
- `interface CameraPictureOptions` — Options for takePictureAsync.
- `interface CameraRecordingOptions` — Options for recordAsync.
- `type CameraType = front | back` — Which camera.
- `CameraView(props: CameraViewProps): VNode` — The camera view. With onBarcodeScanned it opens denext's scanner on mount and reports the first code (with a button to scan again after a cancel). Otherwise it shows a live getUserMedia preview (facing, mode, mute, active, zoom, the torch), and its ref takes pictures and records video (see CameraViewHandle).
- `interface CameraViewHandle` — The ref handle of a CameraView (what Expo's class instance offers).
- `interface CameraViewProps` — CameraView props.
- `type DocumentScanningOptions = object` — Options for CameraView.scanDocumentAsync.
- `type DocumentScanningResult = object` — What CameraView.scanDocumentAsync returns.
- `type FlashMode = off | on | auto | screen` — How the camera flashes (applied to the torch where the track supports it).
- `type ImageType = png | jpg` — The image format of a picture.
- `type LensInfo = object` — A camera (lens) the device has, as getAvailableLensesAsync lists it.
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `type PermissionHookOptions<Options> = Options & object` — Options for a permission hook (createPermissionHook).
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `interface PhotoResult` — What PictureRef.savePictureAsync resolves with.
- `class PictureRef` — A picture held in memory until saved: what takePictureAsync({ pictureRef: true }) resolves with.
- `type RecordingProgress = object` — A recording's progress, for onRecordingProgress.
- `interface SavePictureOptions` — Options for PictureRef.savePictureAsync.
- `scanFromURLAsync(url: string, barcodeTypes?: BarcodeType[]): Promise<BarcodeScanningResult[]>` — Decode the barcodes in the image at url with the browser's BarcodeDetector.
- `interface ScanningOptions` — Options for CameraView.launchScanner.
- `type ScanningResult = Omit<BarcodeScanningResult, bounds | cornerPoints>` — What CameraView.onModernBarcodeScanned listeners get.
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `useCameraPermissions: (options?: PermissionHookOptions<object>) => tuple` — Hook form of the camera permission: [response, request, get].
- `useMicrophonePermissions: (options?: PermissionHookOptions<object>) => tuple` — Hook form of the microphone permission: [response, request, get].
- `type VideoCodec = avc1 | hvc1 | jpeg | apcn | ap4h` — A video codec, by Expo's name.

### `denext/expo/cellular`

- `enum CellularGeneration` — The cellular generation.
- `getCarrierNameAsync(): Promise<string | null>` — The carrier's name: not readable here.
- `getCellularGenerationAsync(): Promise<CellularGeneration>` — The connection's generation, from the Network Information API (its effectiveType is the connection's measured speed class, which is what Expo's web build reports too). Only a cellular connection has one: a connection whose type says otherwise is UNKNOWN, and so is one without a type (a desktop browser or Deno Desktop, where a fast wired or Wi-Fi link reads "4g"), except in the Android shell, where the connection is the phone's.
- `getIsoCountryCodeAsync(): Promise<string | null>` — The carrier's ISO country code: not readable here.
- `getMobileCountryCodeAsync(): Promise<string | null>` — The carrier's mobile country code: not readable here.
- `getMobileNetworkCodeAsync(): Promise<string | null>` — The carrier's mobile network code: not readable here.
- `getPermissionsAsync: () => Promise<PermissionResponse>` — The phone-state permission: none is needed here, so granted.
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `type PermissionHookOptions<Options> = Options & object` — Options for a permission hook (createPermissionHook).
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `requestPermissionsAsync: () => Promise<PermissionResponse>` — Ask for the phone-state permission: none is needed here, so granted.
- `usePermissions: (options?: PermissionHookOptions<object>) => tuple` — Hook form of the permission: [response, request, get].

- `hasStringAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether the clipboard holds text.
- `hasUrlAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether the clipboard's text is a URL.
- `isPasteButtonAvailable: false` — Whether ClipboardPasteButton is available: never, here.
- `removeClipboardListener(sub: Subscription): void` — Remove a clipboard listener.
- `setStringAsync(text: string, _options?: SetStringOptions): Promise<boolean>` — Put text on the clipboard.

### `denext/expo/contacts`

- `addContactAsync(contact: LegacyContact, _containerId?: string): Promise<string>` — Add a contact to the default container.
- `addContactsChangeListener(listener: () => void): EventSubscription` — Call listener when the address book changes (a contact added, changed or removed, by this app or another): CNContactStoreDidChange on iOS, a ContentObserver on Android (which may batch changes by a few seconds, and report one change twice). Needs DenextContacts; on the web, or without it, the listener never fires (as in Expo's web build).
- `type Address = object` — A legacy postal address.
- `enum CalendarFormats` — Calendar formats of a legacy Date.
- `type CalendarFormatType = CalendarFormats | ${[0m[38;5;12mCalendarFormats[0m}` — A CalendarFormats member or its string.
- `class Contact` — A contact of the address book, by id. Reads go through the plugin on each call; writes read the stored record, change it and write it back.
- `ContactAccessButton: ContactAccessButtonComponent` — iOS 18's ContactAccessButton. The plugin does not provide it, so it renders nothing and isAvailable() is false, as on Android and the web in Expo.
- `interface ContactAccessButtonComponent` — The ContactAccessButton component with its static check.
- `type ContactAccessButtonProps = object` — Props of ContactAccessButton (iOS 18's limited-access button).
- `type ContactDate = object` — A class-API date: month is 1–12.
- `type ContactDetails = object` — Every detail of a contact, as the class API reads it.
- `enum ContactField` — The class API's contact fields (contact.getDetails(fields)).
- `type ContactFieldKey = mapped` — A ContactField's key in ContactDetails.
- `type ContactPatch = object` — A partial change to a contact (contact.patch); null clears a text field.
- `type ContactQuery = object` — A legacy contact query.
- `type ContactQueryOptions = object` — Options of Contact.getAll.
- `type ContactResponse = object` — A page of legacy contacts.
- `type ContactSort = ${[0m[38;5;12mSortTypes[0m}` — A legacy sort order.
- `type ContactsPermissionResponse = PermissionResponse & object` — A contacts permission answer, with how much of the address book is shared.
- `enum ContactsSortOrder` — The class API's sort orders (ContactQueryOptions.sortOrder).
- `type ContactType = ContactTypes | ${[0m[38;5;12mContactTypes[0m}` — A ContactTypes member or its string.
- `enum ContactTypes` — Person or company.
- `class Container` — A container of contacts (an account: on the device, iCloud, Exchange, …), by id. iOS only, as in Expo, through DenextContacts; elsewhere every call rejects with ERR_UNAVAILABLE.
- `type ContainerClassType = local | exchange | cardDAV | unassigned | unknown` — A container's kind as the class API reports it.
- `type ContainerQuery = object` — A legacy container query.
- `type ContainerType = ContainerTypes | ${[0m[38;5;12mContainerTypes[0m}` — A ContainerTypes member or its string.
- `enum ContainerTypes` — Kinds of contact container.
- `type CreateContactRecord = object` — A new contact (Contact.create).
- `type CreateFormOptions = object` — Options of Contact.presentCreateForm (ignored here).
- `createGroupAsync(name?: string, _containerId?: string): Promise<string>` — Create a contact group.
- `type Date = object` — A legacy date: month is 0-based, as JavaScript's Date.
- `type Email = object` — A legacy email address.
- `type EventSubscription = Subscription` — Expo's name for a listener subscription.
- `type ExistingAddress = NewAddress & object` — A postal address of a contact.
- `type ExistingContact = LegacyContact & object` — A legacy contact with its id.
- `type ExistingDate = NewDate & object` — A date of a contact.
- `type ExistingEmail = NewEmail & object` — An email address of a contact.
- `type ExistingExtraName = NewExtraName & object` — An extra name of a contact.
- `type ExistingImAddress = NewImAddress & object` — An IM address of a contact.
- `type ExistingPhone = NewPhone & object` — A phone number of a contact.
- `type ExistingRelation = NewRelation & object` — A relation of a contact.
- `type ExistingSocialProfile = NewSocialProfile & object` — A social profile of a contact.
- `type ExistingUrlAddress = NewUrlAddress & object` — A URL of a contact.
- `enum Fields` — The legacy API's contact fields (ContactQuery.fields).
- `type FieldType = Fields | ${[0m[38;5;12mFields[0m}` — A Fields member or its string.
- `type FormOptions = object` — Options of a contact form. Only allowsEditing is honoured here.
- `getContactByIdAsync(id: string, fields?: FieldType[]): Promise<ExistingContact | undefined>` — One contact.
- `getContactsAsync(contactQuery?: ContactQuery): Promise<ContactResponse>` — A page of contacts. pageSize / pageOffset page it, name keeps names containing the text, id keeps those ids, groupId keeps the group's members, sort orders by given or family name, and fields limits what is read.
- `getContainersAsync(containerQuery: ContainerQuery): Promise<LegacyContainer[]>` — The containers (iOS): the one holding a contact (contactId) or a group (groupId), the ones with the given ids (containerId), or every one.
- `getDefaultContainerIdAsync(): Promise<string>` — The default container's id: where new contacts go (iOS).
- `getGroupsAsync(groupQuery: GroupQuery): Promise<LegacyGroup[]>` — The contact groups, optionally only the one with groupId or the ones named groupName.
- `getPagedContactsAsync(contactQuery?: ContactQuery): Promise<ContactResponse>` — getContactsAsync, by its paging name.
- `getPermissionsAsync(): Promise<ContactsPermissionResponse>` — The contacts permission, without prompting. Read and write are asked together; granted means both (iOS 18 limited access reads as granted with accessPrivileges: "limited").
- `class Group` — A contact group, by id.
- `type GroupQuery = object` — A legacy group query.
- `hasContactsAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether the address book has any contact.
- `type Image = object` — A legacy contact photo.
- `type InstantMessageAddress = object` — A legacy instant-message address (not read here).
- `isAvailableAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether the address book can be used: the plugin's answer in the shell.
- `type LegacyContact = object` — A legacy contact (Expo's Contact type of the legacy API).
- `type LegacyContainer = object` — A legacy container.
- `type LegacyGroup = object` — A legacy group.
- `type NewAddress = object` — A new postal address.
- `type NewDate = object` — A new date.
- `type NewEmail = object` — A new email address.
- `type NewExtraName = object` — A new extra name.
- `type NewImAddress = object` — A new IM address.
- `type NewPhone = object` — A new phone number.
- `type NewRelation = object` — A new relation.
- `type NewSocialProfile = object` — A new social profile.
- `type NewUrlAddress = object` — A new URL.
- `type NonGregorianBirthday = object` — A non-Gregorian birthday.
- `enum NonGregorianCalendar` — Calendars of a NonGregorianBirthday.
- `type PartialContactDetails<T> = object & mapped` — The details getDetails(fields) returns: the id and the asked-for fields.
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `type PhoneNumber = object` — A legacy phone number.
- `presentContactPickerAsync(): Promise<ExistingContact | null>` — Let the user pick a contact with the system picker. Off the shell, where the browser has the Contact Picker API (Chrome on Android), its picker (pickContact from denext/mobile): the contact then has no id (""), and only its name, emails and phone numbers. Expo's web build has no picker; elsewhere it rejects with ERR_UNAVAILABLE, as Expo's does.
- `presentFormAsync(contactId?: string | null, contact?: LegacyContact | null, formOptions?: FormOptions): Promise<void>` — Show the system contact form: an existing contact (editable unless allowsEditing is false), or a new one prefilled from contact.
- `type Relationship = object` — A legacy relationship (not read here).
- `removeAllContactsChangeListeners(): void` — Remove every listener addContactsChangeListener added.
- `removeContactAsync(contactId: string): Promise<void>` — Delete a contact.
- `removeGroupAsync(groupId: string): Promise<void>` — Delete a contact group.
- `requestPermissionsAsync(): Promise<ContactsPermissionResponse>` — Ask for the contacts permission (read and write).
- `type SocialProfile = object` — A legacy social profile (not read here).
- `enum SortTypes` — Legacy sort orders (ContactQuery.sort).
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `updateContactAsync(contact: object & Partial<ExistingContact>): Promise<string>` — Change a contact: the given fields replace the stored ones, the rest are kept.
- `type UrlAddress = object` — A legacy URL.

### `denext/expo/contacts/legacy`

- `ContactAccessButton: ContactAccessButtonComponent` — iOS 18's ContactAccessButton. The plugin does not provide it, so it renders nothing and isAvailable() is false, as on Android and the web in Expo.
- `type ContactAccessButtonProps = object` — Props of ContactAccessButton (iOS 18's limited-access button).
- `type ContactQuery = object` — A legacy contact query.
- `type ContactResponse = object` — A page of legacy contacts.
- `type ContactSort = ${[0m[38;5;12mSortTypes[0m}` — A legacy sort order.
- `type ContactsPermissionResponse = PermissionResponse & object` — A contacts permission answer, with how much of the address book is shared.
- `type ContactType = ContactTypes | ${[0m[38;5;12mContactTypes[0m}` — A ContactTypes member or its string.
- `enum ContactTypes` — Person or company.
- `type Container = object` — A legacy container.
- `type ContainerQuery = object` — A legacy container query.
- `type ContainerType = ContainerTypes | ${[0m[38;5;12mContainerTypes[0m}` — A ContainerTypes member or its string.
- `enum ContainerTypes` — Kinds of contact container.
- `createGroupAsync(name?: string, _containerId?: string): Promise<string>` — Create a contact group.
- `type Date = object` — A legacy date: month is 0-based, as JavaScript's Date.
- `type Email = object` — A legacy email address.
- `type ExistingContact = LegacyContact & object` — A legacy contact with its id.
- `enum Fields` — The legacy API's contact fields (ContactQuery.fields).
- `type FieldType = Fields | ${[0m[38;5;12mFields[0m}` — A Fields member or its string.
- `type FormOptions = object` — Options of a contact form. Only allowsEditing is honoured here.
- `getContactByIdAsync(id: string, fields?: FieldType[]): Promise<ExistingContact | undefined>` — One contact.
- `getContactsAsync(contactQuery?: ContactQuery): Promise<ContactResponse>` — A page of contacts. pageSize / pageOffset page it, name keeps names containing the text, id keeps those ids, groupId keeps the group's members, sort orders by given or family name, and fields limits what is read.
- `getContainersAsync(containerQuery: ContainerQuery): Promise<LegacyContainer[]>` — The containers (iOS): the one holding a contact (contactId) or a group (groupId), the ones with the given ids (containerId), or every one.
- `getDefaultContainerIdAsync(): Promise<string>` — The default container's id: where new contacts go (iOS).
- `getGroupsAsync(groupQuery: GroupQuery): Promise<LegacyGroup[]>` — The contact groups, optionally only the one with groupId or the ones named groupName.
- `getPagedContactsAsync(contactQuery?: ContactQuery): Promise<ContactResponse>` — getContactsAsync, by its paging name.
- `getPermissionsAsync(): Promise<ContactsPermissionResponse>` — The contacts permission, without prompting. Read and write are asked together; granted means both (iOS 18 limited access reads as granted with accessPrivileges: "limited").
- `type Group = object` — A legacy group.
- `type GroupQuery = object` — A legacy group query.
- `hasContactsAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether the address book has any contact.
- `type Image = object` — A legacy contact photo.
- `type InstantMessageAddress = object` — A legacy instant-message address (not read here).
- `isAvailableAsync(): Promise<boolean>` — Whether the address book can be used: the plugin's answer in the shell.
- `onContactsChangeEventName: onContactsChange` — The native event name the address-book change listener subscribes to.
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `type PhoneNumber = object` — A legacy phone number.
- `presentContactPickerAsync(): Promise<ExistingContact | null>` — Let the user pick a contact with the system picker. Off the shell, where the browser has the Contact Picker API (Chrome on Android), its picker (pickContact from denext/mobile): the contact then has no id (""), and only its name, emails and phone numbers. Expo's web build has no picker; elsewhere it rejects with ERR_UNAVAILABLE, as Expo's does.
- `presentFormAsync(contactId?: string | null, contact?: LegacyContact | null, formOptions?: FormOptions): Promise<void>` — Show the system contact form: an existing contact (editable unless allowsEditing is false), or a new one prefilled from contact.
- `type Relationship = object` — A legacy relationship (not read here).
- `removeContactAsync(contactId: string): Promise<void>` — Delete a contact.
- `removeGroupAsync(groupId: string): Promise<void>` — Delete a contact group.
- `requestPermissionsAsync(): Promise<ContactsPermissionResponse>` — Ask for the contacts permission (read and write).
- `type SocialProfile = object` — A legacy social profile (not read here).
- `enum SortTypes` — Legacy sort orders (ContactQuery.sort).
- `updateContactAsync(contact: object & Partial<ExistingContact>): Promise<string>` — Change a contact: the given fields replace the stored ones, the rest are kept.
- `type UrlAddress = object` — A legacy URL.

### `denext/expo/expo`

- `class CodedError` — Expo's CodedError (expo-modules-core, re-exported by expo): an Error with a code that tells errors apart without subclassing.
- `createPermissionHook<P, Options>(methods: object): (options?: PermissionHookOptions<Options>) => tuple` — Expo's createPermissionHook: a hook returning [response, request, get] that reads (or, with request: true, requests) the permission on mount.
- `createSnapshotFriendlyRef<T>(): object` — A ref object ({ current: null }), as Expo's snapshot-friendly ref is.
- `disableErrorHandling(): void` — Turn off Expo's global error handler (there is none here): does nothing.
- `class EventEmitter<Events>` — A typed event emitter, as Expo modules use.
- `type EventSubscription = Subscription` — Expo's name for a listener subscription (EventSubscription in expo-modules-core).
- `interface ExpoPlatform` — Expo's Platform (expo-modules-core): the web build's, which is what runs here.
- `fetch(input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response>` — expo/fetch: the platform's WinterCG fetch (streaming bodies included).
- `getExpoGoProjectConfig(): null` — The Expo Go project config: none.
- `installOnUIRuntime(_uiRuntimeHolder?: object): void` — Install Expo Modules on the worklets UI runtime (there is no UI runtime here): does nothing.
- `isRunningInExpoGo(): boolean` — Whether the app runs in Expo Go: never.
- `interface Listenable` — The slice of an emitter useEvent and useEventListener use.
- `class NativeModule<Events>` — A module implemented in JS (see registerWebModule).
- `type PermissionExpiration = never | number` — When a permission expires: "never", or a timestamp.
- `type PermissionHookOptions<Options> = Options & object` — Options for a permission hook (createPermissionHook).
- `interface PermissionResponse` — A permission answer, as every Expo permission API returns it.
- `enum PermissionStatus` — A permission's state, as expo-modules-core reports it.
- `Platform: ExpoPlatform` — Expo's Platform: OS is "web" and select picks web, then default (as Expo's web build; React Native's own Platform from react-native is the one that reports the Capacitor shell). The DOM facts are read when asked, so importing it is safe anywhere.
- `type PlatformSelectOSType = ios | android | macos | windows | web | native | electron | default` — A platform key Platform.select matches (native never matches here).
- `registerRootComponent<P>(component: Component<P>): void` — Mount component as the app: react-native-web's AppRegistry in React Native mode (the app key main, as Expo registers it), else denext's createRoot.
- `registerWebModule<T>(moduleImplementation: T | parenthesized, _moduleName?: string): T` — Register a module implemented in JS: a class is instantiated, an object returned as is.
- `type ReleasingSharedObjectLifecycle<TSharedObject> = object` — How useReleasingSharedObjectWithLifecycle creates, updates and releases.
- `type ReleasingSharedObjectLifecycleContext = object` — What ReleasingSharedObjectLifecycle's callbacks receive.
- `reloadAppAsync(_reason?: string): Promise<void>` — Reload the app (the page).
- `requireNativeModule<T>(moduleName: string): T` — The native module moduleName: the Capacitor plugin of that name inside the iOS/Android shell, or the desktop extension of that name on Deno Desktop. Its functions take Expo's positional arguments and return Promises. Where neither exists (a browser, a test) it returns a stand-in whose functions throw when called, so a module that asks for it at import time still loads (Expo's web build throws at the requireNativeModule call itself).
- `requireNativeView<P>(moduleName: string, viewName?: string): Component<P>` — A native view as a component: denext/mobile's native view slot for the type nativeViewType names (the DenextNativeViews plugin, denext mobile add native-views). Its JSON props go to the native factory, a native event name calls the on<Name> prop with { nativeEvent }, style styles the slot and its children are drawn over the view. Where that view type is not registered natively (the web), the children render instead.
- `requireOptionalNativeModule<T>(moduleName: string): T | null` — The native module moduleName when this runtime has it (see requireNativeModule), else null.
- `class SharedObject<Events>` — An object shared with native code: a JS object here, released explicitly.
- `class SharedRef<Type, Events>` — A reference to a native resource (an image, a file): a JS object here.
- `interface Subscription` — What Expo's add…Listener functions return.
- `class UnavailabilityError` — Expo's UnavailabilityError: a CodedError (ERR_UNAVAILABLE) for a method or property the running platform does not have. The platform is always web here (the Capacitor shell runs the web build).
- `useEvent<T>(emitter: Listenable, eventName: string, initialValue?: T | null): T | null` — The latest payload of eventName on emitter.
- `useEventListener(emitter: Listenable, eventName: string, listener: (...args: never[]) => void): void` — Call listener for each eventName on emitter while mounted.
- `useReleasingSharedObject<TSharedObject>(factory: () => TSharedObject, dependencies: DependencyList): TSharedObject` — A shared object for the component's lifetime: factory's result, released on unmount and replaced (the old one released) when dependencies change.
- `useReleasingSharedObjectWithLifecycle<TSharedObject>(lifecycle: ReleasingSharedObjectLifecycle<TSharedObject>, dependencies: DependencyList): TSharedObject` — A shared object for the component's lifetime, made by lifecycle.factory and released (by lifecycle.release, else its release()) on unmount or when the dependencies change. With shouldRecreate returning false, a dependency change calls update on the same object instead. Hiding the component in an <Activity> does not release it. Expo's own semantics.
- `uuid: UUID` — Expo's uuid: v4() over the platform's CSPRNG, v5(name, namespace) over SHA-1.
- `interface UUID` — The shape of Expo's uuid export.

### `denext/expo/file-system/legacy`

- `bundleDirectory: string | null` — The bundled assets: the page's own origin (read-only).
- `cacheDirectory: string | null` — The app's cache folder (file:///cache/); the OS may clear it.
- `copyAsync(options: RelocatingOptions): Promise<void>` — Copy a file or folder (or anything fetch can read, such as a picker's blob: URL), replacing what is at the destination.
- `createDownloadResumable(_uri: string, _fileUri: string, _options?: DownloadOptions, _callback?: FileSystemNetworkTaskProgressCallback<DownloadProgressData>, _resumeData?: string): DownloadResumable` — Not provided (native resumable downloads): throws an error naming denext. Use downloadAsync.
- `createUploadTask(_url: string, _fileUri: string, _options?: FileSystemUploadOptions, _callback?: FileSystemNetworkTaskProgressCallback<UploadProgressData>): UploadTask` — Not provided (native upload sessions): throws an error naming denext.
- `deleteAsync(fileUri: string, options?: DeletingOptions): Promise<void>` — Delete a file, or a folder and everything in it.
- `deleteLegacyDocumentDirectoryAndroid(): Promise<void>` — Android's legacy-folder cleanup: there is no such folder here, so it resolves.
- `type DeletingOptions = object` — Options for deleteAsync.
- `documentDirectory: string | null` — The app's documents folder (file:///documents/).
- `downloadAsync(uri: string, fileUri: string, options?: DownloadOptions): Promise<FileSystemDownloadResult>` — Download a URL to a file (replacing it). As in Expo, an HTTP error status still resolves, with that status.
- `type DownloadOptions = object` — Options for downloadAsync.
- `type DownloadPauseState = object` — A paused download's saved state.

- `type DownloadProgressData = object` — Download progress.

- `class DownloadResumable` — A native resumable download. Not provided: constructing it throws an error naming denext.
- `enum EncodingType` — How File.write and the readers carry text.
- `type FileInfo = object | object` — What getInfoAsync reports.
- `type FileSystemAcceptedUploadHttpMethod = POST | PUT | PATCH` — The HTTP methods an upload may use.
- `class FileSystemCancellableNetworkTask<T>` — A native network task. Not provided: constructing a subclass throws an error naming denext.
- `type FileSystemDownloadResult = FileSystemHttpResult & object` — What downloadAsync resolves with.
- `type FileSystemHttpResult = object` — The HTTP part of a download or upload result.
- `type FileSystemNetworkTaskProgressCallback<T> = (data: T) => void` — A network task's progress callback.
- `type FileSystemRequestDirectoryPermissionsResult = object | object` — What the Storage Access Framework's permission request resolves with.
- `enum FileSystemSessionType` — The session a native network task runs in (native tasks are not provided here).
- `type FileSystemUploadOptions = parenthesized & object` — Options for uploadAsync (uploads are not provided here).
- `type FileSystemUploadResult = FileSystemHttpResult & object` — What an upload resolves with.
- `enum FileSystemUploadType` — How uploadAsync sends the file.
- `getContentUriAsync(fileUri: string): Promise<string>` — Android content URIs do not exist here: rejects with an error naming denext.
- `getFreeDiskStorageAsync(): Promise<number>` — The storage still free to this app: the origin's quota minus its usage.
- `getInfoAsync(fileUri: string, _options?: InfoOptions): Promise<FileInfo>` — Facts about a file or folder.

- `type MakeDirectoryOptions = object` — Options for makeDirectoryAsync.

- `type ProgressEvent<T> = object` — A native progress event.
- `readAsStringAsync(fileUri: string, options?: ReadingOptions): Promise<string>` — Read a whole file as text, or as base64.
- `readDirectoryAsync(fileUri: string): Promise<string[]>` — The names of a folder's entries.
- `type ReadingOptions = object` — Options for readAsStringAsync.
- `type RelocatingOptions = object` — The source and destination of moveAsync and copyAsync.
- `StorageAccessFramework: StorageAccessFrameworkApi` — Android's Storage Access Framework. Its own calls throw or reject with an error naming denext; the aliases (readAsStringAsync, writeAsStringAsync, deleteAsync, moveAsync, copyAsync) are the functions above, for file:// URIs.
- `interface StorageAccessFrameworkApi` — The shape of StorageAccessFramework.
- `uploadAsync(url: string, fileUri: string, options?: FileSystemUploadOptions): Promise<FileSystemUploadResult>` — Upload a file with fetch: its bytes as the body (BINARY_CONTENT, the default) or as the fieldName part of a multipart form with parameters as extra fields (MULTIPART). Resolves with the response even on an HTTP error, as Expo does.
- `type UploadOptionsBinary = object` — A binary upload.
- `type UploadOptionsMultipart = object` — A multipart upload.
- `type UploadProgressData = object` — Upload progress.
- `class UploadTask` — A native upload task. Not provided: constructing it throws an error naming denext.

- `type WritingOptions = object` — Options for writeAsStringAsync.
